ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: High river flows produced seepage through vertical slots in the metal sheet piling at Catcliffe, led to water ponding on Orgreave Road and created a risk of the River Rother overtopping the defence wall; this made surface-water pumps ineffective at the site.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The Rother (as part of the Don and Rother WFD catchment) was part of the most severely affected catchment during the event; the Don and Rother catchment accounted for 514 internally flooded properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: High river levels drive flood risk locally; a proposed pumping station will over-pump surface water into the River Rother when gravity discharge is not possible, but the scheme will not reduce the River Rother flood risk itself.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: River levels rose to a pre-determined level causing the penstock to close; without the penstock river water could reverse into surface water pipes. Water from the river was observed seeping under metal capping near the top of the sheet-piled flood defence and ponding on Orgreave Road; peak flow remained at its highest level until 23:59 on 21 October 2023.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The River Rother overtopped the existing sheet-piled flood defence (metal capping) and caused floodwater to spread across Orgreave Road and into nearby communities, leading to widespread property flooding in the River Rother corridor.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Peak flows on the River Rother contributed to flooding risk during Storm Babet; alignment of River Rother peaks with the River Don could cause severe flooding in Rotherham centre and downstream into Doncaster. Post‑event modelling indicated that even with all regulators operating the River Rother still contributed to flooding impacting Catcliffe and Treeton.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Began seeping through flood defences and then overtopped, contributing to surface-water/river flooding that prompted warnings and multi-agency response and evacuations.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The River Rother is identified as the source of flood risk to downstream areas (Catcliffe and Treeton). Options to manage the hazard include upstream storage/NFM to reduce peak flows (anticipated to have minimal effect downstream), raising and extending defences along the river, and improving conveyance (including addressing restrictions at the Treeton Lane bridge).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The river's conveyance is constrained by the Treeton Lane bridge (studied for restriction of flow). The River Rother is also the receptor for surface water pumped from streets/properties when gravity drainage failed, contributing to local flood risk.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The River Rother overtopped during Storm Babet (Oct 2023), leading to internal flooding that affected properties in Catcliffe and Treeton Villages.

info.text: The River Rother overtopped/was the primary source of flooding in the Chesterfield South community; flooding from the Rother produced most of the flooded homes on the adjacent floodplain (most flooded homes were west of the river). ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Rother was the primary source of flooding: it overtopped flood defence structures at several locations causing inundation of low-lying areas. Overtopping occurred near Derby Road bridge and along the west bank defences, producing flow routes through gardens into streets and causing internal flooding of homes, businesses and an electricity substation.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Rother overtopped its banks (floodwater reached ~76.0 mAOD in topographic data), causing floodwater to flow over the bank by Derby Road bridge into properties along Riverview, through gardens on Bridge Street and into Hawthorne Street; it also inundated properties at St Giles Close and Healaugh Way and flooded a Yorkshire Water pumping station which failed.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Localised storms in October 2023 delivered significant flows and volumes into the River Rother, producing high river levels and elevated flood flows in the Rother catchment.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Experienced elevated/peak flows during Storm Babet (19–21 Oct 2023); flows were diverted via the Meadowgate regulator into wetlands to reduce peak flow in the Rother and to prevent peaks coinciding with the River Don.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: River Rother levels at Catcliffe rose such that the Environment Agency reached its Result Threshold in the early hours of 21 Oct 2023, triggering an automated Flood Warning. The EA maintained regulator levels overnight (20 Oct) but once levels rose again the warning was activated at 01:36am and sent to customers at 02:14am. Reports indicate the first properties were impacted by fluvial water at approximately 04:00 on 21 Oct 2023.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: River levels at Catcliffe were within 200 mm of overtopping defences; flows were regulated into flood storage areas by the Environment Agency and the Council pumped surface water for several days, avoiding widespread flooding though 2 houses were flooded by a localised surface water issue.

ref.title: Section 19 Report November 2019 Floods

info.text: The River Rother was identified as part of the area of intense rainfall and flood assessment (centred on Doncaster, Rotherham and Sheffield) for the 7–8 November 2019 event and contributed to river flooding in the Rotherham area.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: River levels were already elevated from the 25-26 October 2019 rainfall, particularly in the River Rother and lower River Don reaches, and the elevated Rother flows contributed to the combined peaks experienced on the River Don during the November 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: The hydrology report assessed flood flows on the River Rother during the 7–8 Nov 2019 event; these flows contributed to flooding in the catchment.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: Elevated river flows and river flooding associated with the South Yorkshire weather front (7–8 Nov 2019). The hydrology report included the Rother in its assessment of flood flows for the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: The Environment Agency interim hydrology report focussed on flood flows on the Don, Dearne and Rother associated with the persistent rainfall on 7–8 November 2019, indicating significant river flooding on the Rother catchment during this event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: Significant flood flows in the River Rother catchment associated with the 7–8 November 2019 weather front; included in the Environment Agency interim hydrology report assessing flood flows for the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: Generated Flood Warnings/Alerts that remained in place longer than others across Sheffield; associated flooding affected properties in Sheffield and prompted an EA review.

ref.title: Investigation Into the Flooding Event In Sheffield On 20th October 2023

info.text: High flows in the River Rother contribute to flood risk downstream at Catcliffe and Treeton; conveyance constraints (including at Treeton Lane bridge) are identified as influencing flood risk, and upstream peak-flow reductions from NFM are expected to be minimal.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Identified as the watercourse requiring raised and extended defences on both banks to increase the standard of protection for Catcliffe and Treeton; works would also require alterations to the bridge on Treeton Lane to improve conveyance.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The River Rother converges with The Moss near the recorded flood outline; this convergence is spatially associated with the flood recorded during Storm Babet and may have contributed to the local fluvial flooding affecting areas adjacent to The Moss and properties in Eckington (stated as a likely contributor).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Elevated river levels in the Rother catchments contributed to significant peak flows on the River Don as antecedent rainfall on 25–26 Oct 2019 left ground saturated prior to the November event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation

info.text: The River Erewash and its channel network are described as part of the sub-catchment hydrological response during Storm Babet (flowing south through multiple towns into Attenborough Nature Reserve).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Erewash catchment experienced higher concentrations of internally flooded properties during the Storm Babet event, driven by higher magnitude rainfall in the east of the county and local population density; watercourse overtopping and surface water were significant causes, with some sewer-related flooding where pumping stations were overwhelmed.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: High river levels caused overland flows into the surrounding area and prevented local gullies from discharging effectively, and therefore was a main contributing source of flooding to nearby streets.

ref.title: Section 19 Report –Stapleford – Storm Babet, October 2023

info.text: A Flood Alert was issued for the River Erewash (covering Derbyshire and Nottinghamshire) on 19 Oct 2023 at 01:13, and a Flood Warning was issued for the River Erewash at Langley Mill on 20 Oct 2023 at 06:44 during the storm period.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River flooding/adjacent river levels contributed to internal flooding of properties in Ilkeston; the community is on the river's floodplain and proximity to the river is linked to clusters of flooded homes.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Erewash flooding during Storm Babet/October 2023 caused inundation of adjacent residential properties in the Ilkeston floodplain, specifically properties on Digby Street, Station Street and Wentworth Street.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Fluvial flooding from the River Erewash (conveyed via the canal) caused flooding in the Ilkeston community; the river was the source of fluvial flood water that inundated properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Contributed to internal flooding of the Sandiacre community during Storm Babet; residential and some commercial properties between the River Erewash (east) and the Erewash Valley Canal (west) were flooded.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Erewash flooding affected the Sandiacre community (community on its floodplain); contributed to internal flooding of residential and commercial properties during the storm. Historic floods of similar extent are recorded for the river.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overtopping/inundation from the River Erewash caused internal flooding of residential properties and some commercial premises in the Sandiacre community. Properties that flooded during Storm Babet had previously flooded from the River Erewash; the community lies on the Erewash floodplain and many flooded properties are within Flood Zone 2.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding of the adjacent Sandiacre community; river flooding from the River Erewash caused the internal property flooding reported during the event. Historic similar flood extents recorded in 1947, 1957, 1960, 1977 and 1978.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Erewash overtopped its banks and flowed into the Erewash Canal north of Gas Street; this overtopping initiated the flow path that led to widespread property flooding in the community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The river overtopped its banks, flowed into the Erewash Canal north of Gas Street and caused overtopping of defence walls (west and east banks) opposite Megavaux. Overflowing led to flood water flowing westward and south across Station Road, flooding the industrial park, railyard and residential/business areas; the railway became a flow path and was closed.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Erewash overflowed, causing flooding to an industrial estate and a railyard south of Station Road; the Environment Agency issued a Flood Alert (19 Oct 2023) and a Flood Warning for the River Erewash at Sandiacre (21 Oct 2023).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Main river adjacent to the flooded Long Eaton community; flooding from the River Erewash inundated residential properties in Long Eaton during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River levels on the River Erewash prompted a Flood Alert (19 Oct 2023) and a Flood Warning (21 Oct 2023) and contributed to internal flooding in the Long Eaton community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Erewash overflowed and conveyed floodwater into the Long Eaton community, entering via Doncaster Road/Doncaster Grove and causing internal flooding to houses.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The community (Langley Mill) sits on the floodplain of the River Erewash and was flooded during the event, causing inundation of residential terraced homes and non-residential properties (restaurants, shops, depot yard, self-storage). Critical infrastructure lies adjacent (Midlands Railway Line, A608 Derby Road, A610) and a Severn Trent pumping station and Millhay Heanor STW lie approximately 400m and 900m downstream respectively of the flooded area.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Erewash is the main watercourse running through the mapped area and is implicated in river-flooding interactions with the urban area; culverted sections and tributaries run close to streets and buildings that experienced flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Erewash is identified as the primary watercourse along which the highest flood risk (Flood Zone 3) is concentrated. Properties in Langley Mill flooded internally during Storm Babet; many of those flooded properties fall within the river flood zones shown adjacent to the River Erewash and Erewash Canal, indicating river flooding from the River Erewash impacted the community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Primary source of flooding in the Langley Mill community. The river overtopped (first identified at a 90° bend south of the Crabapple Drive allotments) and drove floodwater into the Erewash Canal (which acted as a conduit) and, in some locations, interacted with flows from Nether Green Brook to cause internal flooding of properties on Cromford Road, Dean Street, Queen Street, Station Road, Derby Road, Boundary Lane and Enterprise Way.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Erewash overtopped its west embankment at a 90-degree bend south of the Crabapple Drive allotments. Overtopping and subsequent flow across industrial yards and the DandD Transport car park routed floodwater onto Cromford Road and caused internal flooding of properties on adjacent streets.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Experienced exceptionally high flows that overtopped banks and infrastructure, contributing to flooding across Langley Mill and adjacent roads. Wrack marks show peak water reached 59.9mAOD; the river produced record gauge levels at Shipley Gate, reflecting the primary source of the observed inundation.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: Across Staffordshire the existing public sewer and highway drainage networks (including combined, surface water and foul sewers) may be overwhelmed during large or prolonged storm events. Older sewers built to earlier, lower design standards can be unable to cope, leading to restricted flows or backing-up, surcharging to surface via manholes or drainage points, and surface water flooding affecting highways and properties.

ref.title: Section 19 – Investigation, Barton-Under-Needwood

info.text: Highway drainage (gullies, channels and underground sewers/culverts) can be overwhelmed during heavy or prolonged rainfall or when blocked. When the carriageway cannot contain flows water can pond on the highway, overtop kerbs and spill onto adjacent land, entering properties that are at or below road level. Historic variations in sewer design and capacity mean some parts of the drainage network surcharge or are unable to accept highway runoff, contributing to property and highway flooding.

ref.title: Investigation Report into November 2019 Derwent Floods in Derby City

info.text: High river flows in the River Derwent and its tributary (Folly Brook) overtopped banks. Fluvial water entered a low-gradient, poorly maintained ditch and then the highway drainage outfall (which lacked a non-return valve), allowing river water to backflow into gullies and emerge at the A61 Pektron Island roundabout causing highway flooding. Flood flows from the overtopping also followed Folly Brook onto Haslams Lane, then onto the Rugby Club grounds and Darley Fields. The Pektron Island area was submerged and the roundabout required temporary closure.

Five of the seven flooded homes are in Flood Zone 3 (river >1% AEP); two are in Flood Zone 1. All internally flooded homes have medium surface-water flood risk; some have high surface-water flood risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper overtopped banks at multiple locations through the village (including near Old Mill Pond), Old Mill Pond overtopped, and floodwater and runoff flowed through the village (notably along Loads Road) pooling at the Loads Road / New Road low spot. This led to internal flooding of residential properties on The Alders, New Road and Loads Road, internal flooding of one business, highway flooding and significant soil/silt deposits on Loads Road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Clean‑up of silt and blockages from an access chamber following the event; senior officers coordinated the clean‑up. Responsibility for ongoing maintenance was transferred to Severn Trent who will include the chamber in their maintenance programme.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: A small, culverted ordinary watercourse running parallel to Lilac Way had limited capacity and a small, poorly designed inlet that became restricted. During Storm Babet water bypassed the culvert, flowed through rear gardens of properties on the west side of Lilac Way and entered homes through doorways. Flood depths in doorways reached about 0.6 m. Siltation and debris in a downstream chamber impeded flow and was subsequently removed.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Culvert flow at Lilac Way was impeded by partial siltation and debris in an access chamber which exacerbated local flooding; residents attempted to remove debris during the event; Fire and Rescue pumped water and silt from the area; the chamber was later de-silted and cleared.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bar Brook exceeded its capacity and overflowed into the community; surface-water runoff from Cock Hill (A619), springs related to old mine workings and an erosion-related burst water main contributed to large volumes of surface water running downhill. These combined mechanisms flooded the Nether End car park, Baslow Village Hall and nearby residential properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flows in Bar Brook (a tributary of the River Derwent) overtopped or surged onto its floodplain during Storm Babet, causing internal flooding of residential properties on Cock Hill and Church Lane and of non-residential properties in Nether End in Baslow East.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bar Brook ran through the centre of the Baslow East area and caused river flooding concentrated along its banks, resulting in adjacent properties and nearby roads being flooded during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Cock Hill sits at a local low point in the valley adjacent to Bar Brook. ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bar Brook exceeded its banks and the long‑term surface‑water risk map shows the highest surface‑water flood risk where watercourses cross Cock Hill; properties and the road adjacent to the stream are reported or mapped as being affected by flooding during the incident (inferred from the brook overtopping and the mapped high-risk area).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Large volumes of surface water flowed from north of Cock Hill (from springs related to old mine workings) down the hill toward a low point on Cock Hill (A619). This surface-water flow, and associated road erosion (and anecdotal reports of a burst water main), contributed to flooding of the Nether End car park, Baslow Village Hall and nearby properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The surface‑water risk map highlights high risk where the watercourse crosses Church Lane and, given Bar Brook overtopped its banks during the event, buildings and the road at Church Lane are reported or mapped as being affected by flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: High river levels in Bottle Brook during the event contributed to flooding impacts in adjacent communities; elevated levels would have closed a flap valve preventing ingress to the surface water network and were associated with internal flooding of nearby properties (including eight homes in the local community and 17 properties in Lower Kilburn during Storm Babet).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: High river levels in Bottle Brook contributed to flooding in Lower Kilburn, closed a flap valve on a surface water outfall and would have prevented discharge back into the brook, impacting the connected surface water network.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bottle Brook floods its floodplain and has caused river flooding of Lower Kilburn; historical flood incidents are recorded (1977, 2007) and the Environment Agency assessment following Storm Babet indicates recent flood activity associated with the brook that has affected nearby properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River flows in Bottle Brook inundated Gypsy Bridge to the north of Lower Kilburn and then spread southwards, contributing to flooding in Lower Kilburn (combining with surface water from the east).

Floodwater entered properties from both front (via Derby Road) and rear.

The flooded properties lie within Flood Zone 3 and within the Bottle Brook flood alert/warning extents; the long-term surface-water map shows high surface-water flood risk in this area.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Dam Brook, an ordinary watercourse in Derby, was part of the local drainage network associated with the flood event of 08 Nov 2019 - 09 Nov 2019 and is reported alongside other ordinary watercourses and privately owned ditches that were affected. It likely contributed to localised runoff/overland flow and drainage connectivity during the event (some privately owned ditches connecting into the brook were affected). There is insufficient detail to state precise overtopping locations or property-level inundation.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Ock Brook, an ordinary watercourse flowing through the village and culverted under Collier Lane, was associated with the internal flooding of nearby residential properties during Storm Babet. The culverted section beneath Collier Lane is highlighted as a critical location linked to the flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Culvert blockage and raised water levels in Ock Brook caused the brook to overflow its banks; floodwater travelled westward along Cole Lane and Collier Lane and resulted in internal flooding of nearby residential properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of residential properties adjacent to Ock Brook where the channel is culverted; properties lie within or close to the Ock Brook floodplain and were inundated during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: A culvert under Cole Lane was partially blocked, causing Ock Brook to rise upstream and overtop; floodwater flowed along Cole Lane and caused internal flooding to residential properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of residential properties adjacent to Ock Brook at or near a culverted section beneath the road; properties lie within or close to the Ock Brook floodplain and were inundated during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overtopping of Ock Brook led floodwater to flow westward along Collier Lane, resulting in internal flooding of residential properties adjacent to the brook.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from the overflowing Ock Brook flowed along Collier Lane. Exceedance flow from an unnamed watercourse (culverted from Victoria Avenue) also ran down Collier Lane, contributing to out‑of‑bank flows and internal flooding of properties on the lane.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding associated with Dale Brook led to internal flooding of properties in the village of Stoney Middleton; ten properties suffered internal flooding (seven residential and three non-residential).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Dale Brook is the main watercourse through the village and the community is within its floodplain; flooding associated with Dale Brook contributed to internal flooding of nearby properties in Stoney Middleton.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Dale Brook, a shallow watercourse with culverted sections and upstream trash screens, exceeded culvert capacity during the event and flowed out of bank, causing internal flooding to nearby properties and contributing to inundation of The Nook and The Dale; CCTV showed culvert capacity was exceeded though screens/culverts were not blocked.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Dale Brook lies in the valley through the community and its floodplain is the primary cause of river flooding affecting properties along the valley bottom. Flood Zone 3 extents are concentrated immediately along the brook and adjacent properties have been identified as being at high river-flood risk; properties close to the brook also have medium-to-high surface-water flood risk from overland flows.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties along the valley bottom adjacent to Dale Brook were flooded; homes in the community lie in Flood Zone 3 and Flood Zone 2 and have experienced river flooding, and many properties (except one on Denman Crescent) are at medium to high risk of surface-water flooding. A documented flood from a dam failure at Glebe Mine (January 2007) and frequent flooding associated with old mine drainage (soughs) have caused local flooding and flows along a surface-water route from Castle Hill down to The Nook.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: One property in the central Bank area suffered internal flooding during the event; location is close to Dale Brook within the village floodplain.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Non-residential properties located off The Bank were flooded internally.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Bank (labelled on maps as 'The Bank') runs immediately adjacent to Dale Brook and is within the mapped Flood Zone 3/2 extents. Flood mapping and the Long Term Flood Risk Map indicate the highest river and surface-water flood risk concentrated along The Bank, placing properties there at elevated risk and within the area that contains the community's flooded homes.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Middleton Lane lies within the valley area influenced by Dale Brook and falls inside the Flood Zone 3/2 mapping and the Long Term Flood Risk Map's medium-to-high surface-water risk shading. Properties on Middleton Lane therefore lie within the mapped corridor that contains the community's flooded homes and are exposed to river and surface-water flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Eaton Fold is located within the settlement area influenced by Dale Brook and is captured within the Flood Zone 3/2 extents and the Long Term Flood Risk Map's surface-water risk areas. Properties at Eaton Fold are therefore within the mapped floodplain corridor associated with the community's known flooded homes and are exposed to river and surface-water flood hazards.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: A cluster of properties east/south of The Bank, near The Avenue, experienced internal flooding during the event; these properties are close to Dale Brook and in Flood Zone 2/3.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Avenue runs close to Dale Brook and is specifically identified on the flood maps as being within Flood Zone 3/2 and within the Long Term Flood Risk Map's area of highest surface-water risk. Mapping analysis highlights The Avenue as one of the streets where the highest river and surface-water flood risk is concentrated, placing properties there within the zone that contains the community's flooded homes.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of a property on Denman Crescent; the property was flooded despite being located higher on the hillside and mapped in Flood Zone 1.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: One property on Denman Crescent experienced internal flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Surface water runoff from the field behind Denman Crescent caused internal flooding of a home.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: A property on Denman Crescent is recorded among the flooded homes in the community but is located higher on the hillside and mapped in Flood Zone 1 (low river-flood probability).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Local accounts identify a significant surface-water flow route originating on the northwest side of Castle Hill and running down to The Nook, contributing to overland/surface-water flooding of lower properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties around The Nook experienced internal flooding; The Nook road was flooded (including surcharging of old mine drainage/soughs) and damage to properties was observed. Non-residential properties located off The Nook also flooded.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Soughs (old mine drainage) surcharged and flooded properties and The Nook road; surface water runoff from the steep hillside also contributed to flooding of low-lying properties adjacent to the watercourse.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding affected the highway and existing properties in the Edge View/Meadow Close area; Derbyshire County Council is delivering a small mitigation scheme to reduce flood risk to the highway and properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding affected properties in the Edge View/Meadow Close area; a small mitigation scheme will be delivered by Derbyshire County Council to reduce flood risk to the highway and existing properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from ordinary (upstream) watercourses affected the area immediately upstream of the school; Derbyshire County Council are investigating the flooding mechanisms to determine required maintenance actions.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internally flooded as one of the non-residential properties affected in the community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The school (a non-residential property located off Park Road) experienced internal flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Suffered internal flooding primarily from the overflow of ordinary watercourses west of the school and south of the River Ecclesbourne, with additional overland surface water routes from the south contributing. The school was temporarily closed and pupils were relocated to temporary classrooms for several months while flooded classrooms were repaired.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Park Road lies adjacent to the River Ecclesbourne and is shown on the map as being within Flood Zone 3, placing properties along the street at high risk of river flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Wirksworth Road is indicated on the map as being adjacent to the River Ecclesbourne within Flood Zone 3, so properties on this road are at significant risk of river flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the River Ecclesbourne led to internal flooding of one property on Wirksworth Road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Chapel Street is within the mapped flood area and a flood wall is shown running along the riverbanks through the area near Chapel Street, indicating river flood risk to the street and the presence of flood defence infrastructure.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Ecclesbourne corridor at/adjacent to Chapel Street is mapped as a concentrated high surface-water-flood-risk area. Maintenance works (600 tonnes of silt removed under the bridge at Town Street and Chapel Street) were carried out two months before the 18–21 Oct 2023 event to improve conveyance, and the area was within the Duffield locations associated with flooded properties and flood warnings during that event. It is therefore identified as being in the area affected by flooding risk during 18–21 Oct 2023 (some uncertainty remains about whether individual properties on Chapel Street were recorded as flooded).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Milford Road is included within the map extent where flood zones extend into residential streets adjacent to the rivers, indicating exposure to river flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: King Street falls within the mapped urban area where flood zone shading extends into streets adjacent to the rivers, indicating risk from river flooding to properties on the street.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Donald Hawley Way is shown on the map with a flood wall running through the area, indicating it is adjacent to river flood extents and has flood defence infrastructure protecting it.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Homes on Ecclesbourne Avenue were flooded during the event; flooding is spatially associated with the nearby River Ecclesbourne and nearby culverted watercourses, and the street is noted as having a medium chance of surface water flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Some properties on Ecclesbourne Avenue are reported as having flooded and are identified as having a medium chance (1%–3.3% AEP) of surface water flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the tennis courts flowed into rear gardens and onto the road around 14:47 on 20 October 2023, with several properties on the road internally flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the overtopped tennis courts and overflowing River Ecclesbourne flowed into rear gardens and onto the road, causing several properties on Ecclesbourne Avenue to flood internally.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Map evidence and Flood Zone extents indicate the street lies within the river floodplain adjacent to the River Ecclesbourne, putting properties on Ecclesbourne Close at risk of river flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The map shows Flood Zone extents encroaching into residential streets in this area; Granville Close is labelled within that area and therefore was at risk of, and likely affected by, river flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Hill View appears within the mapped Flood Zone extents that extend from the River Ecclesbourne into nearby residential streets, indicating exposure to river flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Holloway Road is shown on the flood map in an area where Flood Zone shading extends into built-up streets adjacent to the River Ecclesbourne, indicating it was exposed to river flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Ecclesbourne overflowed its left bank and flowed overland via the riverside footpath, leading to flooding on Holloway Road (and Tamworth Street); one property on Holloway Road internally flooded.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from the overflowing watercourse at Duck Island reached Holloway Road, causing flooding of the road surface.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Downstream reaches of the River Ecclesbourne recorded shorter and earlier responses to the heavy rainfall during Storm Babet. Gauging stations on the River Ecclesbourne produced some of the highest-ranked flows or levels on record in response to the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River flooding on the Ecclesbourne floodplain was associated with internal flooding of properties in Duffield; flooded homes are concentrated adjacent to the watercourse (notably around Ecclesbourne Avenue and Village Court).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Ecclesbourne flows through the Duffield floodplain and is identified as a main river contributing to flooding of adjacent properties; flood maps show Flood Zone 3/2 adjacent to the river and the report records past and recent flooding in Duffield linked to the watercourse.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding of properties in Duffield associated with the River Ecclesbourne during the event; the river is the subject of flood alerts/warnings and has historic flood defence walls (constructed 1970–1975) intended to provide ~1% AEP standard of protection. The river’s condition (conveyance) was a focus of maintenance activity immediately prior to the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Ecclesbourne exceeded its capacity and overflowed its banks and formal defences in several locations through Duffield, overtopping left banks and defences, flowing overland via the riverside footpath, across Duck Island bridge, and directly causing internal flooding to numerous properties and flooding of roads and gardens.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Raised flows/overflow from the River Ecclesbourne contributed to flooding of adjacent low-lying areas in Duffield, including overflow of ordinary watercourses near the school and flood flows toward Village Court and nearby locations.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Town Street (A6) is mapped with a high chance of surface-water flooding. Two months before the 18–21 Oct 2023 event, 600 tonnes of silt were removed from under the bridge at Town Street (and Chapel Street) to improve conveyance. Town Street was therefore within the area of concern and mapped high-risk corridors associated with the reported flooding and flood warnings during 18–21 Oct 2023 (uncertain which specific Town Street properties flooded).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from the River Ecclesbourne and overtopping defences flowed down Town Street (by ~16:00 on 20 Oct), leading to road closure and internal flooding of residential and non‑residential properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Water flowed down Town Street, forcing the road to be closed for safety.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Defence walls at the club were overtopped (reported to start overflowing at 13:19 on 20 October 2023), resulting in flooding across the tennis courts and contributing to flooding of adjacent properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties on Village Court were internally flooded during the event; homes experienced internal flooding damage.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater reached property thresholds around 14:04 on 20 October 2023 following overtopping of defence walls, and internal flooding of properties occurred.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flood defence walls were overtopped at about 14:04 on 20 Oct 2023, causing floodwater to run across the tennis courts and into properties on Village Court (including the tennis club).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Ecclesbourne overflowed the left bank and flowed over Duck Island bridge onto Duck Island; one property on Duck Island experienced internal flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overflowing at Duck Island led to floodwater spilling onto adjacent roads (annotated as overflow onto Holloway Road) and contributed to local flooding flow routes toward the River Ecclesbourne.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Ecclesbourne overflowed its left bank and flowed overland via the riverside footpath, causing inundation of Tamworth Street.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Environment Agency is considering modifications to the middle of Bradwell Brook to increase capacity because the brook contributed to flooding and flood risk in the village.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bradwell Brook flowed through the village and was associated with concentrated flooding along and near the watercourse; this led to internal flooding of residential and non-residential properties in Bradwell.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bradwell Brook is identified as a source of flooding for the village and is linked to flood alerts/warnings for the area; flooding from the brook has contributed to the community flood incidents described.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from Bradwell Brook contributed to property flooding in the village during Storm Babet; the brook flows through the centre of Bradwell and is associated with flood zones and the 'Bradwell Brook at Bradwell' flood warning. Culverts and a debris screen on the brook are noted in the area.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bradwell Brook exceeded its capacity and overtopped at Church Street bridge, contributing to flooding of Church Street and Soft Water Lane. High flows combined with converging surface water to flood onto adjacent streets. A culvert under a property built over the brook may have been restricted by silt/debris, exacerbating local flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Bradwell Brook is identified in the report as the watercourse causing local flooding; properties adjacent to the brook are within the flood warning/alert area and have been flooded in past events. The brook contributes to elevated surface-water flood risk concentrated along streets adjacent to the watercourse.

info.text: Internal flooding of residential properties on Brookside caused by high flows in Bradwell Brook and concurrent surface water during Storm Babet; properties were inundated internally.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Surface water flowed downhill onto Brookside, discharging through a drystone retaining wall onto the road. This surface water runoff contributed to internal flooding of properties on Brookside.

info.text: Drainage surcharging (potential sewer/drain surcharge) was reported on Church Street during the flood investigation; Severn Trent is investigating the issue.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties on or near Church Street were among those internally flooded in Bradwell when Bradwell Brook and associated runoff inundated parts of the village during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties on Church Street experienced internal flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties on Church Street suffered internal flooding from an unnamed watercourse to their rear; residents reported fast-flowing water through properties and opened doors to let water pass to limit structural damage. Drains on Church Street were observed surcharging with manhole covers lifted. Flood water from the unnamed watercourse also contributed to flooding on the B6049. Flood depth near the bridge was reported as shin deep.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Reported shin-deep flooding near the bridge on Church Street during the event; issues of potential drainage surcharging on Church Street are being investigated by Severn Trent.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of residential properties on Soft Water Lane due to overflow from local watercourses and surface water runoff during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Surface water from the north, east and south converged down towards Bradwell Brook; high flows in Bradwell Brook exceeded channel capacity and flooded onto Soft Water Lane. Flooding on Soft Water Lane was exacerbated by a property built over Bradwell Brook where a silt/debris build up under the property may have reduced culvert capacity. Flood depths on Soft Water Lane were reported to be deeper than shin‑depth.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of properties in the village during Storm Babet; both residential and non-residential buildings were flooded, affecting homes, businesses and the local tourist economy.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of domestic and non-domestic properties in the village: properties located on the floodplain of Peakshole Water were inundated during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of homes and businesses in the community during the Storm Babet event; residents used sandbags and makeshift defences were built on the Riverside Path.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Peakshole Water (the main watercourse through the village) and surface water caused internal flooding of homes and businesses; residents used sandbags and makeshift defences; flood alert issued and local flood wardens responded.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Peakshole Water reached capacity and overtopped its banks: a large volume of water emerging from the cave system caused flooding of The Stones; overflow from Peakshole Water flooded Eades Fold and Vicarage Lane; water breached drystone walls behind Mill Court gardens, flowed onto Millbridge and then surged down Tricketts Close (first recorded flow on this route); flow was constrained by the low bridge on Millbridge causing upstream backup; floodwater also escaped at the culvert grill at Eyre's Farm and flowed south along Hollowford Road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Peakshole Water overtopped/triggered river flooding affecting properties on its floodplain in Castleton; properties that flooded during the event have also been flooded by Peakshole Water in previous years.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Identified as the watercourse expected to cause flooding; high river levels from Peakshole Water contributed to flooding and prompted alerts and the use of a flap valve to prevent backing up into the surface water drainage network.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Identified as the main source of flooding — rapidly rose during intense rainfall (fed by the cave system/Peak Cavern) and overtopped its banks, flooding adjacent streets (for example onto The Stones, and causing flooding at Eades Fold and Vicarage Lane) and properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Reached capacity and overflowed its banks; flooded over the right bank onto The Stones and was the source of flooding to nearby streets and properties (Eades Fold, Vicarage Lane, Mill Court, Millbridge and Tricketts Close).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Forty-five homes internally flooded; floodwater reached about halfway up external doors and walls. All properties on the east side of Windemere Road and the majority on the west side were internally flooded. Some properties on Clay Lane, Coniston Drive and Grasmere Avenue also flooded. Roads were impassable during the event, preventing sandbag delivery by the district council.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Smithy Brook flows southwards through Clay Cross and its floodplain underlies part of the community; Flood Zones 2 and 3 follow the brook and are concentrated along it, indicating the brook caused river flooding affecting adjacent residential properties and Meadow Farm Pond.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties adjacent to Windermere Road were located within Flood Zones 2 and 3 and experienced flooding risk from Smithy Brook (river flooding). The Long Term Flood Risk Map indicates many properties on the east side have medium–high surface water flood risk and some properties (including on the west side) experienced internal flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Widespread internal flooding of residential properties: all properties on the east side of Windemere Road flooded internally and the majority of properties on the west side flooded; floodwater marked about halfway up a door/wall in at least one property.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: St Mary's Bridge on the River Derwent experienced the longest lag time between peak rainfall and peak flow (27 hours) and produced one of the highest-ranked flows or levels on record in response to Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: St Marys Bridge acted as a constriction on river flow during the event; exceedance channel routing and overtopping were used to bypass the constriction so flows could re-enter the channel south of the bridge, altering local flow paths and contributing to water collecting in the underpass.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: A request was made to raise the flood warning threshold at Ambergate affecting the Ridgeway community following the event.

info.text: Internal floodwaters reached about 0.9 m and entered homes via doorways. The local pumping station was overwhelmed and had no free outlet, causing the sewer network to back up and residents to experience foul flooding overflowing from drains around properties. Surface water flowing downhill from the railway/Bullbridge area to the north of Riversdale contributed to the flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooded when Bar Brook exceeded its channel capacity and overflowed its banks; combined with surface-water runoff from Cock Hill (including flows from springs and road-erosion-related flows), this led to inundation of the car park.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Debris blocked a culvert (reported ~60% blocked) restricting flows; post‑event inspections identified undermined banks, a missing flap valve from an outfall and sections of walls in poor condition requiring riparian owner repairs.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper flooding caused elevated flood risk to downstream communities (Holymoorside, Chatsworth Rd West, Brampton, Central Chesterfield, Tapton Terrace); the Environment Agency is exploring upstream flood-storage options to reduce this river flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the River Hipper (ordinary watercourse through Holymoorside) inundated residential properties in the village, causing internal flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flows through Holymoorside on its floodplain and contributed to flooding during the event; flood outlines were recorded along the watercourse and at nearby road crossings, associated with internal flooding of local properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: High river levels at the Holymoorside gauge on 20 October 2023 (rise beginning ~00:00, peaking ~12:00) contributed to the flood extent in Holymoorside and inundation of nearby residential properties and a business. River Hipper levels reached a record gauge reading and are identified as a causal contributor to the internal flooding of properties on The Alders, New Road and Loads Road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper rose rapidly (peak gauge at Holymoorside on 20 Oct) and overtopped its banks at multiple locations through the village and near Old Mill Pond; overtopping entered properties from the rear (including The Alders, New Road and Loads Road) and contributed directly to the internal flooding of homes and the overtopping of Old Mill Pond.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The river overtopped its banks at multiple locations near Old Mill Pond and through Holymoorside; Old Mill Pond overtopped local to a weir. Overtopping upstream of Loads Road bridge and restricted bridge arch capacity caused floodwater to flow east along Loads Road and pool at the Loads Road / New Road low spot, contributing to internal flooding of properties (including The Alders and two homes at the New Road/Loads Road junction).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper flooded during the storm and is identified as the main river flowing through the community; floodwaters from the River Hipper resulted in internal flooding of nearby properties (all flooded properties are within 75 m of the river). The Storm Babet recorded flood outline closely follows the River Hipper corridor.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the River Hipper affected the adjacent Chatsworth Road West community; properties on the river floodplain and at similar elevation to the top bank were internally flooded.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper water levels rose during the event, reaching a recorded peak (gauge c.20 m upstream of Walton Road bridge reached 3.59 m, the highest on record) on 20 Oct, with levels rising from early morning and peaking at 13:00; these high river levels caused flooding of the nearby residential properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper exceeded its channel and breached its banks at multiple locations in the community. At Chapel Lane West the river breached the north bank and flowed north up the street. River water entered five homes on Walton Road through their rear gardens and flooded them internally. River flows are also understood to have been a dominant source of flooding at Chapel Lane West and are likely connected to flooding affecting Grove Cottages (possible flows through drainage holes in the riverside wall). Residents reported waist‑high water at the south end of Chapel Street West adjacent to the River Hipper.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper flowed through Brampton and was a principal flood source during Storm Babet; it contributed to internal flooding across the community. The Hipper is heavily modified and culverted at multiple locations within the community, which is described in the report as part of the flooding mechanism.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper overtopped/caused fluvial flooding across the local floodplain during the event, inundating built-up areas south of Chatsworth Road (including Wheatbridge Road, Dock Walk and Anna Street West). Topographic data shows flooded properties sit at similar elevation to the top bank, with low spots in the floodplain contributing to inundation.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper is a primary watercourse in the Brampton floodplain and is identified as concentrating the highest flood risk along its banks (Flood Zone 3), contributing to the flooding of adjacent properties and areas.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper rose to very high levels on 20 October 2023 and its rise contributed to fluvial flooding that led to internal flooding in the Brampton community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overtopped on the right bank upstream of Factory Street Bridge and was a primary source of floodwater that inundated a derelict brownfield site, flowed onto Factory Street and into the Lidl car park, and generated flow routes into low-lying areas of the community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper overtopped near a derelict brownfield site upstream of Factory Street, inundating that site and initiating flooding of Factory Street, the Lidl car park and downstream sections of Chatsworth Road; the river also surcharged a culvert beneath the Lidl entrance allowing river water to join the road network.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper overtopped just upstream of the culvert beneath Boythorpe Road, contributing to localised flooding and infrastructure damage. Overtopping and high flows are linked to internal flooding in the adjacent streets and to structural damage (a riparian-owned brick wall collapsed upstream of the culvert immediately west of Boythorpe Road).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flood Warning issued for the River Hipper at Brampton on 20/10/2023 (11:15). EA/FIDO reported River Hipper flooding with lots of debris and land drainage blockages, a collapsed wall was reported on the Hipper in Chesterfield, and post-event channel clearance and inspections were carried out (including identification of defects in retaining/boundary walls and a culvert). Floodwater made some properties inaccessible and prompted sandbag requests from local streets.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding along the River Hipper caused internal flooding to businesses at multiple locations as it passed through central Chesterfield.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overtopping/channel flooding from the River Hipper inundated adjacent floodplain and contributed to flooding of properties and urban areas in Central Chesterfield during the 19 Oct 2023 – 21 Oct 2023 event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the River Hipper led to internal flooding of properties adjacent to the watercourse; a Flood Warning for 'The River Hipper at Central Chesterfield' was issued on 20 Oct 2023 covering the internally flooded properties (excluding one business on Park Road).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper overflowed its banks, causing internal flooding to businesses at Queens Park and Ravenside Retail Park; watermarks show substantial internal inundation at affected buildings.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper overflowed its banks at Queens Park and Ravenside Retail Park, causing internal flooding to businesses in those locations. Floodwater reached approx. 0.7 m depth at a Queens Park business and approx. 0.8 m depth inside an internally flooded business at Ravenside Retail Park; ten businesses at Ravenside/Queens Park were flooded. Hydrology at the Chesterfield Park Road Bridge gauge on the River Hipper recorded an unprecedented peak on 20 October (gauge peak reached 2.93 m). The River Rother overflowed near Hasland Road (about 100 m upstream of its confluence with Spital Brook), causing internal flooding to one commercial property to the west of the river and four residential properties to the east.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Hipper overtopped near the Clayton Street Bridge, initiating flooding that flowed north down Clayton Street and contributed to internal flooding of properties on Clayton Street.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the River Hipper places properties in Chesterfield at risk; the Environment Agency is developing a business case for a flood alleviation scheme to reduce that risk.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Flood Warning issued for the River Hipper at Brampton on 20/10/2023 (11:15). EA/FIDO reported River Hipper flooding with lots of debris and land drainage blockages, a collapsed wall was reported on the Hipper in Chesterfield, and post-event channel clearance and inspections were carried out (including identification of defects in retaining/boundary walls and a culvert). Floodwater made some properties inaccessible and prompted sandbag requests from local streets.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Seven residential properties suffered internal flooding in the main group of houses west of the River Doe Lea during Storm Babet; flooding occurred in the area west of the River Doe Lea with nearby ordinary watercourses and ditches (Pools Brook, Ditch 1, Ditch 2) connected through the local drainage network.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Seven residential properties suffered internal flooding during Storm Babet. The recorded Storm Babet flood outline (pink) covered central and eastern parts of the village, particularly areas near Staveley Road, The Grove and Cottage Close. Flooding was associated with local ordinary watercourses and ditches (Pools Brook, Ditch 1 and Ditch 2) in the vicinity of the affected properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Recorded flood outline from Storm Babet (Oct 2023) overlaps parts of the community; homes within the community were flooded during the event and homes near Ditch 1 have high surface-water flood risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding occurred to properties within the village during Storm Babet. Six residential properties and one non-residential property suffered internal flooding across two streets: five properties adjacent to the Staveley Road / Poolsbrook Crescent junction and two newer-build homes on the Erin Court development. National mapping also shows a high surface-water flood risk (≥3.3% AEP) for homes near Ditch 1 and along low-lying areas adjacent to the River Doe Lea.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flood extent at Poolsbrook covered the low spot at the Staveley Road / Poolsbrook Crescent junction and surrounding area; parts of Erin Court and Staveley Road were impacted and land surrounding Ditch 1 flooded. In total six residential properties and one non-residential property suffered internal flooding across the area.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from woodland and from Ditch 2 flowed into the Erin Court housing development, internally flooding two newer-build homes. That water then flowed downslope along Staveley Road to the low spot at the Staveley Road / Poolsbrook Crescent junction, resulting in internal flooding of properties at that low spot. The sewer network also discharged at locations including the rear of No.58 Staveley Road, the junction of Staveley Road and Poolsbrook Crescent, and from a trunk sewer adjacent to the eastern end of Ditch 1, which contributed to the event. Land surrounding Ditch 1 also flooded.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater flowed from Ditch 2 and the ordinary watercourse to the south, with a partially blocked headwall identified during investigations as likely contributing to flooding. Overland flow from the ordinary watercourse to the south was also identified as a contributing/exacerbating source. The Environment Agency flood alert covered part of Poolsbrook to the east (though internally-flooded properties were not located within the alert area).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Outflowing floodwater entered Erin Court and flowed down Staveley Road; an unnamed ditch passing through Erin Court ('Ditch 1') was identified for maintenance to better accommodate floodwater capacity. Investigations were carried out to determine whether drainage arrangements to the south of the southern ordinary watercourse contributed to the outflow into Erin Court.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Storm Babet recorded flood outline overlaps parts of the Erin Court development; those parts experienced flooding during the Oct 2023 event. The same area was also flooded by the River Doe Lea in June 2007 prior to development.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of newer-build homes within the Erin Court housing development.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from the woodland to the south flowed into the Erin Court development and internally flooded two newer-build homes near the end of Staveley Road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23
