ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding of the River Whitting during Storm Babet inundated adjacent floodplain and contributed to internal flooding of properties on Station Road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Whitting overtopped or threatened its banks and caused river flooding of the retail/residential floodplain. Properties that flooded sit at similar elevation to the top of the River Whitting bank and are lower than surrounding ground. Flood Zone 3 covers the properties affected; the October 2023 event (19 Oct 2023 - 21 Oct 2023) produced more extensive flooding than the June 2007 event. Flood management features (walls, embankments, culverts) are present along the river corridor.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flood Warnings were issued for the River Whitting at Old Whittington and Sheepbridge; properties on Station Road and a business on Whitting Valley Road flooded on the banks of the River Whitting. The river corridor and adjacent embankment were implicated in the flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The River Whitting was the primary source of flooding: it rose on 20 Oct and overtopped its east bank (south of the Station Road bridge), initiating the overland flow that inundated Whitting Valley Road and Station Road properties. Gauge data at Sheepbridge reached a peak (highest recorded) and coincided with the timing of impacts in the community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Area around the intersection of Station Road and Whittington Way was the focus of Storm Babet flooding; nearby residential properties suffered internal flooding. The community sits on the River Whitting floodplain and properties are at similar elevation to the top of the river bank, contributing to inundation.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Road and adjacent retail/residential properties lie within Flood Zone 3 along the River Whitting floodplain and are shown on mapping to have a high risk of surface water flooding. Properties adjacent to Whittington Way were within the flood warning area and exposed to both river inundation and surface water flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Street and nearby properties sit within the Flood Zone 3 area along the River Whitting corridor and are indicated as having high surface water flood risk. They were exposed to river flooding and surface-water inundation during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Located adjacent to the River Whitting/Ridding Brook flood corridor within Flood Zone 3 and mapped as high surface water risk; properties and infrastructure on Whitting Valley Road were impacted by river and surface-water flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Storm Babet recorded flood outline overlaps Brimington Road on the map and high/medium surface-water risk zones are adjacent to the road, indicating the road was exposed to floodwater during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Non-residential properties in the industrial area around Brimington Road flooded as part of the localised impact from the River Rother.

info.text: Holland Road is shown adjacent to Flood Zone 3 along the River Whitting/Ridding Brook with properties in the vicinity mapped as high surface-water flood risk; adjacent commercial and residential properties were exposed to river and surface-water flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties and commercial buildings on Prospect Road (part of the retail district on the River Whitting floodplain) were inundated by river flooding from the River Whitting and by surface water flooding during the 19 Oct 2023 - 21 Oct 2023 event. ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Subject of an investigation (site inspection and discussions) by the Derbyshire County Council Flood Team to determine the mechanisms and extent of flooding on Chapel Lane West.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: At Chapel Lane West the River Hipper breached its banks and flowed northward up the street to about 92.7 mAOD. River water was the dominant flood source at Chapel Lane West, with additional contribution from surface water runoff from Chatsworth Road (either direct runoff or surcharging of the surface water network).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Hipper passed south of Lordsmill Street and two businesses were internally flooded due to the river flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Identified as a key transport route within or adjacent to Flood Zone 2/3 and inside the Flood Warning Area along the river corridors. Lordsmill Street was affected by river-flooding impacts during the 19 Oct 2023 - 21 Oct 2023 event, posing disruption to transport and access in Central Chesterfield.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding/raised flood risk at Horns Bridge led Yorkshire Water to investigate the feasibility of a storage measure to reduce future flood risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Located close to the River Hipper/River Rother flood corridors within Flood Zone 3 and inside the Flood Warning Area. The roundabout and immediate transport infrastructure were affected by river flooding during the 19 Oct 2023 - 21 Oct 2023 event, creating risk and likely disruption to traffic and access.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Was located within the 'River Rother at Central Chesterfield' Flood Warning area issued on 20 October 2023 and is mapped as being within high surface-water flood risk adjacent to the River Rother; the roundabout and its immediate infrastructure were therefore exposed to flood risk during the 19–21 October 2023 event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: All arms of the roundabout were impassable due to flooding; watermarks on railings and signposts indicate flood depths reached about 0.5m. Flooding at the adjacent A617 low spot (beneath the railway) exceeded 0.5m and was caused by a combination of the River Rother overflowing, sewer surcharging and surface water.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Experienced surcharging of the sewer/network and was identified as a location that may have contributed to local flooding during the storm; subject of consideration for capacity improvements.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Catchment experienced high flows that contributed to flooding downstream into the River Rother; authorities are identifying potential sites for upstream flood storage to slow flows and reduce downstream flood risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Spital Brook, an ordinary watercourse joining the River Rother in central Chesterfield, is within the area that experienced internal flooding (central Chesterfield areas included Spital Lane).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overtopping or local runoff associated with Spital Brook contributed to flooding in its corridor, impacting properties on/near Spital Lane and adjacent areas in Central Chesterfield during the 19 Oct 2023 – 21 Oct 2023 event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties adjacent to Spital Brook were identified as affected and were included in the 'River Rother at Central Chesterfield' Flood Warning issued on 20 October 2023; those adjacent properties experienced internal flooding during the 19–21 October 2023 event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Spital Brook exceeded channel capacity and contributed to internal flooding of properties adjacent to the brook and River Rother.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Spital Brook overflowed and delivered floodwater to properties along Spital Lane, causing internal flooding of homes and non-residential buildings before joining the River Rother.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Ground floor internal flooding of the building caused by the River Rother overflowing its banks; reports of sewage indicate the sewer system was overwhelmed and contributed to contamination.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding occurred in Meadow Close within New Whittington during Storm Babet, affecting local residences.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Station Lane lies within the recorded Storm Babet flood outline adjacent to Meadow Close; ordinary watercourse flows beneath Station Lane and the flood outline overlapped this road, forming part of the local flood pathway that contributed to internal flooding of nearby properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from the River Rother crossed Station Lane, indicating inundation of the highway and flow paths crossing the road.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Moss tributary was identified as the primary source of flooding affecting the community; flood flows from The Moss inundated low-lying areas north of the watercourse and caused internal flooding to nearby properties. Trees fell and were reported blocking The Moss after the event, creating a continued flood risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties on Pipworth Lane were internally flooded as part of the event driven by The Moss tributary; residents reported flood depths and blockages (fallen trees) on The Moss which exacerbated flooding risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Maped high/medium surface-water risk zones and the recorded Storm Babet flood outline extend into built-up areas near Sheffield Road; the recorded flood outline aligns with these risk areas, indicating Sheffield Road environs were likely affected by surface-water/urban flooding during Storm Babet. The text and map do not give an explicit statement that the road itself was inundated.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The southern end of Sheffield Road was flooded during the incident.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Homes on Rotherham Road flooded internally during Storm Babet; these homes were flooded due to overbank/tributary flooding associated with The Moss (possible additional influence from high River Rother levels). An additional commercial property in the same immediate area also flooded internally.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Five homes on Rotherham Road (north of The Moss tributary and east of the River Rother) flooded internally during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Pools Brook is an ordinary watercourse to the west of Poolsbrook and lies within the local drainage network shown on the Storm Babet recorded flood mapping. It is located immediately west of the area where residential properties flooded during Storm Babet and is part of the watercourse system linked to the flooded area (via Ditch 1). This places Pools Brook within the vicinity of the recorded flooding and as a likely component of local flow pathways during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties adjacent to the watercourse experienced internal flooding during Storm Babet. Flood Zone 3 coverage is mapped adjacent to Cotton Mill Hill indicating river flooding from the River Hipper, and national surface water mapping shows medium–high surface water flood risk for the internally flooded homes.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Areas around Bobbin Mill Lane are shown within or adjacent to the Storm Babet recorded flood outline and some homes on Bobbin Mill Lane are identified as having high long‑term risk of surface water flooding; the recorded event indicates the lane/nearby properties were affected by flood inundation or high surface water during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Clifton Street is shown within the mapped Flood Zone 2/3 extent and overlapping flood alert/warning areas in Brampton, and therefore was within the area exposed to river and surface-water flooding during the 19–21 Oct 2023 event. Properties here are in the floodplain of the River Hipper / Holme Brook and were part of the mapped flood-affected area.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Map and flood-zone mapping in the report place Springfield Avenue inside the mapped floodplain/flood zone area for the community (overlapping Flood Zone 2 / Flood Zone 3 and Flood Alert/Warning outlines). ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Old Hall Road is shown within the mapped Brampton floodplain where Flood Zone 2 (and areas of Flood Zone 3 nearby) overlap streets and properties. ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Foljambe Road is mapped within the Brampton floodplain area where Flood Zone 2 and Flood Zone 3 extents and Flood Alert/Warning outlines intersect streets and properties. The road and nearby properties were therefore exposed to river flooding from the River Hipper / Home Brook and to surface-water inundation during the 19–21 Oct 2023 event, contributing to local property flood risk.

info.text: Located adjacent to the River Rother within the mapped Flood Zone 3 area; it lies within the footprint of flooding that produced most of the flooded homes west of the river during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from the River Rother flooded properties in the Tapton community. Twenty-six homes on Tapton Terrace suffered internal flooding (rear of properties first, then the front) with flood depths reaching up to 1.5 m in some properties; external PFR measures were exceeded. One resident died. Nearby industrial areas around Brimington Road and Holbeck Close also experienced internal flooding of non-residential premises, contributing to a combined total of forty-three residential and non-residential properties flooded in the local community.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: River Rother at Tapton was issued a Flood Warning (20 Oct); Tapton Terrace within Tapton saw requests for sandbags and emergency service attendance including a fatality.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The A61 was flooded from Horns Bridge Roundabout to about 200m south at the Byron Street junction; the A61/Around Byron Street was impassable and the electricity substation on the A61 opposite Byron Street was flooded, leaving homes without power.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from the River Rother accumulated at the low spot beneath the railway underpass/bridge (East Midlands Main Line), causing pooling beneath the structure, preventing safe passage through the underpass and contributing to internal flooding of nearby ground-floor properties; footage shows people evacuating east of the underpass by wading through floodwater.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwaters from the recorded Storm Babet outline extended into business/industrial areas near Rotherside Road; commercial properties within/adjacent to the business park experienced internal flooding.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Commercial properties on Eckington Business Park (south of The Moss and east of the River Rother) were internally flooded during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Recorded flood outline from Storm Babet extended into Rotherside Road and adjacent land; flood waters affected nearby residential and business areas and were associated with internal flooding of properties in Eckington.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The recorded Storm Babet flood outline on the map overlaps areas adjacent to Rotherside Road; built-up areas near the road lie within high/medium modelled surface-water risk and the observed outline aligns with those risk areas. It is therefore likely the area near Rotherside Road was affected by surface-water/flooding during Storm Babet, though the map does not explicitly state the road surface itself was inundated.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Dove sub-catchment experienced hydrological effects during Storm Babet (changes to river flows and levels across the Dove catchment).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Dove sub-catchment experienced extreme rainfall during Storm Babet which drove high river flows in the catchment; Henmore Brook is a tributary of the Dove and contributed to flooding in Ashbourne.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: High flows on the River Dove at the confluence with Rolleston Brook are implicated in the mapped flood location; River Dove flows and its confluence contributed to flooding observed adjacent to Rolleston-on-Dove.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: The River Dove influenced the extent of flooding in the area and contributed to inundation of nearby residential areas; its proximity to Brookside is linked to properties there being flooded during the event on 16 February 2020.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: High flows in the River Dove prompted the operation/closure of nearby control gates during the flood response. Two control gates under the railway were closed during the weekend of 16–17 February 2020, and the Tutbury sluice gate was closed on the morning of 17 February 2020 to prevent River Dove flood flows moving through culverts or down the Tutbury Mill Fleam. The report concluded these gates do not have capacity to divert significant volumes and were unlikely to have caused the flooding experienced at Brookside.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: Identified as influencing flooding of the Rolleston Brook; the modelling study will assess the River Dove's influence and joint probability of events with Rolleston Brook to understand flood mechanisms and impacts on properties.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: The River Dove is described as increasing the extent of Flood Zones 2 and 3 in the lower-lying parts of the floodplain downstream of the hotel at Brookside, contributing to larger flood extents in that area.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: Responded rapidly to Storm Babet (short lag between peak rainfall and peak flow) and produced high flows that contributed to flooding in Ashbourne; peak flow during Storm Babet was the second highest on record at the Ashbourne gauging station.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Henmore Brook had a very large peak flow during Storm Babet (second highest on the gauging station record), with a short 3-hour lag from peak rainfall to peak flow; the brook on its floodplain contributed to internal flooding of properties to the west of Ashbourne.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overbanking of Henmore Brook during the storm caused river flooding that inundated the adjacent residential community in central Ashbourne. Floodwaters entered homes in the Almshouses on School Lane and properties on Coachmans Close and affected non‑residential buildings including St Oswald’s Church Centre (hall), Kingdom Hall and the Bridge Public House on Dig Street.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding from Henmore Brook overtopped flood defences and caused internal property flooding in the adjacent Ashbourne community (properties on School Lane, Coachmans Close and nearby non-residential buildings). Flood warnings were issued for the Henmore Brook at Ashbourne during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Identified as the primary source of flooding during Storm Babet; overtopping of Henmore Brook banks and a retaining wall allowed flow to escape the channel and inundate adjacent streets and properties (notably School Lane and Coachmans Close).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Banks of Henmore Brook overtopped, sending water northwards along School Lane into the Almshouses courtyard and properties; overtopping adjacent to School Lane bridge also directed flows that flooded nearby buildings. Flood levels exceeded the previous 1% AEP design standard at this location and at Coachmans Close. The embankment protecting the Almshouses did not overtop but was purposefully lowered after Storm Babet's peak to allow trapped water to drain and was subsequently reinstated.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Described as the subject of post-event actions: the Environment Agency is updating the Henmore Brook flood model to investigate the current standard of protection provided by defences and to test whether water can be stored earlier in the Ashbourne Flood Storage Reservoir during lower-magnitude events. These actions follow flooding on 20 October 2023.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Internal flooding of properties in the Almshouses complex on School Lane; the majority of the community's flooded homes were in this complex.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties within the Almshouses complex had floodwater enter the courtyard and then the properties through doorways after Henmore Brook overtopped adjacent defences; internal flooding depths reported up to 15 cm. The protective embankment did not overtop but was temporarily lowered after the peak to allow trapped water to drain.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Properties on School Lane (including the Almshouses) experienced internal flooding during Storm Babet; the area sits on the Henmore Brook floodplain.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: The Almshouses complex on School Lane (majority of properties in the complex) were part of the community that flooded; properties experienced internal flooding during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flooding affected the School Lane area, prompting the Environment Agency to consider raising defences, raising access ramps/embankments and to investigate lowering a downstream bank to allow flood water into the floodplain earlier to reduce flood levels.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater from Henmore Brook overtopped the banks and a retaining wall, flowed north along School Lane into the Almshouses courtyard and entered properties through doorways, causing internal flooding and prompting lowering of a protective embankment post-peak to drain trapped water (subsequently reinstated).

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties on Coachmans Close, north of Henmore Brook, suffered internal flooding during Storm Babet; parts of Coachmans Close are also identified on long-term mapping as having a high surface-water flood risk.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Residential properties on Coachmans Close were flooded during the event; properties experienced internal flooding as part of the community-wide flooding adjacent to Henmore Brook.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Lowest sections of flood defences at Coachmans Close were identified for raising to a consistent level to provide additional short-term protection following flooding; works are planned by the Environment Agency.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Floodwater flowed over the embankment north of the properties and flood defence wall to the east and south of Coachmans Close overtopped along its length, resulting in internal flooding of properties.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flood levels in this location exceeded the previous 1% AEP design standard during the event.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Flood defences around Coachmans Close were identified as having low sections and embankment height issues during the response to the 20 October 2023 flooding. Short-term works planned for summer 2024 include raising the lowest sections of the defence wall to a consistent crest level and raising the embankment to match the coping stones.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Hilton Brook overflowed upstream of Hilton village, overtopped its channel (upstream of the relief channel) and caused flooding onto Uttoxeter Road and into nearby properties. ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Overflowed (about 600 m upstream of the Uttoxeter Road crossing) and overtopped upstream of the village; a blocked culvert beneath Uttoxeter Road caused the channel to overtop and flood onto Uttoxeter Road, with floodwater flowing westwards and along flow routes to Main Street and Mill Lane, internally flooding local properties. Internal depths reached almost 1 m at some properties; some semi‑detached properties are known to flood frequently; one property had a sump and pump; a few properties only flooded externally.

ref.title: Derbyshire County Council Section 19 Investigation Report – Storm Babet 18/10/23 – 21/10/23

info.text: Hilton Brook overtopped/caused flooding at Sutton on the Hill and Uttoxeter Road (Hilton), leading to property flooding. Sandbags provided to some properties were overwhelmed by high flood levels. The flood relief channel was inspected and found to be operating as designed; investigations are exploring redirecting floodwater that currently escapes upstream back into the Hilton Brook channel to reduce future property flooding.

info.text: The urban surface water sewer network in the Oakwood area of Derby discharges to Oakwood Brook. During the intense rainfall of 19th July 2014 the network capacity would be exceeded and large volumes of runoff from paved urban areas were focused rapidly toward the sewer outfall and the brook, increasing downstream surface water flood risk and concentrating flow toward the base of the local valleys.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Bishops Drive, Oakwood 19th July 2014

info.text: During the intense rainfall event on 19 July 2014, large areas of impermeable urban surface drained to adopted highways gullies and to public surface water sewers which outfall to an unnamed tributary of the River Derwent. Floodwaters propagated along local overland flow routes toward the Wood Brook and Oakwood Brook valleys. At least 10 homes were flooded internally on Bishops Drive, Saffron Drive, Columbine Close, Santolina Drive, Morefern Drive and Bryony Close. An undetermined number of properties suffered severe external flooding to highways and gardens, with some external inundation close to entering ground-floor living areas.

ref.title: Section 19 Report: Markeaton

info.text: The village experienced flooding in July 2012; the previous study concluded that surface water runoff (overland flow) was a significant contributing factor to the observed July 2012 flood extents, and river flooding from local brooks alone could not recreate the extent of inundation seen in the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Report: Markeaton

info.text: The July 2012 flood extents in Markeaton are attributed largely to surface water runoff (overland flow following topography) rather than river flooding alone; surface water runoff was identified as a significant contributing factor to the observed flooding extents in July 2012.

ref.title: Section 19 Report: Markeaton

info.text: Previous flood-risk work specifically modelled flooding mechanisms along Mackworth Brook as part of assessing the July 2012 event. The brook is identified as a watercourse flowing from the northwest toward downstream receptors and was therefore implicated in the movement of water toward the Markeaton study area; the report does not explicitly confirm overtopping or a direct record of the brook causing the internal flooding of properties but treats it as a potential contributor to the July 2012 flooding.

ref.title: Section 19 Report: Markeaton

info.text: Surface water runoff and drainage capacity on Markeaton Lane were examined after the July 2012 event. DCC (highways authority) maintained the drainage to its design capacity; options to reduce flow easterly into a culverted ditch under Markeaton Lane were identified as a potential low‑cost mitigation, and improvements to the local drainage outfall were considered but judged unlikely to materially reduce flood severity in extreme events. The assessment concludes the July 2012 flooding was driven by an extremely wet catchment and that even a redesigned surface water system may not have significantly reduced the observed severity.

info.text: Map material and the report describe surface water and watercourse flows being channelled toward Markeaton Park and Markeaton Lake, with flood-relief culvert inlets at the park's northern boundary. The July 2012 event resulted in Markeaton Lane being impassable to the north of Markeaton village and reduced visitor numbers to a commercial site (attributed to the access restriction). The park is therefore a downstream receptor of the runoff and was indirectly affected via access disruption and reduced visitation; the text does not clearly document internal inundation of park buildings.

ref.title: Section 19 Report: Markeaton

info.text: The Markeaton and Mackworth brooks interact via weirs and high-level overflows at the west side of Markeaton Park, creating hydraulic interactions that influenced flow paths during heavy rainfall and contributed to the flood behaviour observed in July 2012.

ref.title: Section 19 Report: Markeaton

info.text: River flows during July 2012 were modelled (including >1 in 100 annual probability flows and culvert blockages) and while river flooding was expected along Markeaton Brook, the modelling showed river flooding alone would not reproduce the observed July 2012 flood extents nor produce internal property flooding; thus Markeaton Brook contributed but was not the sole cause of the July 2012 flooding.

ref.title: Devon Floods 20-21st October 2021

info.text: Multiple watercourses and surface runoff caused widespread flooding across Axminster. The Weycroft area had nine properties flooded (three due to the River Axe overtopping and six primarily from ordinary watercourse and surface runoff). The flood bank upstream of Stoney Bridges was overtopped. Surface water runoff from adjacent farmland into Lodge Lane and overtopping of an unnamed ordinary watercourse caused significant flooding in Weycroft around 20:30–21:00 on 20 October 2021, which was then exacerbated by the Axe overtopping around 23:30 with peak river conditions at 00:05 and 03:00 on 21 October 2021. At least two other ordinary watercourses overtopped where culverted under the A358 during peak flows, causing property flooding in the southern urban extent. A local school and church also experienced surface water flooding; garden and road flooding occurred on multiple streets including Musbury Road, Fairy Lane, Lyme Road and Stoney Lane.

info.text: On 17 September 2023 intense rainfall caused overwhelming runoff and the local watercourse to exceed capacity, producing flood flows that internally flooded properties across the village. Floodwater swept through Mamhead Road, down Church Road and into the Triangle, crossed Fore Street (A379) and affected properties at the lower end of the village (Bramley Close). Downstream on the River Kenn a further four properties on Powderham Estate were flooded and one property outside Kenton at Chiverstone was flooded. The flood depths reached up to 1 m in places; the force of the water ripped tall garden gates off their hinges and sent them into a school building.

ref.title: Kingsbridge 4th June 2022

info.text: Central Kingsbridge (including the Bridge Street area) experienced the majority of flooding on 4 June 2022: heavy rainfall caused surface water to overwhelm highway drains and flood into properties; fluvial risk from the local watercourse exacerbated surface water flooding when the watercourse could not accept additional flows; tide locking contributed to drainage failure in the combined system. Photographic evidence shows floodwater reaching the bottom of car doors and building entrances.

ref.title: Kingsbridge 4th June 2022

info.text: The area around Bridge Street and central Kingsbridge experienced the majority of the flooding on 4 June 2022; surface water from heavy rainfall overwhelmed highway drains and flooded into properties. The town centre has both fluvial and surface water flood risk, with tide locking and combined system issues making drainage inadequate for a 1-in-10-year event.

ref.title: Kingsbridge 4th June 2022

info.text: Multiple properties within the town were flooded on 4 June 2022 (clustered around Dodbrooke Stream and its culvert). The highway network was affected by surface water, sewer discharges from combined sewers may have occurred (e.g. at Bridge Street and the bus station), and muddy/silty flood waters were conveyed through the town during the event.

ref.title: Kingsbridge 4th June 2022

info.text: Flooding occurred in Kingsbridge on 4 June. Hydraulic modelling predicted the areas that flooded except Manor Park, which flooded from pluvial (surface water) runoff. Flooding happened after high tide; the surface water system had reduced discharge flow for at least 1–2 hours after high tide, which hampered catchment drainage and possibly caused discharges from combined sewer overflows at Bridge Street and the bus station. Ongoing development sites contributed to muddy and silty flood waters being conveyed through the town.

ref.title: Kingsbridge 4th June 2022

info.text: The chapter recommends multiple flood-management actions for Kingsbridge: progress Kingsbridge IUDM flood improvements; consider Property Flood Resilience measures; consider natural flood management in the catchment; sewer network maintenance and potential investment (including storm water separation); ensure highway drains and culverts are maintained; ensure Dodbrook Stream culvert is maintained. These recommendations indicate the town experienced flooding issues prompting these measures.

Surface water/runoff into Lodge Lane and possible ordinary watercourse overtopping occurred around 20:30–21:00, then Axe overtopping around 23:30, with peak Axe conditions at 00:05 and 03:00 on 21 October 2021. At least three properties flooded internally by surface water experienced up to 18 inches (45 cm) of internal flooding. A flood warning for the River Axe was issued at 22:46 but many properties had already flooded from runoff-related impacts.

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

info.text: Site experienced flooding on 24 December 2013. Hydraulic modelling concluded the only viable explanation that matched the observed flood at Gladelands was elevated water levels in the Uddens Water downstream of the A31/Palmersford Roundabout; debris in the Uddens Water was also reported at the time of the event.

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

info.text: Floodwaters entered the Gladelands site after upstream water levels rose due to downstream elevated levels on the Uddens; the 600mm culvert crossing the site and an upstream box culvert were drowned out, allowing floodwater from the Palmersford roundabout and the A31 to inundate land to the west of the site and the site itself.

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

info.text: The Gladelands site lies at a local low point immediately south of the A31; overland surface water flows collect on the site and are trapped by the A31 dual carriageway embankment which effectively forms a dam between the site and the Uddens Water.

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

info.text: The Uddens Water is the major watercourse in the area (Main River). Within the study area it is open channel through woodland and it passes beneath the A31 Palmersford Roundabout via a 6 m wide, 2.5 m high concrete box culvert; it also receives flows from a tributary and from surface water sewers that connect into the river (one connection inside the box culvert beneath the Palmersford Roundabout and another immediately downstream).

ref.title: Gladelands Flood Study: Ferndown

info.text: Water levels in the Uddens rose above bank/above ground, producing overbank/overland flows that entered the Gladelands site from the north‑west and contributed to the flooding; downstream level at the culvert was estimated from photographs.

info.text: The village has a history of flooding caused by heavy rainfall and the local ordinary watercourse. Significant flooding occurred in 2003 and 2012 caused by heavy rainfall leading to surface water, groundwater and fluvial (river) flooding. Additional flood incidents are recorded in 1997, 2000, 2002 and 2013. The catchment is described as having a flashy response to storm rainfall and is spring-fed; groundwater flooding has occurred historically though it was not experienced in the flood event described in this report.

The catchment is described as having a flashy response to storm rainfall and is spring-fed; groundwater flooding has occurred historically though it was not experienced in the flood event described in this report.

Surface water flooding affected five properties from three sources (an ephemeral watercourse originating at Credenhill Park Wood, direct runoff from fields south of the A480, and runoff impacting a low-lying property). A further four properties were flooded from Yazor Brook or its upstream tributaries. Drains/gullies were reported at capacity, with reports of overflowing ditches, blocked culverts/bridges and at least one report of groundwater/spring involvement.

info.text: Exceptionally intense rainfall on 16 September 2016 caused overland surface water flows and secondary surcharging of sewers and highway drainage in and around Bovingdon. Piped drainage was overwhelmed and localised flooding occurred across the investigation area.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: Surface water flooding occurred during the event on 16 September 2016; the incident led to properties in the village being inundated and prompted a Section 19 investigation to identify drainage asset issues and resilience measures.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: Figure 3 and the investigation-area map identify a red‑outlined area in central Bovingdon that coincides with the Environment Agency 'Risk of Flooding from Surface Water' (1-in-100-year) maximum extent and is labelled as including a flooded area. The investigation area runs west–east through central Bovingdon and crosses residential streets (including St. Norbert Road and Green Lane) and is adjacent to community facilities (library, education facility). The contributing surface water catchment directs flows west to east through this area.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: Intense rainfall (approx. 05:00–07:00 on 16 September 2016) caused flash flooding in the village; properties were flooded, Hertfordshire Fire and Rescue attended near the area known as 'Bovingdon Docks', and Thames Water recorded sewer-related flooding to dwellings. HCC sent questionnaires to properties identified as potentially affected.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: The village experienced surface water flooding on 16th September 2016. Most properties rely on private plot-level soakaways and infiltration into the ground is very limited; soakaways are likely in poor condition or inefficient, reducing infiltration capacity. Highway drainage for the affected area drains to local soakaways/boreholes and to a large attenuation/infiltration tank (beneath the private car park between Eastnor and Hamer Close) — these drainage arrangements constrained runoff conveyance and contributed to surface water flooding during the event.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: The highway drainage serving Bovingdon was described as running at or near design capacity and was overwhelmed by the rainfall on 16 September 2016; gullies, soakaways and the local attenuation/infiltration tank were unable to fully contain runoff, and surface water (including overland flow from private property) exceeded the drainage system causing surface-water/urban flooding across the investigation area.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: On 16 September 2016 intense rainfall exceeded the highway drainage capacity in Bovingdon. Highway gullies were unable to drain the large volumes of water and additional overland flow from private land, gardens and driveways overwhelmed the drainage network. Surface water flowed across the highway (notably High Street and Green Lane) and discharged to the Bovingdon Docks open water feature.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: The 16 September 2016 storm produced a large volume of surface water runoff that exceeded highway drainage capacity. Highway drainage from Green Lane and the High Street discharges to Bovingdon Docks (the only local open water feature); defects or silted soakaways would have reduced infiltration/storage and increased surface runoff entering the highway drainage. TWUL received reports during and after the event of foul sewer network surcharging causing foul water to discharge inside and outside properties; residents also raised concerns that a historical pipeline from the airfield may have discharged surface water toward Hamer Close during the event.

ref.title: Hertfordshire County Council Section 19 Flood Investigation Report: Bovingdon

info.text: Observed surface water flooding occurred on and around Hyde Lane during the 16 September 2016 event. Intense rainfall exceeded the urban drainage capacity producing overland flows that drained along the corridor where Hyde Lane lies (heatmap hotspot). Local foul sewers and the main sewer line in the area were partially involved through surcharge or infiltration of surface water, which limited the ability of gullies and highway drainage to remove water. The Bovingdon Docks serving the highway drainage were full and overflowing, reducing discharge capacity and contributing to flooding impacts in this location.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Deal

info.text: Intense afternoon rainfall caused the sewer network to surcharge; manholes along Albert Road surcharged and sewage and surface water ponded and accumulated. The road flooded from the junction with Middle Deal Road to the railway. Internal flooding was reported by properties; some properties experienced external flooding where sandbags or flood boards prevented internal ingress. Southern Water did not initiate their emergency response and the road was not initially closed; vehicles drove through the floodwater creating bow waves that threatened internal flooding. KCC highways and the police later implemented a road closure and KCC provided a tanker to clear flood water.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Snodland

info.text: Intense rainfall produced significant overland flows that drained towards culverted watercourses and collected in topographical lows. ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Flooding Affecting the Tunbridge Wells Area on 19 July 2017

info.text: Surface water from surrounding hills and roads converged in the central area (The Pantiles / Nevill Street / Warwick Park low point ~80.3mAOD). Converging flow routes and limited ability for water to flow away, combined with a small local pump serving basements, increased loads on drainage and the pump and led to surface water and sewer-related flooding in the central area, including flooding of basements and water on highways during the 19 July 2017 event.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Flooding Affecting the Tunbridge Wells Area on 19 July 2017

info.text: On 19th July 2017 excessive/intensive rainfall exceeded the capacity of the town's drainage and combined sewer systems. Surface water accumulated in topographic low points and entered properties; parts of the town (including London Road, Castle Street and the Royal Victoria Place area) experienced overwhelmed gullies/combined sewers and blocked drains. Kent County Council attended (water had cleared from some highways by 03:54) and drains were cleansed and audited following the event.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Flooding Affecting the Tunbridge Wells Area on 19 July 2017

info.text: Following the 19 July 2017 flood event, KCC undertook drainage cleansing on roads in Tunbridge Wells that were affected by flooding; a resident flood action group was formed (facilitated by the National Flood Forum) to address local flood issues; natural flood management measures were delivered in local green spaces (Hilbert Woods and Grosvenor Park) to reduce peak flows.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Flooding Affecting the Tunbridge Wells Area On 24th August 2015

info.text: Surface water flooding during the 24 August 2015 event with highway gullies on the western side of Nevill Street (adjacent to the Pantiles) found during clean-up to contain some tarmac in their sumps; these deposits were not significant and did not block outlet pipes. A nearby manhole showed a build-up of silt at an access to a non-return valve but this was not causing a blockage; CCTV showed the non-return valve to be in full working order. Damaged pipework near Warwick Park (close to Nevill Street) from utility works was noted and may have contributed to higher surface water flows towards low points on Nevill Street. Small amounts of solid debris were recovered during maintenance/clean-up.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Capel-Le-Ferne

info.text: A flood incident occurred in Capel-le-Ferne overnight linked to intense local rainfall. The incident took place between 23:00 on 04 November 2023 and 00:45 on 05 November 2023, coinciding with heavy short-duration rainfall and preceded by high antecedent rainfall in the previous days.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Capel-Le-Ferne

info.text: Intense, antecedent rainfall produced large runoff from surrounding agricultural land which flowed southeast into the village. ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Capel-Le-Ferne

info.text: Surface water runoff from saturated agricultural fields accumulated in a local topographic depression between the junction of Capel Street and Lancaster Avenue and the junction of Lancaster Avenue and Elizabeth Drive. The highway drainage system was overwhelmed and obstructed, resulting in flooding of the carriageway and at least six properties (five of which flooded internally). KCC Highways attended the incident and carried out inspection and jetting of road gullies and mainlines on 09 November 2023. Kent Fire Rescue Service attended with vehicles and pumped floodwater out of affected properties and gardens into the highway drainage network.

The map notes the estimated extent covers roads only and does not mark properties as flooded.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Capel-Le-Ferne

info.text: The primary flood source in the village is surface water (overland flow). Natural surface water overland flow paths are described: one flowing west–east from Great Cauldham Farm across an agricultural field to the junction at Capel Street and Lancaster Avenue, and a larger path flowing from Dawkinge Wood towards that junction and then towards Dover. Soils with impeded drainage lead to increased runoff. Two drainage ditches were removed/infilling following the 2007 flood event, affecting local drainage.

info.text: The River Wharfe has a long history of causing destructive river flooding: in 1673 it reached unprecedented levels damaging and overturning bridges (including Otley Bridge) and destroying other bridges; on 16 Feb 1935 fifty houses near the bridge were marooned; severe events occurred in December 1936 and January 1982 when the river reached the bridge arches. info.text: Local ditched watercourses had fallen into disrepair, which prevented proper drainage and obstructed highway drainage outfalls. Under heavy rainfall the road flooded and a local house flooded on a number of occasions directly from the road. The ditched watercourses were subsequently cleared and there have been no repeat reports of flooding to homes since the works were completed.

ref.title: November 2020 Flooding In Lancashire

info.text: Flooding of a house and road at Warpers Moss Lane caused by an obstructed culvert and capacity constraints / obstructions in local ditched watercourses; connected highway drainage systems failed to function as historically expected. Culvert and highway drainage were cleaned and jetted earlier in the year; remaining risk was addressed when excess silt and vegetation were cleared from the private land watercourses.

ref.title: November 2020 Flooding In Lancashire

info.text: Surface water drainage on the public highway was overwhelmed and failed to discharge because downstream ditched watercourses were obstructed by silt and vegetation, causing floodwater to back up into the highway and into at least one home. Repeated reports of flooding were recorded in 2019 and 2020; a resident reported his home flooded on 24 November 2020 and that this had occurred on three separate occasions. The council identified three obstructed ditched watercourses, notified landowners, and remedial works were completed with no further reports of home flooding after clearance.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report of the Flood Event Thursday 22nd June 2023 (South and East Leicester City)

info.text: Properties across a large area of the city were recorded as flooded during the storm covered by this report.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report of the Flood Event Thursday 22nd June 2023 (South and East Leicester City)

info.text: On 22 June 2023 intense rainfall caused many sewers to surcharge in the south and east of the city. Evidence included displaced manhole/inspection covers. The event caused rapid overland flow to low areas, overwhelmed highway gullies and outfalls, and resulted in damage to roads, paving and significant damage to highway surfacing.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report of the Flood Event Thursday 22nd June 2023 (South and East Leicester City)

info.text: Widespread surface water and sewer surcharging across the city (particularly south and east) caused displaced manhole/inspection covers, roads and paving damage, flooded roads, and internal property flooding. Overland flows moved rapidly to low areas; emergency response and highway repairs were required.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Unprecedented flooding across the Leeds district (25–29 December 2015) had devastating consequences for residents, businesses and communities; some homeowners/tenants remained unable to return while repair works continued, and the flooding had a major impact on businesses and jobs with some businesses moving operations out of the area and out of the UK.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Widespread flooding across the district during the event causing significant disruption to residents, businesses and communities; major transport links and critical infrastructure were flooded or disrupted (including A65 Kirkstall Road, Linton Bridge, Network Rail lines at Kirkstall, Northern Power Grid substations and IT/data centres).

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Leeds city (located on the River Aire and affected by the River Calder and tributaries) experienced river and urban flooding during Storm Eva; Leeds city centre and neighbouring areas were particularly vulnerable and suffered severe impacts including inundation of communities and disruption to transport and key sites. High-rise and multi-occupancy buildings in the city suffered indirect impacts (stranded cars in basements, disabled lifts, power outages) that caused severe inconvenience and loss to residents and businesses.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Widespread flooding across the metropolitan district: 4,712 reported flooding incidents (internal and external), including 2,826 affected by internal flooding; property damage to homes and businesses, some buildings left empty or undergoing remediation; indirect impacts to high-rise/multiple-occupancy buildings (e.g. cars stranded in basement car parks, lifts incapacitated, power outages); businesses ruined and many homeowners displaced into temporary accommodation.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Floodwaters from the river overtopped and ran through central Leeds: a building in School Close was struck and demolished; an empty barge was swept from Howard's wharf and was broken to pieces and sank after striking another coal-barge which became fixed against the abutments of Leeds Bridge; a landing stage at Leeds Bridge was washed away the following morning, throwing people into the flood; floodwater ran down Swinegate into the mills (lower flat completely flooded); floodwater entered Meadow Lane and Water Lane (penetrating as far as Mr Green's machine works), reached from Water Hall to Marshall Street in Holbeck, covered Meadow Lane to Christ's Church, rendered Dock Street impassable, and extended along Hunslet Lane to the Theatre Royal; Timble Beck flooded Marsh Lane and the bottom of Kirkgate, rising to Church Lane and Mill Street in Marsh Lane; extensive damage to shop property in the neighbourhood and cellar dwellings in Duke Street were completely flooded; residents in low-lying dwellings in East Street were removed to safety; the lower part of the Parish Church burial ground was inundated; roads and fields near Sheepscar Bar, Knostrop and Thorpe Hall Pastures were covered with several feet of water; an empty barge and another barge were driven into and obstructed arches at Leeds Bridge causing accelerated currents and further local damage and wash-away of structures.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: River flooding associated with Storm Eva in late December 2015 affected the city, prompting immediate recovery activity and the commissioning of a catchment‑wide feasibility study (River Aire Flood Alleviation Scheme). Flood impacts required infrastructure repairs (for example Linton Bridge) and targeted communications to affected businesses and residents.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Experienced flooding during Storm Eva that affected residents and businesses, prompted community engagement and recovery actions, and led to infrastructure impacts such as repairs and alternative travel arrangements around Linton Bridge.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Storm Eva flooding in Leeds on 26 December 2015 flooded industrial/office premises occupied by businesses (example: Company A). Three of four industrial/office units were flooded, leading to loss of two months' production and significant damage to essential production machinery, work in progress and business stock. The business submitted a multi‑million pound insurance claim and faced a large increase in future flood insurance costs (reported as a 460% premium increase), prompting consideration of relocation out of the floodplain.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Internally flooded properties located in/near Leeds as part of the February 2022 event; properties shown on the report map as part of the 15 internally flooded properties across the Nidd, Wharfe and Aire catchments.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report into the flooding in February 2022

info.text: The district has a long history of main river (fluvial) flooding from the River Aire, River Wharfe, River Calder and tributaries; flooding events affect residential and business properties and city-wide infrastructure. The city centre is identified as being at significant risk from the River Aire. During Storm Eva the district experienced numerous concentrated incidents, particularly adjacent to main rivers and in the central corridor.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: During Storm Eva (25–29 Dec 2016) flooding was concentrated along the River Aire corridor in Leeds, with the highest density of incidents around Newlay and Rodley. Floodwaters overtopping the river and overland flow routes contributed to property flooding in these neighbourhoods; photos (Figures 44–47) show residential internal flood depths in Newlay of 800 mm to 1100 mm.

ref.title: Leeds Strategic Flood Investigation Report: Storm Eva Flood Event, 25-29 Dec 2015

info.text: Monitoring at Allerton Ings (Leeds) showed elevated water depths through February associated with Storm Ciara and subsequent storms; levels did not return to pre-storm values by the end of the month, indicating prolonged high water in the washlands.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: February 2020

info.text: Elevated river levels and repeated high-stage peaks in Leeds resulted in Knostrop and Crown Point weirs being lowered and sustained high flows through the middle and lower Aire. Multiple consecutive peaks at Knostrop left washlands fuller for longer and contributed to sustained elevated water levels downstream; gauge data and anecdotal reports noted a ‘surge’ in levels in the channel and West Bank Pond. Significant peak stages were recorded on gauges in and around Leeds and on downstream reaches of the Aire and Ouse during February 2020.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: February 2020

info.text: Elevated river levels passed through Leeds on multiple occasions in February 2020; the Leeds Flood Alleviation Scheme (weirs) were actively operated to manage levels (weirs were lowered once on 24 Feb 2020 at 16:00). The scheme reduces the floodplain through the centre of Leeds, affecting upstream levels while increasing flows downstream toward Lemonroyd weir.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: February 2020

info.text: Flood peaks passed through the city on the dates listed, indicating river flooding affected Leeds during the February 2020 events.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: February 2020

info.text: Flood peaks passed through Leeds on 9, 16, 22, 23 and 24 February 2020. The Leeds flood alleviation scheme weirs were operated during the period and were lowered on 24 February 2020 at 16:00.
