info.text: Lower Caversham has experienced rising River Thames water levels such that artificially raised ground has been created to provide informal protection from those rising levels. The area is identified as being close to the main watercourse and thus at risk of property flooding if river/channel capacity is exceeded.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Modelled flood extents show that substantial parts of Lower Caversham lie within the mapped floodplain up to the 1 in 1000 year event (pink), with nested 1 in 20 to 1 in 100 year extents closer to the river. The mapping indicates that adjacent urban areas and infrastructure in Lower Caversham are within modelled river-flood inundation zones.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Residents reported flooding of basement areas that may be indicative of groundwater flooding through river gravels; this flooding occurred concurrently with the January 2024 event, though the direct contribution of groundwater is uncertain.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Mapped flood extents show inundation of low-lying areas adjacent to the river in Lower Caversham during the January 2024 event; public consultation was held for affected residents indicating the area experienced flood impacts.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Rapid onset flooding in January 2024 gave residents little time to prepare. Surface water drainage capacity was exceeded in parts of the area. Sandbags were provided on 7 January 2024 which helped prevent water entering the front of properties but were too late to prevent flooding of gardens and outbuildings that had already begun. Late or no flood warnings were reported by some residents.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Residential properties at the eastern end of Queens Road experienced exterior and basement flooding from late evening 5 Jan; internal ground-floor flooding of several properties occurred on 7 Jan. Basement water levels fully receded by 15 Jan (total flood duration 10 days). Flooding arose from exceedance of Christchurch Ditch capacity and culvert blockages by debris, with floodwater flowing via gardens, footpaths and roads into Queens Road and then to Mill Road, Coldicutt Street, Champion Road, Piggott's Road and Mill Green. Sandbags provided on 7 Jan reduced front-of-property inundation but were too late to prevent gardens/outbuildings already flooding. A raised bund to the south of Christchurch Ditch slowed drainage back to the Thames, prolonging inundation. A boat stuck on Caversham weir downstream of Heron Island was reported and may have impeded flows during the event.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Floodwater from Christchurch Ditch and the River Thames entered the area via residential gardens, footpaths and roads causing internal and external flooding. Basements and ground floors were flooded; front gardens and outbuildings were also inundated. Stantec modelling and a resident sketch show converging flow paths across Lower Caversham during the event. Basement water levels had fully receded by 15 Jan (total reported flood duration of ~10 days).

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Area was included within the scope of River Thames flood alerts and reviews following the January 2024 River Thames flood event affecting Reading borough.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Floodwaters, including flow from Christchurch Ditch northwards, affected Lower Caversham; RBC cleared debris and blockages in ditches within this area as part of the response.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Lower Caversham received floodwater flowing northwards from Christchurch Ditch, resulting in inundation of the low-lying area and impacts to nearby properties as reported by residents.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Surface water flooding affected roads and pavements in Lower Caversham (notably Queens Road at the entrance opposite Coldicutt Street), impeding vehicular and pedestrian movement in the residential area.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Residential streets in the area were inundated: roads and pavements (notably Queens Road and the Queens Road/Mill Road junction) were submerged, front gardens were reached by floodwater and routes were rendered impassable for pedestrians and vehicles.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Residential streets in Lower Caversham (including Queens Road and Mill Green) experienced flooding. Inundation extended into Caversham Meadow and Christchurch Ditch (photo from Reading Bridge documents extent), impacting roads, pavements, parked vehicles and local access.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Modelled 1-in-30-year flood flow paths and present-day modelled 1-in-20 to 1-in-1000 year extents indicate predicted inundation across central and southern Lower Caversham, with flow converging from northwest, west and northeast and multiple flow paths affecting a broad area; community infrastructure (schools, churches) is shown within the modelled flood zone.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: The side-channel/pond area where Christchurch Ditch outfalls at Heron Island was reported as choked with trees and vegetation and the nearby marina had silt build-up, reducing capacity to receive and convey floodwater during the January 2024 event.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Public footpath adjacent to residential properties at Heron Island bordered the cleared section of Christchurch Ditch; outfall structure at Heron Island is overgrown and the closed culvert outfall cannot currently be viewed, indicating obstruction issues addressed as part of post‑flood works.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: The Christchurch Ditch outfall at Heron Island was overgrown and could not be inspected as part of post‑flood investigations; included in recommended CCTV survey and repair actions following the January 2024 flood.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: The outfall location at Heron Island was blocked by thick vegetation, preventing access to the ditch outfall during the flood investigation on 7 Jan 2024 and likely hindering inspection or maintenance actions during the flood period.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: A closed section of culvert at Heron Island and accumulation of excessive woody debris along the channel leading to the culvert entry were observed; these obstructions contributed to restricted flow and localised flooding issues.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Exterior and basement flooding began late evening 5 January; internal ground-floor flooding of several properties occurred on 7 January. Floodwaters flowed via residential gardens, public footpaths and roads into Queens Road and then extended to adjacent streets. Basement water levels had fully receded by 15 January, giving a total flood duration of 10 days.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Properties at the eastern end experienced exterior and basement flooding beginning late evening 5 Jan, with internal ground-floor flooding of multiple properties on 7 Jan. Floodwater reached fronts of properties due to exceedance of surface water drainage causing street pooling. Sandbags and airbrick covers were provided by RBC on 7 Jan to mitigate rising water. Residents reported basement flooding potentially linked to rising groundwater through river gravels; basements receded by 15 Jan.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Local surface water drainage network in Queens Road was checked and cleared by the RBC Highways Team as a post‑flood intervention to restore drainage capacity following the flood event.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: A Queen's Road resident reported observed flow of floodwater from Christchurch Ditch northwards into Lower Caversham. The resident recorded water levels in and around their property and provided a timeline of flooding that affected their property and adjacent properties between 5th and 15th January 2024.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Back gardens and access paths flooded by overflow from Christchurch Ditch; basement flooding in multiple properties (rising to and above ground-floor level in some cases), outbuildings flooded to skirting/damp-course level, water reached front doors and flooded cycle path and pavements. Electrical issues/partial loss of electricity at some properties; residents required pumping and bailing; sandbags provided by council; fire brigade attended and advised turning off ground-floor electricity.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Back gardens and access paths filled and continued to rise; water from gardens and a nearby apartment block car park flooded the cycle path and overflowed into Queen's Road gardens; cycle path and pavements flooded, water flowed across fronts of houses at the eastern end, reached front doors and flooded beyond parking bay lines; footpaths behind Queen's Road filled from Ditch overflow; an outbuilding was surrounded and flooded up to below its damp course; water rose to the gate level of one property; one property experienced a partial loss of electricity; basement level conditions reported for one property.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Basements and gardens at the eastern end flooded: water from an apartment block car park overflowed into a Queens Road garden and gardens filled rapidly. Multiple basements experienced rising floodwater (including one basement reaching ground floor level), kitchens began to flood, residents used bailing and pumping to try to mitigate levels, RBC placed sandbags at the front of houses and airbrick covers were applied, outbuilding flooded up to seat level, back gardens flooded to approximately 1m from the houses, and Fire Brigade attended and advised isolating ground-floor electricity.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Floodwater at the eastern end of Queens Road flooded in front of properties. Basement flood levels rose then began to drop; clearance under ground floor later recorded at approximately 1 cm. Front-of-property water reached the gutter; back garden floodwater came within about 3 m of houses. Garden areas were passable with wellies as levels receded.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Floodwater overflowed onto the road and pavement at the entrance to Queens Road (opposite Coldicutt Street), partially submerging the carriageway and making passage difficult or impossible for vehicles and pedestrians.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Pavement and part of the carriageway were flooded, blocking pedestrian access and partially encroaching onto the road. The flooding made the street impassable for pedestrians and reduced vehicle access; water was observed reflecting houses and reaching close to property entrances.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Commercial properties experienced internal flooding (basement and/or ground floor). At least one commercial property experienced external flooding.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Floodwater flowed northwards/eastwards as recorded by residents into Mill Green and adjacent roads as part of the Christchurch Ditch overflow pathway, causing inundation of public roads and nearby areas.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Significant flooding to residential gardens and/or outbuildings was reported.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Road surface and parked vehicles were inundated; water covered much of the street, partially submerging parked vans and restricting vehicle and pedestrian access.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Residential properties flooded at the south end of Circuit Lane and Sylvan Walk, reported in the Southcote / Holy Brook – River Kennet flood investigation section.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Backflow of water from the River Kennet floodplain and exceedance of local ditch/channel capacity (including culverted and open channels in Linear Park) caused floodwater to flow northwards under the railway towards residential areas. Blocked ditches (woody debris) and a blocked/partially collapsed culvert reduced conveyance, contributing to internal flooding of houses on Circuit Lane and Sylvan Walk.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Debris build-up was observed north of the railway bridge (Briscoe's Bridge) in Southcote on 05 Jan 2024; debris and bridge/culvert issues impeded flow and contributed to localised flooding risk.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Areas in Southcote experienced flooding: debris and water accumulation north of Briscoe's Bridge (river overbank flow from the River Kennet floodplain) and surface water flooding at the southern end of Circuit Lane making the lane impassable.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Damage to post-2014 bank works and path repairs near Holybrook overbridge was reported; a muddy, partially flooded path with standing water leading to a brick-arch underpass was photographed.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Local flooding eroded a repaired river bank and damaged an adjacent footpath near Holybrook Overbridge; damage was recorded by a resident and photographed.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: An allotment site south of Brunel Road was flooded: standing water covered plots and adjacent areas, with sheds and greenhouses partially submerged. Flooding was concentrated on the northern and western plots and inundated paths within the site.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Photograph and caption show a temporary bund under Briscoe's Bridge holding back water from the floodplain, demonstrating that floodwater reached the floodplain and was being retained by the bund to prevent further encroachment onto adjacent land.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Properties closest to the River Kennet at Southcote were subject to a flood warning in force 02/01/2024 - 11/01/2024, indicating threat from river flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Present-day modelled flood maps for Southcote show extensive flood extents across the neighbourhood for a range of return periods (1 in 20 to 1 in 1000 years). A separate climate-change 1 in 100 year scenario (with allowances of 25–70%) increases the mapped extents, bringing additional residential areas, schools and roads into the flood footprint.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Flooding at the allotment site south of Brunel Road, impacting allotment holders and preventing access to plots.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Damage to banks and footpaths on the River Kennet in Katesgrove was reported following the flood event.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Metal path under Reading Bridge flooded as river levels rose, indicating inundation of riverside infrastructure and contributing to wider path/park flooding along the river bank.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Southcote Lane is depicted within the Southcote modelled flood extents and flow-path mapping (1-in-30-year), with flow arrows across the lane indicating predicted inundation and routing of floodwater along this corridor.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Shown on the Southcote flood flow direction modelling where the 1-in-30-year extent (light blue) covers the largest area; the model indicates flow across Southcote generally from southwest to northeast and identifies flow paths and extents that include streets such as Hatford Road, indicating predicted inundation or flow across that corridor.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Hatford Road lies within the mapped area and is shown as within or adjacent to modelled flood extents (1 in 20 to 1 in 1000 year), indicating potential inundation risk to the road and nearby properties/school grounds in those scenarios.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Tallis Lane is inside the map bounding box and falls within or next to the modelled flood extents for the 1 in 20 to 1 in 1000 year events, meaning the lane and adjacent properties are shown at risk in the modelling.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: The Avon Canal has sluice gates that can be opened to release water into the surrounding floodplain when water levels are high. In the context of the January 2024 rainfall and Storm Henk, the canal and its control structures represent a pathway by which high water levels can transfer water to floodplain areas, contributing to floodplain inundation when river channels exceed capacity.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: A section designated as part of the Kennet and Avon Canal (within Katesgrove) suffered bank and footpath damage during the flood event; responsibility for maintenance lies with the CRT.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: The Kennet and Avon Canal exceeded its capacity and overtopped; high canal water levels flowed south from the canal into the developed area at Burghfield Bridge when the north bank overtopped.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: During the 2024 flood event the Kennet and Avon Canal overtopped its south bank and flowed south into the developed area of Burghfield Bridge. The south banks were noted as being significantly weakened in places from mooring canal boats and lack of management, and there was concern that canal boats could break loose and block flow downstream under Burghfield Road bridge.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Unstable banks along the Kennet and Avon Canal (particularly the south bank) were highlighted, likely from erosion by mooring boats; the condition reduces canal capacity and risks overtopping during high flows, prompting recommendations for remedial works and bank strengthening to prevent further overtopping.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Kennet and Avon Canal is described as a fluvial source and as a barrier to floodwater escape; it contributed to the flooding and trapping of water at Pingewood during early 2024 when lakes overtopped.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Kennet and Avon Canal contributed to fluvial flooding in the area (noted as part of the flood sources affecting Sheffield Bottom) and its overflow/overtopping was linked to local inundation during the January 2024 event.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: During high flows a large volume of flows passed below Station Road and the Canal/canal infrastructure was used to move floodwaters away from Sheffield Bottom (hatches opened by the Canal and River Trust to allow canal flow to move floodwater).

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Locks along the Kennet and Avon Canal were operated in response to high flows; residents consider lock operation (or closure) may have influenced downstream flow and contributed to flooding in Sheffield Bottom during January 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The island between the River Kennet and the Kennet and Avon Canal is believed to have had additional properties affected by flooding, though the flood extent and specific impacts are not reported.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Kennet and Avon Canal (adjacent to the River Kennet) is part of the flooding scenario affecting the island between the two watercourses; a flood alleviation scheme is recommended to reduce risk to the island and nearby properties.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Kennet and Avon Canal overtopped its banks on occasions across January and February 2024 (after Storms Henk, Isha and Jocelyn), causing water to flow south through the car park and pub grounds, through a culvert under Burghfield Road and onto Pingewood Road North and Green Lane, contributing to residential flooding and access issues.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Kennet and Avon Canal exceeded its capacity and overtopped; high canal water levels flowed south from the canal into the developed area at Burghfield Bridge when the north bank overtopped.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Floodwaters extended northwards/eastwards along the resident-described pathway and reached Champion Road, contributing to local flooding in the area.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Culverted and open channels within Linear Park (on land owned by RBC) were implicated in the flooding: a ditch immediately south of Circuit Lane was blocked by woody debris and a culvert at the northern end was found blocked by sheet piling/partially collapsed, significantly reducing flows and contributing to local backflow and property flooding.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Flooding at the junction with Scours Lane extended across the carriageway and pavement, blocking access under the nearby railway bridge and preventing passage.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Localized surface water flooding affected the Scours Lane / Stadium Way junction within Tilehurst, making the junction impassable and impacting local transport access.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: The school site is overlaid by the modelled Southcote flood extents/flow paths (1-in-30-year), with flow arrows passing through the area. The modelling predicts inundation of the school grounds and potential flooding of access routes and the site during the modelled event.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Ashampstead Road (and adjacent allotments shown on the map) lie within the Southcote modelled flood extents and flow-path mapping (1-in-30-year), indicating predicted inundation and flow of surface water across this road corridor.

ref.title: Reading Flood Investigation - January 2024 Flood Investigation Report: Appendix 2

info.text: Flooding from the Kennet and its tributaries (including the Holybrook) caused internal flooding of homes in Pingewood over a period of days.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Listed as a location under investigation following the January 2024 storms; the report links these investigations to flooding that led to internal and external property flooding and road closures.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Following Storms Henk, Isha and Jocelyn, 4 properties in Pingewood were reported flooded: 1 property internally flooded and 3 properties externally flooded. Road closures reported: 2.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Pingewood, a topographic low with interconnected fishing lakes and ditches, was inundated when fluvial flows from the River Kennet and Kennet and Avon Canal and overtopping of the lakes to the north caused floodwater to be trapped (barriers such as the canal, railway and M4 prevented escape), resulting in flooding in early 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Fluvial (river) flooding in early January 2024 affected areas of Pingewood (areas in Flood Zone 2 and 3). Internal fluvial flooding affected one residential property on Kirtons Farm Road; external fluvial flooding affected another residential property on Kirtons Farm Road and an angling club. The Cottage Lane Ditch backed up and overtopped, sending water along Cottage Lane into Kirtons Farm Road and down to Berrys Lane; water then flowed into Pingewood Lagoon and Englefield Lagoon via grips. A SSE substation on Cottage Lane was reported to have flooded but not to a degree that caused loss of power. Flooding began in early January following Storm Henk and continued for approximately one month.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Blocked/partially blocked culverts beneath the Reading–Basingstoke railway and dense ditch vegetation caused flows to back up into the northern lakes and southwards; backed-up flows and a partly blocked southern culvert caused flooding of Cottage Lane and surrounding low-lying areas in early 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Blocked culverts and restricted flows caused water to back up into the northern lakes and altered flow patterns through Pingewood, increasing local flood risk and contributing to downstream flooding (notably affecting Cottage Lane).

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Local flooding issues were associated with blocked/poorly maintained drainage (including a blocked northern railway culvert and silted downstream ditch). The situation prompted recommendations to investigate clearing the culvert and to confirm and enforce ditch/culvert maintenance to improve conveyance and reduce flood risk upstream and downstream.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Fluvial flooding occurred in areas mapped as Flood Zone 2 and Flood Zone 3. Four properties were flooded (one internally and three externally). Flooding led to road closures at Kirtons Farm Road and Berrys Lane. The flooding is reported as resulting from Storms Henk, Isha and Jocelyn.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The locality of Pingewood lies within the mapped site boundary; the map shows floodwater entering from the north, flowing southward, and converging in central/southern parts of the site, placing Pingewood within the identified zone at risk and on predicted flood routes. Blocked culverts are noted as likely contributors to increased inflow.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding affected the village from groundwater and fluvial sources. During winter 2013/14 approximately 18 properties were flooded internally and approximately four properties were flooded externally across the entirety of Burghfield. Similar sources (groundwater and fluvial from the River Kennet and Kennet and Avon Canal) contributed to flooding again in early 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Early-2024 flooding in Burghfield Bridge was caused by high groundwater and fluvial overtopping of the Kennet and Avon Canal. Floodwater flowed from the canal south through the Cunning Man pub car park, through a culvert under Burghfield Road onto the first 50 yards of Pingewood Road North and down Green Lane, affecting residential properties. Groundwater emerged across the residential area and had to be pumped south to lower derelict land. Internal flooding affected properties (residential and commercial). High groundwater filled septic tanks causing loss of ability to use showers, toilets and washing machines in some properties; raw sewage emergence from septic fields was also reported. Flooding impeded road access (cars broke down on Pingewood Road North) creating access issues for emergency vehicles. Floodwaters took a long time to subside.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Environment Agency received 10 reports of flooding across Burghfield during the 2024 flood event: two properties reported internal flooding and seven properties reported external flooding. Six of the affected properties were located in Burghfield Bridge.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Subject of site visits following the January 2024 flood event; guidance issued for riparian owners (within Burghfield Bridge) to maintain ditches to allow free passage of water during flood events, indicating local flooding and watercourse/ditch impacts.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Low-lying areas of Burghfield were inundated by fluvial flooding during the early 2024 event. Flooding was driven by the River Kennet and Kennet and Avon Canal overtopping and by the overtopping of nearby lakes, causing water to pond in the settlement's low-lying areas.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Reported flooding across the area during the January 2024 event; two properties reported internal flooding and seven properties reported external flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Two roads in Burghfield (Reading Road and Padworth Road) were closed due to flooding on 5th January 2024; both reopened 8th January 2024.

info.text: Properties closest to the River Kennet at Burghfield were subject to a flood warning in force 02/01/2024 - 11/01/2024, indicating threat from river flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding occurred in Burghfield associated with Storm Henk (02/01/2024), Storm Isha (21/01/2024–22/01/2024), and Storm Jocelyn (23/01/2024–24/01/2024); the event is the subject of a Section 19 flood investigation.

info.text: Area (specifically Burghfield Bridge / Eastbury) affected by wet-weather issues: assets impacted by groundwater infiltration and, in some locations, rivers overtopping/bursting banks. Thames Water is undertaking investigations; no assets are reported as broken or requiring repair at present.

info.text: Flooding occurred in Burghfield (the investigation specifically references the Burghfield Bridge area). The location was included in a Section 19 flood investigation into flooding that occurred in January 2024 and Thames Water was asked to provide details of actions taken in response.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding affected the village from groundwater and fluvial sources. During winter 2013/14 approximately 18 properties were flooded internally and approximately four properties were flooded externally across the entirety of Burghfield. Similar sources (groundwater and fluvial from the River Kennet and Kennet and Avon Canal) contributed to flooding again in early 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Early-2024 flooding in Burghfield Bridge was caused by high groundwater and fluvial overtopping of the Kennet and Avon Canal. Floodwater flowed from the canal south through the Cunning Man pub car park, through a culvert under Burghfield Road onto the first 50 yards of Pingewood Road North and down Green Lane, affecting residential properties. Groundwater emerged across the residential area and had to be pumped south to lower derelict land. Internal flooding affected properties (residential and commercial). High groundwater filled septic tanks causing loss of ability to use showers, toilets and washing machines in some properties; raw sewage emergence from septic fields was also reported. Flooding impeded road access (cars broke down on Pingewood Road North) creating access issues for emergency vehicles. Floodwaters took a long time to subside.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Fluvial flooding from the River Kennet and the Kennet and Avon Canal, together with overtopping of lakes to the west of Sheffield Bottom, led to flooding across Burghfield. The report notes a similar pattern of flooding in the January 2024 event and records that in winter 2013/14 approximately 18 properties were flooded internally and approximately four properties were flooded externally across Burghfield.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Modelled opening (non‑operational) of the Meadowgate Regulator during a 1% AEP produced a pronounced, central inundation basin within the Meadowgate area. The deepest water is concentrated in a central, roughly triangular zone, with shallower flood depths radiating into adjacent low‑lying residential and commercial areas. Two smaller, isolated flooded areas are present to the north and northwest.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Opening of the Meadowgate regulator (MRO scenario) is modelled to increase flood extent and depths across the central and southern parts of the mapped area. New areas become inundated in the southern part (modelled 'Was Dry Now Wet' zones). Depth increases are concentrated in the 0.01–0.50 m range across the largest areas, with small pockets showing increases greater than 1.00 m.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The Meadowgate regulator was not operational and its river level was not recorded during the 19–21 Oct 2023 event (it was under refurbishment). Its non-operation meant no flows were held back at Meadowgate during the event, which contributed to lower river levels recorded at Killamarsh compared with 2007 and 2019.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Was not operational during Storm Babet because it was undergoing refurbishment; therefore it could not perform its flood water storage function for the four lakes (Meadowgate Lake, Nethermore Lake, Rother Valley Lake and Northern Lake) that together provide up to 1,500,000m3 of storage.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Was not operational during Storm Babet (19 Oct 2023 - 21 Oct 2023) because it was being refurbished, so its flow-diversion function into wetlands was unavailable during the event. The gate type was changed from a 'fish belly' gate to a 'guillotine' gate during the refurbishment but its operating method did not change. The Environment Agency normally manages stored water and releases it gradually to avoid creating additional flood risk.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Used as the flow‑regulation point to divert high flows from the River Rother into wetlands during the Storm Babet event (19–21 Oct 2023) to reduce peak flows and avoid coincident peaks with the River Don. The Environment Agency managed stored water and released flows gradually through the regulator to avoid creating additional flood risk; operation has implications for relative protection of upstream versus downstream communities.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The Meadowgate Regulator was not operational during Storm Babet; modelling comparing operational vs non‑operational scenarios shows that when not operational there were slight increases in flood depths and extents in Catcliffe and Treeton for some AEPs (but no additional properties affected in those scenarios). During the event river flows lay between the 1% and 0.5% AEP.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: Meadowgate Regulator was out of operation from the start of the refurbishment works (beginning of September) and remained non-operational during Storm Babet; modelling with the gate out of operation showed slight increases in flood depths and extents in nearby settlements for some AEP scenarios. The regulator being unavailable during the storm delayed installation works and removed its control function for the event.

ref.title: Overview of the October 2023 Storm Babet Flooding Event and Response

info.text: The Meadowgate regulator was out of operation during the event; its non‑operational state changed flood extents and depths in modelling for a 1% AEP event. Contingency arrangements required the other two regulators (Canklow and Woodhouse Mill) to be operated. Maps show different flood extents/depths when Meadowgate is operational versus non‑operational, indicating the regulator’s status materially affected flooding in the area.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Bury Road, Lawshall

info.text: Deep surface water (>0.3 m) occurred in two locations on Bury Road. At the junction of Bury Road/Lawshall Row up to Windsor Close (referred to as Bury Rd South) five properties were severely affected (including sewer flooding at Bury Rd South). On the northern section of Bury Road (Bury Rd North) over a 20 m length two properties were severely affected.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Bury Road, Lawshall

info.text: Sewer surcharge and overloaded drainage caused surface water and sewer flooding along Bury Road. Two manhole covers were lifted by surcharge pressure. Gullies (three) at Bury Road North are prone to overloading during intense storms; approximately 500m of Bury Road has no road drainage, contributing to ponding and flow towards the low point. At Bury Road South the pumping station and sewer were overloaded, contributing to internal flooding of houses. Reduced capacity of the main drainage channel (a 25m length of 225mm culvert) caused throttling of flows.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Bury Road, Lawshall

info.text: Properties on Bury Rd South were internally flooded; road drainage and kerb heights at dropped kerbs in front of doors contributed to water entry. Recommendations include reinstating kerb heights, improving grips and gullies, clearing adjacent watercourse and upgrading pumping station to reduce future flooding.

info.text: Surface water drainage capacity was exceeded by an intense storm on 17th June 2020. The on-site highway drainage (gullies, laterals, elephant chambers and soakaway) was found completely blocked and poorly maintained, contributing to the flood impact.

ref.title: Compiegne Way, Bury St Edmunds

info.text: Repeated flooding of the highway during winter/early spring. February 2024 event caused the road to be closed for 12–24 hours. Pumps were replaced; road surface damage repaired; repairs were delayed by continuous inflow of water from an unknown source. When river levels were high the sump-and-pump drainage outfall could not discharge, contributing to accumulation. Flooding has limited access to the British Sugar factory and prevented access to Bury St Edmunds from the north-east, stranded vehicles, and generated insurance claims.

ref.title: Compiegne Way, Bury St Edmunds

info.text: Low-lying section of the highway accumulates surface water after heavy/prolonged rainfall (pluvial flooding). Road drainage collects runoff from ~1.5 km of road into a sump-and-pump system; the pump discharges via ~1 km of pipe to the River Lark. When river levels are high the outfall sits below peak river level and the highway drainage cannot discharge at full volume, indirectly causing flooding of the highway. Elevated groundwater (recorded Feb 2024) has been observed emerging from the verge and saturating the road surface ('bubbling' reported), consistent with groundwater flooding and contributing to surface inundation and reduced drainage resilience.

ref.title: Compiegne Way, Bury St Edmunds

Highway engineers reported water 'bubbling' out of the verge onto the road even during dry periods; a panel engineer confirmed groundwater emerging from the verge while assessing the adjacent reservoir. The road sits on a narrow band of clayey superficial deposits that remain saturated longer, maintaining surface emergence of groundwater.

ref.title: Compiegne Way, Bury St Edmunds

info.text: Repeated flooding at the low point in Compiegne Way caused by seasonally high groundwater emerging from the chalk aquifer and surface water from a 1.6 km highway catchment that drains to a pumped drainage system. Frequent pump burnout (exacerbated by high silt loading) and an outfall below peak River Lark levels have resulted in the pump being unable to discharge during high river flows. The road becomes partially blocked or inundated to depths requiring emergency road closures; flooding is prolonged because groundwater involvement prevents rapid drainage, requiring extended closures while water is removed and the drainage network/road surface remediated, imposing significant remediation costs on highway authorities and disrupting vehicular traffic, HGV routes and local access.

info.text: Intense rainfall from Storm Babet overwhelmed natural flow routes and the capacity of watercourses and drainage infrastructure, causing converging overland flows, localised ponding and the internal flooding of properties, infrastructure and services within the village.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Storm Babet (20 Oct 2023) produced significant rainfall that caused internal flooding in the village. Flood water entered properties and flowed through defined flow paths from surrounding fields (pluvial runoff), from overtopping local watercourses (fluvial) and from overwhelmed sewerage/drainage systems. The investigation divides affected areas into three zones: West (Newtown and Mill Road), Central (Church Road, Shop Street, Old Stores Close, Willow Tree Yard, Willow Green) and East (Church Street, Worlingworth Hall Farm), indicating multiple streets and clusters experienced internal and external flooding and flow routing through the village.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: A significant surface-water flow path runs west-to-east through the village centre. During the event this overwhelmed local drainage, causing highway flooding in the centre of the village and affecting properties in central Worlingworth.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: During Storm Babet, prolonged antecedent rainfall left ground saturated and the village's clayey, low-permeability soils produced extensive surface water runoff and overland flow, leading to local flooding.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: The western part of the village (Newtown) experienced internal flooding to properties. Blocked and poorly maintained watercourses and silted ponds reduced conveyance and holding capacity; debris and fallen trees in channels caused blockages, leading to water backing up, overtopping features and flowing to low points where houses are located. Reports from Mill Lane were also received but severity is not described in detail.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Overland surface water flows caused internal flooding to several residential houses, damaging furniture, flooring and personal effects. Significant surface water flows also caused damage and deposited debris in surrounding hedgerows, gardens and on highways; ponding occurred in isolated low spots on saturated ground.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Extensive internal flooding of residential properties with water entering from overwhelmed drainage, surcharging manholes and overtopping watercourses. Floodwaters caused damage to furniture, flooring and personal effects; water poured out of manhole covers into road and verges and overtopped watercourses spilled into properties and onto the highway; overland flows damaged hedgerows, gardens and highways.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: The village experienced flooding during Storm Babet from two sources: prolonged heavy rain causing the drainage network to overflow (bringing water up through highway drains and along Shop Street) and overtopping of local ordinary watercourses (notably the west–east watercourses behind Willow Green and Willow Tree Yard and the south–north watercourse adjacent to Swan Road). Floodwater cascaded down Shop Street to Willow Green, affected properties in the Close, overtopped culverts at the highway, and inundated gardens and properties adjacent to the watercourses.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Significant overland flow and watercourse overtopping caused pooling in the village centre, overwhelming drainage and ponds and causing internal and external flooding to residential homes and businesses. Internal flooding reached 37 cm in affected properties. Highways and Anglian Water assets were overwhelmed; water was forced back up manhole covers. Some properties remained uninhabitable six months after the event.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Significant rainfall and saturated ground caused high levels of overland flow toward the centre of the village. Watercourses exceeded capacity and flowed out of bank, contributing to overland flows that overwhelmed water-management features at pinch points near the community centre. Change in topography slowed flows in the village centre, increasing local accumulation and causing drainage systems to be overcapacity.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: The eastern end of the village experienced flooding during the event: a small number of properties were flooded internally and several properties had flooding to gardens and outbuildings due to watercourses and surface-water runoff overtopping and overwhelming local drainage.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Significant rainfall and overland flows caused watercourses to overtop and local low spots to fill in east Worlingworth. Residential properties experienced internal flooding to significant depths; some residents had to move out of their homes for several months. Other properties had water flowing across gardens and into outbuildings without internal inundation.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Residential yard and adjacent open field were inundated; floodwater reached close to the top of a garden gate and covered the yard up to the brick wall, with the neighbouring field extensively flooded, indicating property-level and local area inundation.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Residential backyard and garden were submerged in muddy floodwater. Water covered most of the garden area, reached the bases of the garden shed, hedges and a large tree, and encroached onto a wooden deck, putting items on the deck at risk of being overtaken by rising water.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Floodwater breached the doorway of a residential property and entered the interior, covering the floor to several centimetres, submerging outdoor furniture in the garden and contaminating the house with muddy runoff.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Residential area in central Worlingworth experienced heavy surface-water/urban flooding that covered the road, extended onto verges and lawns and reached up to houses; vehicles were partially submerged and access would have been impeded.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Surface water and overland flows affecting the eastern edge of the village (south of Church Road adjacent to the Anglian Water pumping station) were identified during the investigation. The report recommends reinstating/reprofiling watercourses and attenuation in this area to reduce flood flows.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Reports were received of flooding affecting the Mill Road / Mill Lane area during the event; blocked channels and poor maintenance were reported as contributing to local runoff and flooding of the highway/adjacent properties.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Homes on either side of Church Road were affected by floodwater from overwhelmed drainage networks; floodwater cascaded down the street contributing to flows toward Willow Green.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

A culverted section at the highway was quickly overwhelmed, causing significant overtopping that added to floodwater on the highway and into properties.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: A watercourse running along the south side of Church Road was quickly overwhelmed by runoff; highways grips could not discharge effectively and the watercourse overtopped its banks, adding to water on the road. ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Area around Church Road was implicated in the investigation: reinstatement/maintenance of watercourses south of Church Road (adjacent to AW pumping station) and investigation of piped sections/outfalls were recommended to address surface-water flows and drainage issues observed during the flood investigation.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Areas north and south of Church Road experienced surface water / overland flows. Actions proposed include reinstating an open channel between the AW pumping station and the nearby watercourse and investigating highway drainage to manage surface water.

ref.title: Worlingworth Flood Investigation – Storm Babet October 2023

info.text: Shop Street (in the Central zone) experienced internal flooding of properties from surface water runoff, overtopping watercourses and overwhelmed sewer/drainage systems, forming part of the central flow paths through the village.

info.text: During Storm Babet Shop Street experienced flooding from both overwhelmed drainage infrastructure and overtopping watercourses; drainage network overflowed, water poured from manhole covers and floodwater deepened to affect homes.

info.text: Part of the Wetheringsett-cum-Brockford parish which was severely impacted by flooding between 18–21 Oct 2023; natural and drainage flow routes were overwhelmed, overland flow convergence led to internal flooding of properties and disruption to local infrastructure and services.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Wetheringsett was one of the main affected areas during Storm Babet, experiencing significant internal flooding to property and infrastructure from a combination of surface water runoff, overtopping watercourses and overwhelmed drainage/sewage systems.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Significant internal flooding to properties and village infrastructure in Wetheringsett. The village was identified as one of the main affected areas; floodwater originated from surface runoff, overtopping watercourses and overwhelmed drainage/sewer systems. Localised flooding was also reported in nearby streets (Station Road, Park Green and Weatherup Street).

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Central Wetheringsett is mapped as having significant fluvial flood risk from local watercourses (and associated pluvial flow paths). The settlement is identified as a low-lying convergence point for flows and is expected to be a primary location to experience flooding during high rainfall. Wetheringsett lies toward the upper extent of the Flood Alert area (Flood Alert issued 20 October 2023) for the River Waveney / River Dove.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Significant flooding affected the parish area, inundating residential properties, roads and local infrastructure in Wetheringsett due to saturated catchment conditions and heavy rainfall.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The local area experienced significant surface water runoff and river overtopping causing internal flooding of properties; private sewerage works in the area continued to be affected in months following the event by high water levels, and possible infilling/lack of maintenance of watercourses prevented water egress in places.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: During the event the village experienced both river (watercourse) flooding and significant surface-water/flash flows. At least 10 properties suffered internal flooding with internal depths of up to 500 mm. The watercourse entering the village from the east was overwhelmed and overtopped early, with water forcing its way around or over constrictions (including a weir, two small brick-arch bridges, a culvert under the old mill, and an engineered ~90° turn), adding floodwater onto the highway and into nearby properties. The central area west of the church (a topographic low) was the most impacted. High-gradient southern and western approach roads produced torrents of surface water across the highway that reached the central low spot. The culvert at the primary school overtopped once its capacity was reached. Community reports indicate some sections of the watercourse north of the village required maintenance and may have reduced channel capacity during the event.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The central village junction experienced torrents of surface water from the south and west that travelled at high speed across the highway and pooled in the village low spot. An eastern watercourse overtopped at a culvert, contributing flood flows into the highway and surrounding properties.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water from a large catchment overwhelmed the village watercourse and highway drainage, causing rapid-onset flooding due to steep topography; the village pumping station was submerged, the foul sewer system was overwhelmed and overflowed into gardens and highways, and properties experienced internal flooding.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Natural areas and vegetation were inundated; muddy floodwater covered the ground and rose partway up tree trunks. Flooding was reported close to the church in Wetheringsett.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: An area in east Wetheringsett (near the village church/Church Street) experienced surface water inundation covering ground, vegetation and surrounding buildings; community members required a small boat to move through the flooded area, indicating significant local disruption to movement and access.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Domestic gardens experienced sewage escape following the storm; the village also had observed watercourse blockages and drainage defects (e.g. Church Street, Brockford Street) contributing to local flooding and drainage issues.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Investigation and planned works to improve the watercourse network through Wetheringsett (including investigating capacity at engineered turns) and feasibility work for Natural Flood Management features to attenuate water in the upper catchments.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface-water flows affected the village, prompting proposed works (watercourse improvements and NFM in upper catchments) to improve the village's flood resilience.

info.text: Area identified as low-lying with several south-to-north flow paths converging through Brockford Street; map and report link the River Dove and local surface water flow paths to significant flood risk in this location and describe significant levels of surface water runoff during the October 2023 event, with water able to enter properties via airbricks or gaps under floors.

ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Severe flooding with floodwater from an overtopped River Dove, significant surface water runoff from the A140 and surrounding fields, and overwhelmed watercourses/drainage. ref.title: Wetheringsett-Cum-Brockford Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Figure 15 and the report describe waterflow paths in north Brockford Street directing runoff from the built-up area towards the River Dove. Community reports and the bridge restriction indicate that during the event water left the channel upstream of the bridge and flowed onto the road and surrounding properties on the west side of the A140. Properties along north Brockford Street lie on these flow paths and were likely exposed to converging runoff and risk of inundation during the event (this is inferred from the map and community reports).

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: One of the most significantly impacted communities during Storm Babet (20 Oct 2023). The town experienced major flooding from fluvial and pluvial sources (often combined); the majority of property flooding included a fluvial element as the River Ore and Cherry Brook exceeded capacity and overtopped their banks. Water levels rose rapidly and a Flood Warning was issued.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The central area of Framlingham (including the town spine) was affected by flooding during the event as rising River Ore / Mere levels and heavy rainfall caused inundation of central streets and public areas.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The town has been impacted by multiple historical flood events (fluvial and pluvial) and experienced notable impacts during Storm Babet when several streets were among the worst affected.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Central and low-lying parts of Framlingham experienced surface-water (pluvial) and river (fluvial) flooding. During the October 2023 Storm Babet event, parts of the town (including central areas and locations along the main river channel and tributaries) were among the worst affected — roads and pavements flooded and drainage systems overflowed. The town has a history of pluvial flood incidents since 2012.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Central and low-lying parts of Framlingham experienced converging overland pluvial flows from surrounding higher ground and fluvial influence from the Cherry Brook and the River Ore during the event, causing surface water accumulation and fluvial inundation; the valley acted as a storage area retaining excess flood water which discharged slowly into the river and overwhelmed local infrastructure and watercourses.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Multiple overland pluvial flow paths from higher ground converged in the town; the valley acted as a storage area during intense rainfall causing excess flood water to be retained and slowly discharge into the river and down the catchment. Infrastructure and watercourses were overwhelmed during the event. Low-lying streets identified as some of the worst affected were Brook Lane, Albert Place, Station Road and Fairfield Road.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The town's low-lying position on Lowestoft Formation 'Diamicton' (boulder clay) and surrounding loamy, clayey soils with reduced infiltration led to overland flow and accumulation of surface water during the extreme rainfall (Storm Babet following a wet week). These ground and topographic conditions contributed to surface water/overland flow flooding of the town.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Overtopping of the River Ore and the Mere combined with pluvial runoff from surrounding roads and catchment flow paths caused rapid expansion of flood water across north Framlingham. Flood water inundated The Elms car park and flowed through to flood the Elms residential area; River overtopping also flooded residential, commercial properties and Bridge Street. Flood water propagated south and west towards Riverside and Well Close Square.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Framlingham Mere and the River Ore exceeded capacity and overtopped onto roads. Pluvial flows from multiple pathways added to floodwater and highway drainage assets were overwhelmed. Several locations north of Framlingham reported localised surface-water flooding and overwhelmed highway drainage.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Parts of Framlingham (notably West Framlingham and Brook Lane) experienced fluvial overtopping from Cherry Brook combined with rapid surface water runoff from surrounding fields, producing flow routes through the urban area and causing flooding of roads, gardens and properties.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: High rainfall led to Cherry Brook and the River Ore exceeding capacity, causing overtopping and combining with surface-water flows across Framlingham. Multiple roads (including Brook Lane, Station Road and Fairfield Road) and highway drainage assets were overwhelmed, resulting in road and property flooding across the town.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Central Framlingham acted as a basin into which floodwater collected. Flood flows converged along roads (notably around Albert Place and Station Road), with pluvial inflows from Fore Street, Albert Road and gardens adding to the inundation and highway drainage being overwhelmed.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: River Ore overtopped both eastern and western banks, flooding public open space and commercial buildings west of the river. Surface water and runoff from surrounding fields and roads converged through central corridors producing extensive flood depths and flow routes through the town.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: South Framlingham experienced pluvial flooding from adjacent fields which combined with floodwater on roads. The River Ore overtopped in places, causing external rear flooding to properties. Multiple commercial properties on the north end of Woodbridge Road flooded from the front due to surface water; residential properties on Kettleburgh Road were flooded from pluvial flows and overwhelmed ditches. Assets associated with the sewage works reportedly backed up, with water emerging from manhole covers and causing internal flooding (backed-up toilet) in one property.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: High rainfall generated large pluvial flows from multiple directions that converged on the central area; flood routes show water concentrating towards the main road and green space, overwhelming drains and causing local flooding (eg. car park and riverside areas shown in images).

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Local flooding affected the town: gullies and drains became blocked, in‑channel and woody debris accumulated in watercourses (including the Mere), incidents were reported requiring EA attendance and removal of blockages, and community recovery/resilience activity (including a Framlingham Flood Recovery and Resilience Group) formed in response.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Properties and multiple parts of the town flooded during the October 2023 event (Storm Babet). Flooding affected highway drainage and surface water flow paths leading to impacts on roads and carparks; blockages in the river/channel contributed to local flooding and prompted clearance and maintenance actions.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023
