ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Fairfield Road is listed among the lowest-lying locations and was identified as one of the worst-affected areas following Storm Babet, indicating it experienced surface water accumulation and local inundation.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Floodwater flowed along the road and could not discharge into the River Ore because river levels were exceedingly high; highway drainage assets were overwhelmed, causing road flooding and contributing to floodwater buildup on Fairfield Road.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Culvert capacity was exceeded and flows backed up, causing flood water to flow along Fairfield Road in a southerly direction. The road became described as 'a river' within minutes; extensive flood water accumulated on the road and flooded commercial and residential buildings from the front. Highway drainage was overwhelmed, preventing discharge to the river and creating a large expanse of standing water around properties.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Pluvial flows from fields to the east and exceeded culvert capacity sent large volumes of water along Fairfield Road, flooding the road surface and inundating commercial and residential buildings from the front. Simultaneously the River Ore overtopped its eastern bank, flooding properties from the rear. Highway drainage was overwhelmed so water could not discharge to the river, creating a large expanse of standing and fast-flowing water around properties. Floodwater velocity damaged front fencing at one property; a brick wall in front of another property was knocked over. The Environment Agency recorded up to 110 cm of internal flooding in one residential property.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Floodwaters inundated Fairfield Road and adjacent properties, covering roads and entering residential and commercial buildings; access disrupted and infrastructure affected.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The road was completely inundated with muddy floodwater that extended into adjacent fields and residential properties. Gardens and driveways were flooded and property boundaries were breached; a garden wall on Fairfield Road was damaged.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Following the storm the Environment Agency met a resident about concerns along Fairfield Road and removed multiple channel/blockage obstructions that had arisen after Storm Babet to reduce local flooding risk.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Blockages were observed within the channel along Fairfield Road (including a large willow tree within the channel). Removal actions have been started because these blockages increased flood risk and were linked to the flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Channel blockages and surface water flow affected the road during the event; identified as one of the four worst-affected roads requiring removal of blockages, investigation of highway drainage capacity and potential reconnection of surface water flows back into the river. A large willow in the channel (see Willow) was identified for removal to reduce risk.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water was flowing on Fairfield Road; investigations proposed to route flows back to the main river and to examine/enlarge culvert connections to the river to reduce local flooding.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Culverts beneath Fairfield Road that connect local watercourses to the main river were identified as capacity‑constrained and contributing to flooding; investigation actions propose enlarging these culverts and improving highway drainage to better manage surface water flows.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Pluvial flows from fields to the east and exceeded culvert capacity sent large volumes of water along Fairfield Road, flooding the road surface and inundating commercial and residential buildings from the front. Simultaneously the River Ore overtopped its eastern bank, flooding properties from the rear. Highway drainage was overwhelmed so water could not discharge to the river, creating a large expanse of standing and fast-flowing water around properties. Floodwater velocity damaged front fencing at one property; a brick wall in front of another property was knocked over. The Environment Agency recorded up to 110 cm of internal flooding in one residential property.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Following a February 2024 meeting between the EA and a resident about flooding concerns, blockages along the watercourse near Fairfield Road were removed to address those concerns.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Baines Way is included in the East Framlingham zone and was affected by flooding during the rapid rise in river levels and associated surface water impacts; forewarning was minimal.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Woodbridge Road (part of South Framlingham) was identified in the investigation as being affected by flooding during the event resulting from rapid River Ore level rises.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Multiple commercial properties on the north end were flooded from the front by pluvial/surface water flowing south‑west from Fairfield Road and runoff from fields to the east. The River Ore was at full capacity and overtopped in places to the rear of properties; in‑channel blockages/debris may have slowed river conveyance and exacerbated flooding.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Flood water flowed along Woodbridge Road, impacting properties from the front; highway drainage assets were overwhelmed. Flows originated from higher ground/fields to the east.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Kettleburgh Road (part of South Framlingham) was identified in the investigation as being affected by flooding during the event resulting from rapid River Ore level rises.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Kettleburgh Road has historical reports of flooded roads and pavements and was identified among the worst-affected locations during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Historically recorded flooded roads and pavements and reports of blocked and overflowing drains; identified on the predicted pluvial (surface-water) flood risk map as at risk and listed among locations that were amongst the worst affected by flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Residential properties were flooded from the front after pluvial flows from fields to the west overwhelmed drainage ditches and spilled onto the road. Water also backed up from assets associated with the sewage works: water emerged from manhole covers and caused internal flooding (including a backed‑up toilet) in one property.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The Elms car park flooded (recorded event).

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Flood water from the overtopped River Ore and surface water runoff collected in the car park, producing deep inundation and acting as a conduit for water to reach the adjacent Elms residential area.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The Elms car park was inundated with muddy floodwater; multiple vehicles were almost completely submerged, causing significant damage to vehicles and loss of use of the car park.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water impacted The Elms carpark; actions proposed to improve the carpark drainage system to reduce future inundation.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Runoff from fields to the east rapidly flowed down the watercourse between The Knoll and Fairfield Crescent and down The Knoll itself, delivering additional surface water into the channel and contributing to rapid localised flooding that overwhelmed the downstream culvert.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water flowed down The Knoll into the local watercourse and along roads feeding Fairfield Road, contributing additional floodwater that inundated Fairfield Road and nearby properties.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water flowed down Fairfield Crescent into the connecting watercourse, adding to the volume that exceeded the culvert and contributed to flooding along Fairfield Road.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water flowed down Coopers Close (as one of several roads east of Fairfield Road), bringing additional flood water that contributed to the accumulation on Fairfield Road and local property flooding.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Surface water flowed down Brick Lane into the Fairfield Road area, contributing additional flood water that helped inundate Fairfield Road and led to flooding of nearby commercial and residential buildings.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The open watercourse adjacent to Tett Terrace filled to the top of bank; the culvert under Fairfield Road rapidly exceeded capacity and water from the channel spilled onto Fairfield Road, contributing to the road and property flooding.

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Assets associated with the sewage works on Kettleburgh Road backed up; water emerged from manhole covers on the road. Sewer backup caused internal flooding in one property (backed-up toilet).

ref.title: Framlingham Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Main River channels (River Gipping) overtopped and, when combined with converging overland flow paths, contributed to internal flooding of properties, infrastructure and services in Needham Market.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: River level gauges on the River Gipping recorded peak water levels during the event (surpassing previous records from Feb 1979) and the river contributed to fluvial flooding in the area.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The main river Gipping was a primary fluvial influence contributing to fluvial flooding in Needham Market during Storm Babet, causing inundation of adjacent low-lying areas.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Overtopped its banks near Coddenham Road, causing floodwater to flow onto the road and flood nearby properties to the east.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The main river Gipping experienced high flows during the October 2023 event which contributed to flood risk to adjacent areas; actions recommended include maintaining main river channel and investigating bunds/defences (e.g. between Pinecroft and Coddenham Road) to manage flooding from the Gipping.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Severely impacted by intense rainfall from Storm Babet: multiple overland pluvial flow paths entered the town, flowed through open and piped watercourses and converged with the River Gipping. This overwhelmed natural flow routes and drainage/watercourse capacity, causing overtopping of main river channels and resultant internal flooding of properties, infrastructure and services.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Needham Market experienced major flooding on 20 October 2023 from both fluvial and pluvial sources. The Lion Barn drain and Orchard Gate watercourse exceeded capacity and overtopped their banks causing a fluvial element to most property flooding; surface water run-off caused flooding on Foxglove and Hargrave Avenue. Anecdotal evidence indicates initial flooding on Pinecroft Way from the Lion Barn Drain.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Major flooding on 20 October 2023 during Storm Babet caused internal flooding to residential and commercial properties. Flooding sources were fluvial (River Gipping catchment / local watercourses including Lion Barn Drain and Orchard Gate overtopping) and pluvial (surface water run-off affecting streets such as Foxglove Avenue and Hargrave Avenue).

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Multiple residential streets across four investigation zones in Needham Market were affected by flooding during Storm Babet. Pinecroft Way experienced the first signs of flooding on the morning of 20 October caused by rapid runoff from the Lion Barn Drain. The River Gipping registered record peak water levels which contributed to flood warnings for the town and the downstream flood peak travel.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Significant parts of the town experienced both pluvial (surface water) and fluvial (river/tributary) flooding during the event. Multiple main flow paths enter the town leading to flooding on streets and low-lying areas adjacent to watercourses.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Low-lying central areas of the town were inundated during Storm Babet; the town acted as temporary flood storage with overwhelmed drainage and watercourses. Low-lying streets such as Pinecroft Way and Lion Lane were identified among the worst affected.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Multiple overland pluvial flow paths flowed into Needham Market from higher ground (NW, W - Orchard Gate, SW - Barking Road), converging in the town's lower-lying areas (Pinecroft Way, Lion Lane). Low-lying land in the town acted as temporary flood storage, retaining excess flood water that slowly discharged into the River Gipping. Hawks Mill, Pinecroft Way, Limetree Close, Maitland Road and Lion Lane were identified as some of the worst affected areas following Storm Babet; overwhelmed infrastructure and watercourses were observed during the intense rainfall event.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Needham Market experienced surface water / urban flooding associated with extreme rainfall from Storm Babet. Low-lying topography, naturally high groundwater in floodplain alluvium and surrounding slowly-permeable loamy and clayey soils reduced infiltration so more runoff remained on the surface and flowed along multiple flow paths into the town.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: On 20 October 2023 overland flows from surrounding fields and surcharging drainage entered the town, flowing along Barking Road into Foxglove Avenue; carriageways and private car parks were inundated and properties at the junction of Foxglove Avenue and Barking Road were flooded internally (also affected again during Storm Henk in January 2024).

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Intense, prolonged rainfall produced excess surface-water runoff from fields to the west and south of Needham Market. Runoff overwhelmed highway drainage and some ordinary watercourses, causing surface water flooding across parts of the town and inundation of streets and properties.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Intense/prolonged rainfall caused the Lion Barn drain to exceed capacity and overland flows and river overtopping (River Gipping) inundated the floodplain, entered roads and properties, overwhelmed highway drainage, and caused businesses and properties to flood; culvert constriction and a raised bund impeded drainage and increased local inundation.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Residential and commercial properties on Crown Street were internally flooded. River levels rose close to overtopping the flood wall and the river flowed over the public footbridge. Highway drainage outfalls became submerged or were unflapped, allowing river water to enter the highway drainage and pond on the road behind the flood wall.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Overtopping of the main River Gipping, Lion Barn Drain and Orchard Gate watercourse caused floodwater to enter streets and properties across Needham Market. Floodwater overtopped banks and outfalls flooding properties on the northern and southern sides of Pinecroft Way and Limetree Close, backed up onto Lion Lane and flowed into Maitland Road affecting buildings on the Lion Barn industrial estate, and flowed onto Coddenham Road (reported flood depths ~2–3 ft on the road). Repeated internal flooding of properties on Pinecroft Way and Limetree Close was reported over the winter between Storm Babet and Storm Henk.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Overtopping of the Orchard Gate watercourse led to local flooding in Needham Market; makeshift defences were deployed against overtopping.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Properties within Needham Market flooded during Storm Babet (and were also reported to have flooded during Storm Henk). This prompted cyclic cleansing of highway drainage assets, main river and tributary maintenance, offers of Property Flood Resilience measures and the formation of a local flood group to improve community-level resilience.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The town experienced fluvial and surface-water flooding during the October 2023 event; multiple streets and watercourses were identified as worst-affected and targeted for maintenance, investigations and mitigation (highway drainage, culvert checks, PFR grants, NFM options and surveys).

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Town experienced flooding driven by main river issues and blocked highway drainage during the event; highways and local watercourses were identified as worst-affected, prompting actions for main river maintenance, riparian responsibility enforcement and cyclic highway drainage maintenance to remove observed blockages.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Multiple residential streets across four investigation zones in Needham Market were affected by flooding during Storm Babet. Pinecroft Way experienced the first signs of flooding on the morning of 20 October caused by rapid runoff from the Lion Barn Drain. The River Gipping registered record peak water levels which contributed to flood warnings for the town and the downstream flood peak travel.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The Orchard Gate watercourse exceeded its capacity and overtopped its banks during Storm Babet, contributing a fluvial element to internal flooding of properties in Needham Market.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Orchard Gate acted as both a watercourse and a source of overland pluvial flow into Needham Market; it contributed to surface water and fluvial flooding in the town during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The culvert carrying The Orchard Gate into Hawks Mill millpond (Mill Lades) was blocked with building material and debris, restricting flow and causing water to back up toward the railway embankment and the bottom of Victoria Gardens; witnesses reported significant flows through the culvert under the railway embankment.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The Orchard Gate watercourse overtopped and/or was obstructed, causing internal flooding to properties on Highlands Close and John Swain Close. A culvert at the footbridge became blocked (trash screen/large debris), upstream vegetation impeded flow, and a tall brick headwall limited downstream capacity, all contributing to flooding and overtopping into gardens.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Significant flows in the Orchard Gate watercourse from intense/prolonged rainfall led to overtopping of its banks and flow pathways into adjacent urban areas. Multiple constrictions (bridges, blocked culverts, overgrown vegetation) and a low spot in the southern bank contributed to floodwater overtopping into rear gardens on Highlands Close and John Swain Close and impeded conveyance downstream.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Makeshift temporary flood defences (wooden boards and barriers) were installed along the Orchard Gate watercourse adjacent to residential property boundaries to prevent overtopping and protect homes, indicating the watercourse threatened to overtop and cause flooding.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Environment Agency completed maintenance on the full extent of the main river Orchard Gate watercourse (excluding the concrete channel NE of High Street into Luff Meadow and Network Rail land) as a pre- and post-Storm Babet intervention to manage conveyance and reduce flood risk.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Upper section of the Orchard Gate watercourse required a channel maintenance regime because it contributed to flooding; MSDC identified as landowner for this watercourse section.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Orchard Gate watercourse was identified for topographic survey and hydraulic-modelling updates to improve understanding of flood flow through downstream residential streets, indicating it contributed to flooding risk during the event.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Properties on Coddenham Road experienced internal flooding during Storm Babet. Floodwater included a fluvial element from local watercourses (Lion Barn Drain / Orchard Gate) overtopping their banks, with surface-water runoff also contributing.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The road under the Coddenham Road railway bridge floods and becomes inundated during heavy/prolonged rainfall. Coddenham Road is included in the investigation zone affected during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Floodwater backed up through an unflapped outfall and merged with flows on the corner of Coddenham Road and Lion Lane; this flow continued into Maitland Road and contributed to flooding that affected buildings on the Lion Barn industrial estate.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Water from Lion Barn Drain flowed onto Coddenham Road via pedestrian lane and along the verge after culvert surcharge; further east Coddenham Road was flooded when the River Gipping overtopped its banks.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Properties were flooded and the road was inundated when the River Gipping overtopped its banks; floodwater flowed onto the road and matched mapped surface-water extents.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Road surface beneath the Coddenham Road railway bridge was inundated; water accumulation rendered the underpass impassable and would have required closure or diversion until waters receded.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Potential culvert capacity/drainage issue under Lion Lane / Coddenham Road identified; investigation recommended to address flooding/drainage problems at this location.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Area adjacent to Pinecroft where a bund is required to maintain defence from flooding from the main river Gipping; actions propose investigating bund options to balance estate drainage and river defence.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The River Gipping experienced very high flows during Storm Babet; river level gauges recorded peak levels (recorded at Stowmarket on 20 October and Bramford on 21 October) and the River Gipping was included in flood alerts/warnings affecting Needham Market.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: River Gipping overtopped/acted as the main fluvial influence and contributed to fluvial flooding in Needham Market during Storm Babet, affecting low-lying central and eastern parts of the town.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: The river overtopped its banks upstream of Hawks Mill; floodwater from the river merged with overland flows and inundated the floodplain, causing internal flooding to properties on High Street and adjacent roads.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Banks of the River Gipping overtopped upstream of Hawks Mill; floodwater from the river merged with overland flows and tributary flows, inundating much of the River Gipping floodplain which remained in flood for a considerable period. The Environment Agency-operated sluice gate upstream of Hawks Mill was opened fully and functioned throughout the event; the privately owned gate below the mill was also opened at full capacity.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Peak river levels reached in the early hours of 21 October; river flowed over the public footbridge, overtopped banks in multiple locations inundating the floodplain, rose close to overtopping the Crown Street floodwall, submerged outfalls and contributed fluvial flows into the highway drainage and onto Crown Street.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Crown Street suffered property flooding during Storm Babet. The town-wide flooding largely involved fluvial overflow from the Lion Barn Drain and Orchard Gate overtopping, with surface-water runoff also a factor.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Crown Street is recorded as a local residential road that flooded and caused local disruption in the May 2012 event; it is also identified in predicted pluvial risk mapping and listed among streets affected during Storm Babet (Oct 2023).

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Crown Street experienced both surface water (pluvial) flooding and fluvial (river) flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Residential and commercial properties on Crown Street were internally affected by flooding; river levels came close to overtopping the floodwall and fluvial flows may have bypassed the northern end of the floodwall upstream of the garage on Crown Street.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Floodwater ponded on the road behind the floodwall because river levels rose close to overtopping and outfalls became submerged or acted as pathways from the river; fluvial flows may have bypassed the northern end of the floodwall and entered the surface/highway drainage system, resulting in internal flooding of residential and commercial properties.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Crown Street outfalls into the main river channel were identified for investigation following the event; fitting non-return flaps on the outfalls was proposed as a post-event mitigation measure.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Outfalls from the main river channel at Crown Street were identified as causing backflow and contributing to flooding; recommendation to fit non-return flaps and ensure channel maintenance for the upper section to reduce reoccurrence.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Main river outfalls on Crown Street were affected by silt and backflow risk. Actions proposed include de-silting/cleansing of the main river channel and fitting non-return flaps on outfalls to prevent river water backing into the drainage network.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Crown Street is recorded as a local residential road that flooded and caused local disruption in the May 2012 event; it is also identified in predicted pluvial risk mapping and listed among streets affected during Storm Babet (Oct 2023).

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Hawks Mill Street experienced property flooding during the main event on 20 October 2023; flooding included fluvial overflow from local watercourses overtopping their banks, with surface-water runoff contributing in places.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Residential road flooding occurred. During Storm Babet (Oct 18–21 2023) the street was affected by pluvial (surface water) flooding causing local disruption. Historically (May 2012) Hawks Mill Street was flooded alongside Crown Street with local disruption from a combination of River Gipping flooding and surface water run-off.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Floodwater from the River Gipping overtopped and merged with overland flows, causing floodwater to accumulate on roads and resulting in internal flooding of a small number of properties near the junction with High Street; blocked highway drains and low property thresholds contributed to the impacts.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Culvert under Hawks Mill Street identified for CCTV survey and required maintenance because its condition/capacity contributed to drainage problems during the flood event.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Residential road flooding occurred. During Storm Babet (Oct 18–21 2023) the street was affected by pluvial (surface water) flooding causing local disruption. Historically (May 2012) Hawks Mill Street was flooded alongside Crown Street with local disruption from a combination of River Gipping flooding and surface water run-off.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Part of Zone 4 identified as affected by the main flood event; properties within Highlands Close were impacted by the event which included fluvial elements from local watercourses and surface water runoff as part of the town-wide flooding.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Highlands Close was reported as being affected by flooding during Storm Babet (the October 2023 event). The street experienced pluvial / surface-water flooding impacting the residential area.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Highland Close experienced surface water (pluvial) flooding during Storm Babet.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Several properties suffered internal flooding caused by the Orchard Gate watercourse overtopping and/or being obstructed. Floodwater levels peaked around midday on 20 October and had started to drain away by the early evening. A culvert beneath the footbridge was reported blocked (trash screen/obstruction) and a tall brick headwall and overgrown vegetation reduced channel capacity, contributing to overtopping into gardens.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Floodwater routes tracked from the northeast moved through Highlands Close; a low spot in the southern bank of the nearby watercourse provided a pathway for floodwater into rear gardens. Properties and gardens experienced inundation and residents cut makeshift channels/barriers to manage flows.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Flooding affected the estate during the October 2023 event; the report recommends topographic survey and updated hydraulic modelling to improve understanding of flood risk through Pinecroft Way, Highlands Close and John Swain Close following Storm Babet.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Hydraulic-modelling updates were proposed to improve understanding of fluvial and pluvial flooding affecting Highlands Close, indicating it experienced flood impacts during the event.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Part of Zone 4 identified as affected by the main flood event; properties within John Swain Close were impacted by the event which included fluvial elements from local watercourses and surface water runoff as part of the town-wide flooding.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: John Swain Close was reported as being affected by flooding during Storm Babet (the October 2023 event). The street experienced pluvial / surface-water flooding impacting the residential area.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Properties experienced internal flooding and overtopping from the Orchard Gate watercourse. A low section of the southern bank to the rear of John Swain Close provided a flow pathway into gardens; residents created makeshift barriers after the event. Contributing factors included culvert blockage downstream, a restrictive headwall at the footbridge and overgrown channel vegetation upstream.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: A low section of the southern bank of the adjacent watercourse allowed overtopping into rear gardens. Residents constructed makeshift barriers after Storm Babet to try to prevent water entering gardens; multiple constrictions and blockages upstream hindered conveyance and contributed to local flooding.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Flooding affected the estate during the October 2023 event; the report recommends topographic survey and updated hydraulic modelling to improve understanding of flood risk through Pinecroft Way, Highlands Close and John Swain Close following Storm Babet.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: John Swain Close was identified for hydraulic-modelling updates to understand flood risk and to inform mitigation, indicating it was affected by flooding in the event.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: First signs of flooding were observed on Pinecroft Way on the morning of 20 October 2023; flooding was caused by water from the Lion Barn Drain rather than the River Gipping.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Pinecroft Way was affected by both pluvial (surface water) and fluvial (river/tributary) flooding during Storm Babet, experiencing inundation from surface-water run-off and river influence.

ref.title: Needham Market Flood Investigation – Storm Babet 2023

info.text: Internal flooding of properties caused by water rising up through road gullies. Floodwater travelled down the Lion Barn drain and backflowed into gullies (outfalls largely lacked non-return flaps), contributing to internal property flooding on the estate.

info.text: Local flooding occurred in Oldbury-on-Severn; the report specifically investigates the flood incident affecting the village on 9 March 2016 and examines tidal influence (tide locking) using tide gauge data from Avonmouth and Sharpness to understand sources of the local flooding.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: Oldbury-on-Severn was impacted by flood flows routed through the Oldbury Naite rhine during the event on 9 March 2016; assessment indicates these flows reached the village and produced the reported flooding.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: The centre of Oldbury-on-Severn experienced elevated water levels on 9 March 2016 when high river flows coincided with a high tide. Surveyed high water and photographic evidence show peak levels in the village, with peak levels recorded below the crest of formal defences.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: Oldbury-on-Severn experienced inundation during the 9 March 2016 event. Parish Council survey points in the village recorded high water levels (around 6.1–6.4 m) that were below the approximate crest of formal defences (~6.5 mAOD). The survey and photographic evidence document localized flooding of roads and properties within the village.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: During the 9th March 2016 event there were instances of property and road flooding in Oldbury-on-Severn caused by high rainfall and overland flow routes. Specific properties (the Anchor Inn and Christmas Cottage on Church Road) were flooded; blocked drainage in the Anchor Inn garden was identified as a main cause, with high rhine levels potentially a contributing factor.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: Property and road flooding occurred during the 9 March 2016 event. Properties at the Anchor Inn and Christmas Cottage, immediately south of the main watercourse on Church Road, experienced flooding driven mainly by overland runoff and a blocked drainage feature in the Anchor Inn garden (thresholds were above peak rhine levels so runoff rather than direct rhine overtopping was the primary cause). Runoff down Church Hill and Westmarsh Lane exacerbated flooding of this and adjacent areas; highway drainage condition and capacity contributed to impacts.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: The village area is below the local Highest Astronomical Tide (~8.5mAOD) and experienced elevated water levels during the March 2016 flood, with fluvial–tidal interaction raising levels in the Rhine network and contributing to flooding in Oldbury-on-Severn. Upstream moor storage reduced peak levels.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: Significant parts of Oldbury-on-Severn were vulnerable to elevated water levels when fluvial flows combined with spring tides. The Rhine network experienced raised water levels during the March 2016 event; Chapel Road reached around 6.0mAOD. Existing tidal flaps normally convey flows at low/intermediate tides but offer limited benefit when higher fluvial flows coincide with spring tides. Report notes pumping would need to move several cubic metres per second to materially reduce levels.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: During the 9 March 2016 event floodwater produced raised water levels through Oldbury-on-Severn (around 6.0 mAOD). Peak flows during the event constrained levels in the village and determined the extent/duration of flooding; modelling of upstream storage and field attenuation was identified as relevant to reducing peak levels at Oldbury.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: Oldbury‑on‑Severn experienced elevated flood levels during the event; recommendations refer to flood wall overtopping, flood water passing onto roads, and options to reduce flood levels within the village (including using other rhine systems and increasing tidal gate capacity when high fluvial flows combine with spring tides).

info.text: The lower reaches of the Oldbury Naite rhine (referred to as Lower Oldbury) have limited conveyance capacity; a 2002 review noted the lower reaches capacity (~14.4 m3/s) and identified this as roughly equivalent to a 1-in-10 to 1-in-20 annual probability flood (including a tide-lock allowance). The study highlighted capacity concerns and potential for overtopping in the catchment.

info.text: Peak water levels were recorded in the Naite rhine during the 9th March 2016 event; these high levels may have been a contributing factor to flooding of nearby properties (for example Anchor Inn and Christmas Cottage). The report also flagged capacity concerns in the Upper Oldbury Naite/Rockhampton rhine area and recommended a hydraulic-model review and potential longer-term alleviation measures.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: During the 9th March 2016 event the Rhine experienced tide-locking and high fluvial flows. Closure of the tidal flaps during the rising tide meant fluvial water could not escape for a period (~just under 3 hours), requiring storage within the Rhine and adjacent low-lying ground and raising water levels to the observed peak (~6.1mAOD at Church Road). This raised peak levels contributed to flooding of adjacent low-lying areas and properties.

ref.title: Oldbury-On-Severn Flood Report

info.text: Fluvial flows in the upper Oldbury Naite rhine transferred water into the low-lying upstream moor storage during the March 2016 flood, influencing downstream Rhine network levels and contributing to elevated flood levels in Oldbury-on-Severn. ref.title: Section 19 Investigation Report: June 2016 Flood Events

info.text: During the evening of 16 June 2016 about 40 residential properties across Edgeley flooded (mostly internal). The greatest concentration was around Edgeley Road (25 properties flooded, all but one internally). Other property impacts included 6 properties on Oak Street, 4 on St Lesmo Road, 2 on Clwyd Avenue and 1 on The Circuit. Highway, pavement and driveway flooding occurred at the eastern end of Laburnum Way, and surface water ponding affected the junction of Myrtle Street and the A560 Brinksway. Runoff from Bonar Park and a blockage in the surface water sewer on Myrtle Street contributed to surface water flowing down Myrtle Street onto Oak Street and pooling at the Brinksway junction. United Utilities attended during the event, removed the Myrtle Street blockage and later inspected sewers and removed roots.

info.text: The A555 drainage scheme (networks A, B and C and other elements) exhibited post-flood problems: attenuation and routing arrangements did not adequately manage exceedance flows, there is evidence of potential non-filling of attenuation Pond B, blockages and construction defects, and unattenuated runoff contributed to local flooding during the 28 Jul 2019 - 31 Jul 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The A555 drainage network receives runoff from in excess of 1300 m of carriageway plus substantial green areas (compared with the original design provision for 700 m of carriageway), increasing peak flows and volumes to existing storage and the Hall Moss Lane pumping station. Pond E2 has a storage volume of 981 m3 and a Hydrobrake pass-forward flow of 14.6 l/s. The combined E1/E2 arrangement has an extended drain-down time (estimated between 4.5 days with no inflow and up to 2 weeks with steady inflow of 10 l/s), leaving the highway vulnerable to long-duration and follow-on rainfall events. The original pump station is likely inadequate to drain the combined new and original road to a reasonable standard, increasing flood risk to the carriageway and requiring potential enlargement of ponds or additional mitigation.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Extensive flood damage experienced in the catchments upstream of the SMBC boundary, notably in Poynton.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The highest daily rainfall on 31 July 2019 was centred on Poynton; intense local rainfall led to expected surface water flooding and increased runoff to ordinary watercourses, increasing local flood risk and overwhelming local drainage.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: On 31 July 2019 the water level at the Poynton gauge reached 2.195 m (the highest since records began in December 2008), indicating a significant river flood event affecting the Poynton area; the peak was driven by the 31 July rainfall falling on already saturated ground.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Poynton Brook flooding prompted EA clear-up operations and processing of flood reports; the EA also issued flood warnings for Poynton Brook locations (including Poynton and Midway, and earlier for Wigwam Wood and parts of Armcon Business Park) during the period.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Intense rainfall centred on Poynton on 31 Jul 2019 produced peak flows on Poynton Brook and caused significant river and surface-water flooding; flows exceeded typical drainage design standards.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Experienced significant flood damages in the upper reaches of the Micker Brook / Lady Brook catchment during the July 2019 event; local intense rainfall and runoff contributed to downstream flows.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Subject to flood flows coming from the upper Micker Brook catchment during the late July 2019 event, contributing to notable flooding in the area.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Significant flooding and widespread problems occurred in Poynton during the July–August 2019 event; Cheshire Fire and Rescue Service declared a major incident in Poynton on 31 Jul 2019 in response to flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report: Storm Christoph 18th to 21st January 2021

info.text: Poynton is included in the Micker Brook (and related) catchment descriptions. The report states that localised intense rainfall on these catchments (including Poynton) can result in rapid flooding that the Mersey-based warning system may not detect, implying Poynton may have experienced rapid/flash flooding or contributed runoff to the Micker Brook system during the event (uncertain/not quantified in the text).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Recorded clear spikes in flow on 28 July and 31 July 2019 with the peak on 31 July significantly greater than the 28 July peak, indicating rapid runoff and river flooding of Poynton Brook during the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Recorded rapid spikes in water level on 28 July and 31 July 2019, with the 31 July peak substantially larger. At the Poynton gauge the water level reached 2.195 m on 31 July 2019 (the highest since records began in December 2008). Flood-frequency analysis gives an estimated peak flow of around 12 m3/s for the July 2019 event with an indicative return period of about 45 years.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Peak flows were recorded on 31 July 2019; the Poynton gauge reached its highest level on record (2.195 m) during this event, indicating significant river flooding on Poynton Brook driven by the 31 July rainfall on saturated ground.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The Environment Agency conducted clear-up operations on Poynton Brook, clearing accumulated debris and processing flood reports; flood warnings were issued for sections of Poynton Brook (Wigwam Wood, parts of Armcon Business Park, Poynton and Midway) during the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Peak flows recorded on 31 July 2019; gauge records show the 31 July peaks exceeded those on 28 July, indicating significant river response during the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A major reservoir safety incident was declared at Toddbrook Reservoir with a risk of imminent dam failure following the heavy rainfall; pumping was later commenced to lower stored water and pumped water was discharged to the River Goyt (which flows to the River Mersey).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A reservoir safety incident developed on 01 Aug 2019 (driven by the heavy rainfall on 31 Jul 2019) that threatened downstream inundation of nearby communities; emergency interventions prevented the inundation.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Whaley Bridge was affected by the Toddbrook reservoir safety incident (risk of dam failure) prompted by the rainfall and high inflows to the reservoir; pumping operations were undertaken to lower the reservoir, with discharge to the River Goyt.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Community affected by the Toddbrook Reservoir safety incident which created a risk of downstream inundation and prompted risk-to-life reports and emergency actions; actual inundation was averted.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Original A555 pump station adjacent to Hall Moss Lane was exposed as deteriorating; during the March event only two of four pumps were working and in July drainage relied on a temporary pump in the wet well. Flooding at Hall Moss Lane led to A555 closure and prevented contractor access to the pump station during the July event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Deep flooding at Hall Moss Lane prevented access. Runoff collected at Hall Moss Lane overwhelmed Network E attenuation and pumping capacity (the single temporary pump in operation could not cope), causing attenuation ponds E1 and E2 to overflow onto the A555 carriageway and flow westwards toward the original pump station. Overflow contributed to carriageway flooding and inundation of the pump station; supplementary temporary pumps were required to drain the carriageway and attenuation storage.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The original A555 pump station no.4 at Hall Moss Lane overloaded/failed during the storm, contributing to surface-water flooding and making the A555 completely impassable.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The original A555 Hall Moss Lane pumping station received discharge from Network E, which had been designed to a lower standard (30-year); no assessment of the combined original and new drainage was made. This contributed to inadequate conveyance and surcharging during the 28 Jul 2019 - 31 Jul 2019 floods.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A555 flooded at Hall Moss Lane adjacent to the original A555 pump station (Network E); the pump station could not be accessed by contractor APS on 28 Jul due to depth of flooding. Road closure and police attendance were reported (police call at 11:45, road closed 13:30 on 28 Jul).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Original A555 pump station adjacent to Hall Moss Lane was exposed as deteriorating; during the March event only two of four pumps were working and in July drainage relied on a temporary pump in the wet well. Flooding at Hall Moss Lane led to A555 closure and prevented contractor access to the pump station during the July event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The original A555 pump station at Hall Moss Lane is described as likely inadequate and is sited immediately below Spath Brook; its vulnerable location and the brook's small, overgrown channel increase risk of the brook overflowing to the A555 and of the pump station being overwhelmed.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding occurred at the A555/Hall Moss Lane location; the original A555 pump station at Hall Moss Lane was exposed as deteriorating during heavy rain (pumps failing), requiring temporary pumping from the wet well to Spath Brook and later replacement of pumps and controls. Flooding at this location contributed to road closures and repeated inundation of the carriageway.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Attenuation ponds at Woodford Road gyratory were damaged in the March event. During the July event the A555 carriageway at Woodford Road (Poynton) flooded, the Network C pump alarm triggered and the adjacent Network C pump station experienced pump trips; the Network C attenuation pond overflowed and was damaged.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A555 flooding affected the Woodford Road / Woodford gyratory area (Poynton); attenuation ponds at the Woodford Road gyratory were damaged and Network C pump alarms triggered. The Woodford Road section was closed and later cleared/reopened (cleared and reopened between A523 and Woodford gyratory on 29 July).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A555 carriageway flooded at Woodford Road (Woodford Road bridge). Network C pump station adjacent to Woodford Road experienced pump trips and high pond levels; APS attended on 29 Jul, restarted pumps and cleared floodwater, and on 31 Jul pumps tripped again as the pond was full and overflowed, causing the carriageway to flood.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Attenuation ponds at Woodford Road gyratory were damaged in the March event. During the July event the A555 carriageway at Woodford Road (Poynton) flooded, the Network C pump alarm triggered and the adjacent Network C pump station experienced pump trips; the Network C attenuation pond overflowed and was damaged.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A555 flooding affected the Woodford Road / Woodford gyratory area (Poynton); attenuation ponds at the Woodford Road gyratory were damaged and Network C pump alarms triggered. The Woodford Road section was closed and later cleared/reopened (cleared and reopened between A523 and Woodford gyratory on 29 July).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The A555 Manchester section under Wilmslow Rd Bridge (within Cheshire East Council boundary) was closed because of flooding during the late-July 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A555 Manchester section closed under Wilmslow Rd Bridge due to flooding in that location (closure noted as not SMBC responsibility).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Hydraulic capacity of the Wilmslow Road bridge over Micker Brook was exceeded by the flow on 31 July 2019, associated with overland flow across Wilmslow Road and upstream/backwater effects.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Debris accumulations observed upstream and debris and siltation observed downstream of the bridge, contributing to blockages and localised flow restrictions during the Micker Brook flood in late July 2019.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Poynton Brook flooding threatened/impacted Wigwam Wood; the EA issued Flood Warnings for Poynton Brook at Wigwam Wood (28/07/2019 and 31/07/2019) and carried out post-event clear-up of debris from the watercourse.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The Environment Agency carried out clear-up operations on Norbury Brook, removing accumulated debris and processing flood reports following the July 2019 intense rainfall.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: During the July 2019 event Norbury Brook experienced high flows from upstream catchments; bank slippage at a manhole partially exposed the manhole and removed the outfall headwall of an adjacent drain. Debris was observed trapped in an outlet pipe downstream of Pond B.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: High flows and/or surcharged carriageway drainage contributed to bank slippage adjacent to Norbury Brook. Bank slippage partially exposed a manhole and removed the outfall headwall of a nearby landscaping drain; debris was noted in an outlet pipe downstream of Pond B.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Environment Agency carried out clear-up operations and removed accumulated debris from the watercourse following the intense rainfall on 28–31 July 2019; flood reports for the watercourse were processed and reviewed against EA flood mapping.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Long‑standing flooding in the Adswood area (including Clover Avenue and Culver Road) was exacerbated in the July 2019 event; flooding was linked to a partially blocked culverted watercourse beneath the Stockport–Crewe railway (grout blockage) reducing conveyance and contributing to surface/river flooding of the street and adjoining properties/areas.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: A known blockage in a culverted watercourse under Network Rail land caused the UU surface-water network to surcharge and directly flood Adswood Road and adjacent highway drains, contributing to highway and property flooding; highway gullies and the local drainage were affected and there is likely linkage to UU foul/combined system.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Road and adjacent areas were flooded as part of exceedance flows from high ground; UU surface water network was overwhelmed causing surface water to spill onto the road and contribute to local flooding.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: UU surface water network was overwhelmed and spilled onto roads; overland flows from higher ground and blocked highway gullies caused flooding along Guywood Lane as part of an interlinked set of incidents in the area.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding of a basement flat at Guywood Lane produced a 'Risk to Life' report during the July 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Drainage networks feeding Guywood Lane were identified as having capacity restrictions during the July 2019 event, resulting in ponding and surface water flooding; investigations were recommended to identify constraints and options to drain ponded areas (including Leyfield Avenue).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding from overland surface water flows and surcharge of the surface water network affected the road and surrounding area during the July 2019 event; blocked gullies and overwhelmed drainage contributed to the impacts.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: UU surface water network overwhelmed; surface water spilled onto Sandy Lane with blocked road gullies and some overland flow contribution from higher ground.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface-water ponding and drainage network capacity issues affecting Sandy Lane during the July 2019 event; prompted investigation into full extents of drainage networks and options for upstream source control, local storage, exceedance flow paths and enhanced drainage of ponding areas.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding concentrated on Leyfield Avenue as exceedance flows from high ground and an overwhelmed UU surface water network spilled onto roads; blocked gullies exacerbated inundation of the street and adjacent properties/areas during the July 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Observed ponding of surface water at Leyfield Avenue during the July 2019 event; listed as a location where investigations and interventions (options to drain ponded water) are required.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Leyfield Avenue experienced ponding during the drainage exceedance identified from the July 2019 event; the report recommends reviewing opportunities to enhance capacity including options to drain ponded water at Leyfield Avenue to reduce flood impact.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding was reported at Mostyn Road during the 2019 event. The likely cause is surface water runoff from adjacent roads/fields, with a possible contributory role from surcharge in the local drainage network; further investigation of the drainage network was recommended.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: At least one property experienced flooding below the floorboards and garden flooding to a depth recorded up to 600 mm.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Floodwater occurred at Mostyn Road; reporting indicates the water may have been from surface water runoff from adjacent roads/fields and/or surcharge from the local drainage system.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Fluvial flooding from Micker Brook at Sandringham Road produced observed flood extents during the July 2019 event that were greater than the Environment Agency's mapped extents; report recommends review of modelling and mapping for this location.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: July 2019 flood outline exceeded the current 1 in 1000 flood extent, causing flooding of new residential properties on Sandringham Road.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding occurred at Sandringham Road with the flooded extent exceeding the Environment Agency's mapped 1,000‑year flood extent; the report highlights this as an out‑of‑modelled-extent event and recommends investigation into modelling deficiencies or significant blockages.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Fluvial flooding associated with Lady Brook / Micker Brook inundated Sandringham Road during the July 2019 event, contributing to the need to validate 2019 flood extents and consider channel and infrastructure interventions.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding during the July 2019 event with flood extents identified along the road that require validation in updated fluvial flood mapping.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Experienced flooding during the same July 2019 event as part of the Lady Brook / Micker Brook modelled reach; identified for review alongside other nearby road flooding locations.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Six recently constructed houses on the north side were flooded from the rear as the flood extent of Lady Brook expanded. Contaminated floodwater entered properties to a depth of about 0.3 m (1 ft). Foul sewage was forced from sinks as UU foul/combined sewers became surcharged by surrounding fluvial floodwater.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Residential properties on Sandringham Road were flooded during the July 2019 event. The observed flood extents match the EA pluvial (surface water) flood mapping but conflict with the EA fluvial (river) mapping, suggesting either modelling error or elevated levels caused by partial blockage/structures (weirs) behind properties. This indicates a need to review flood modelling and consider mitigation for the road/properties.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Sandringham Road experienced fluvial (river) flooding in late July 2019 caused by flows on Lady/Micker Brook; the road corridor corresponded with the high-risk flood corridor on the EA surface-water map for the area.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Fluvial (river) flooding from Lady/Micker Brook was identified as the primary driver of flooding at Sandringham Road in July 2019.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Linked in the report to flooding from the same brook/river model that produced out-of-bank flow during the 31 July 2019 event. The model under-predicted overland flow in the area and Sandringham Road is flagged for review as part of that hydraulic/model discrepancy.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Demmings (and the weir upstream of it) is part of the Micker Brook catchment network that conveyed flows during the 2019 flood events; it is on a downstream reach receiving cumulative upstream runoff.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Debris was reported in the riverbed upstream and downstream of The Demmings culvert; a possible blockage release at The Demmings is cited as a factor that may have increased the July 2019 flood extent and produced surges downstream.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Development adjacent to The Demmings was approved without apparent due consideration of exceedance flow paths and access to the watercourse. During the 28 Jul 2019 - 31 Jul 2019 event, flows did not follow the assumed culvert route and exceedance flows affected the area, demonstrating the approved measures were insufficient.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Fluvial flooding during the July 2019 event inundated The Demmings area as part of the Lady Brook / Micker Brook flood extents, affecting local streets and adjacent properties and triggering recommendations for survey and mitigation options.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flood inundation observed in July 2019 and identified as needing validation in updated fluvial flood mapping of the catchment.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Experienced flooding during the July 2019 event as part of the Lady Brook / Micker Brook catchment impacts and is identified for model/section review.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Properties at The Demmings were reported flooded during the event of 31 July 2019.

info.text: Out-of-bank flows from Micker Brook caused flooding in the Queens Road and The Demmings area. Increased upstream water levels and debris/back-up were cited as contributing to flow leaving the channel onto adjacent land upstream of Queens Road.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The culvert entrance below Clarendon Road is identified as the likely location of surcharge that led to flooding on Hazelwood Road during the July 2019 event; regular inspection and maintenance of the culvert entrance is recommended.

info.text: Surcharged condition at the entrance to the culvert below Clarendon Road contributed to localised flooding (it was a key location where surcharge occurred).

info.text: Shown on the July 2019 borough map as a hotspot (cluster of reported flooding incidents plotted by postcode), indicating local property/highway flooding reports in that area during the event.

info.text: The United Utilities surface water system was surcharged at this location; blockages were identified and cleared, which is reported to have improved the local flooding situation.

info.text: Localised surface water flooding affecting the road and nearby properties; documented in Appendix M of the report.

info.text: Werneth Road is shown on the hotspot map (Figure 2.1) with clustered reported flooding incidents in July 2019, indicating localised property/highway flooding impacts.
