info.text: Surface water runoff from Werneth Low overwhelmed highway drainage and caused blockages and flooding on Werneth Road.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface water flooding affected Werneth Road; documented in Appendix O of the report (Glenside Drive and Werneth Road, Woodley).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface water overland flows and surcharging of the UU surface water network led to flooding on the road and adjacent areas during the July 2019 event; road gullies were blocked, contributing to inundation.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface water sewer network was overwhelmed and spilled to the road; highway gullies were blocked by debris and overland flows contributed to flooding on Central Drive as part of the Romiley cluster.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Central Avenue (sic) formed part of the drainage catchment identified as experiencing capacity issues and ponding during the July 2019 event; actions were recommended to map and review drainage extents and capacity and to identify interventions to reduce surface water flooding.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface water overland flows and a surcharged UU surface water network caused flooding on Compstall Road during the July 2019 event, with road gullies blocked and runoff concentrating toward Leyfield Avenue.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface water sewer network surcharged and spilled to roads; blocked highway gullies and overland flows contributed to flooding incidents on Compstall Road within the interconnected Romiley area.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface-water runoff/drainage from Sandy Lane and adjacent catchments discharging towards Compstall Road with suspected capacity restrictions contributing to ponding and flooding issues during the July 2019 event; prompted investigations of the discharge route and capacity constraints.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Compstall Road is described as the discharge route for drainage from Guywood Lane/Central Avenue/Sandy Lane and was implicated in capacity/restriction issues during the July 2019 event, contributing to ponding and downstream flood risk; investigations to identify restrictions and options to enhance capacity were recommended.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding was reported at Corfe Crescent during the 2019 event. The likely cause is surface water runoff from adjacent roads/fields, with a possible contributory role from surcharge in the local drainage network; investigation of the drainage network was recommended.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Road carriageway and front gardens of many houses were completely flooded; several properties reported internal flooding. Drains and gullies were surcharged in the locale and there were reports of some sewage contamination. External flooding and flooding of garages occurred on 28 July 2019 with greater depths on 31 July 2019.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: External flooding affecting the street and flooding of garages. Pluvial mapping shows an area of flooding at Corfe Crescent with potential to impact property; reports record greater depth of flooding on 31 Jul 2019 compared with 28 Jul 2019.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Floodwater occurred at Corfe Crescent; reporting indicates the water may have been from surface water runoff from adjacent roads/fields and/or surcharge from the local drainage system.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Brook House was within the July 2019 flood outline which exceeded the modelled 1 in 1000 extents; the report notes that flood mapping did not show the exceedance flow path around this building and identifies debris/possible blockages in the nearby culvert (The Demmings).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: July 2019 (28 Jul–31 Jul 2019): Flooding affected the Brook House area; mapping did not show the exceedance flow path around the building. An upstream blockage/release at Brook House/The Demmings is identified as possibly increasing 2019 flood extents, and debris accumulation was reported.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: An upstream blockage release at Brook House may have increased the extent of the July 2019 flood.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Brook House car park was progressively inundated (stages recorded from ~75 mm up to ~750 mm), the wall adjacent to Brook House collapsed releasing ponded water into the downstream brook, and ground-floor industrial units with floor levels below external ground levels were quickly flooded. Internal flooding in the local area was reported up to 1.3 m deep for residential and commercial properties.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flood waters ponded and depths rapidly increased adjacent to Brook House as the return path was restricted by a brickwork boundary wall at the downstream end of the Brook House car park; at some point the ~0.9m-high wall collapsed into the watercourse and flood depth thereafter reduced. Video evidence indicates internal flooding of right-bank buildings (water draining from cracks).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Overland (pluvial) surface water flow routed around the southern side of the industrial buildings and inundated the area around Brook House; the pluvial flood map and observed extents from 31 July 2019 show an overland flow path affecting Brook House.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: The culvert below Brook House was identified as a channel constriction that would increase upstream water levels and contribute to out-of-channel flow; EA inspected the culvert after the event and reported it clear of obstructions.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Used as an exceedance flow route during the July 2019 fluvial flooding from Micker Brook; preserving an open route via the car park was recommended to allow floodwater to return to the watercourse and to minimise flood depth.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Micker Brook produced fluvial flooding at Broadway Avenue during the July 2019 event with observed extents not consistent with existing EA flood maps; the report recommends review of the modelling for this area.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Properties on Broadway Avenue were flooded during the July 2019 Micker Brook event when flood extents exceeded mapped levels; the flooding may have been increased by upstream blockage release.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Properties on Broadway Avenue were flooded during the July 2019 event as the 2019 flood outline exceeded current mapped extents for the reach.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Fluvial flooding related to the Lady Brook / Micker Brook event in July 2019 affected Broadway Avenue, forming part of the 2019 flood extents that the Environment Agency and Council propose to validate and address through mitigation options.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Identified as within the July 2019 fluvial flood extents on Wilmslow Road/Broadway Avenue; mapping should be validated to confirm inundation during the July 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Broadway is shown on the EA fluvial flood map adjacent to the river corridor in Bramhall Green with medium/low flood-risk zones extending onto nearby residential streets. The EA notes properties between Womanscroft Bridge and the roundabout were flooded during the event (31 July 2019); Broadway lies within the mapped area of flood risk so properties or land on Broadway may have been inundated by fluvial floodwater during 28 Jul 2019 - 31 Jul 2019.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Overland flow from Micker Brook crossed Wilmslow Road and flowed onto Broadway Avenue before returning to the watercourse; flooding followed initial flow from gullies during the evening of 31 July 2019 and is linked in reports to a rapid downstream rise and a release of ponded water at The Demmings Industrial Estate.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Received overland flow routed from Wilmslow Road before returning to the watercourse; downstream break of Micker Brook led to raised flood levels affecting gardens and basements on Broadway Avenue in the same vicinity.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Properties on Broadway Avenue are within the EA's mapped flood extents and were reported as flooded on 31 July 2019; pluvial mapping indicates surface-water flow along Broadway (and High Grove Road) driven by runoff from an unmodelled culverted tributary.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Surface water runoff from the railway reportedly overwhelmed United Utilities combined sewers, causing flooding on Borrowdale Avenue and associated foul flooding reports during the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Pluvial (surface water) runoff ponded at the north bend of Borrowdale Avenue, overwhelming drainage and UU combined sewers. Repeated flooding of the road and reported flooding up to house floor level at several properties. Foul contamination was noted in floodwater. The Manchester–Crewe railway embankment obstructed natural drainage contributing to ponding.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Overland/pluvial flows routed along the railway formed a flow path northwards and ponded at the bend at the north end of Borrowdale Avenue. The ponding and overland flow overwhelmed the United Utilities combined sewer draining the area, causing foul (sewage) flooding in the street.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Flooding in the Torkington/Hazel Grove area was associated with the main river Torkington Brook and surcharge at a culvert entrance below Clarendon Road, causing flooding on Hazelwood Road tied to the July 2019 event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

info.text: Torkington Brook and a surcharged culvert entrance (below Clarendon Road / at Torkington Road) are identified as the likely main source of flooding, producing surcharge and overland flow which affected adjacent streets.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Report for July 2019 Event

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report River Ash and Knowle Green Area

info.text: Floodwater from the County Ditch fed the Aqueduct during the event, contributing to elevated flows that required increased pumping and sluice gate management on the Aqueduct.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report River Ash and Knowle Green Area

info.text: Fluvial flood levels in County Ditch needed control during the event; control relied on preventing inflow from the Colne Brook by closing the Colnbrook West Lake penstocks so that flows in County Ditch matched local rainfall and groundwater baseflow.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Because the main penstock was open, County Ditch (and Cottesbrook ditch) drained a larger upstream area into the West Lake system and through the penstocks into Colnbrook, increasing flows and contributing to groundwater being kept topped up. Engineers estimated flows through the penstocks at about 500 l/s rising to 1000 l/s at peak overflow.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: An open main penstock (noted open on 11 February 2014) allowed a constant flow of water from County Ditch into Colnbrook; this inflow may have maintained high groundwater levels in Colnbrook and contributed to local flooding.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: County Ditch (identified as a source alongside Cottesbrook Ditch) was observed delivering water into the park/road area; flow from the ditch contributed to flooding in Albany Park and the adjacent residential roads and was a focus for pumping to lower levels.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Experienced elevated water levels contributing to flooding risk in flood area 1; EA pumping at the barrage was used to draw down levels in the County Ditch.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Water levels in the County Ditch were observed to rapidly rise and fall despite the West Lake penstock being closed. A tree was removed from the channel and channel cleaning was carried out as part of post‑flood actions.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Water levels in the County Ditch were observed to rise and fall rapidly during the investigation despite the West Lake penstock being closed; this abnormal behaviour was identified as an issue requiring investigation as a potential flood source (possible groundwater, unknown inflows, or local runoff).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: County Ditch fed the Cottesbrook Ditch and formed part of the fluvial pathway that led to flooding in The Albany Park; it also formed part of the pathway (via Hawthorn Ditch and County Ditch) by which water from Colnbrook West Lake entered Colnbrook.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: A tree was down on Mill Street during the flooding; the Environment Agency was informed and arranged removal (advised it would be removed by lunchtime).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: The west (main) penstock on Colnbrook West Lake was open for an unknown period, allowing continuous flow into Colnbrook via Hawthorn Ditch and County Ditch; at the peak the lake overtopped, bypassed the penstocks and flowed into Colnbrook village, worsening local flooding and keeping groundwater levels topped up.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Colnbrook West Lake overtopped its embankment; water bypassed the penstocks and flowed into Colnbrook village. The embankment level was 9 cm below its designed level, increasing overtopping risk.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Embankment level recorded 9 cm below the designed level, increasing the risk of premature overtopping during the Jan–Feb 2014 flood; recommendation made to raise the embankment (permanently or temporarily, e.g. sandbags or concrete kerbs).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: During the January–February 2014 event the Colne Brook overtopped the low embankment and flowed into the West Lakes (including Colnbrook West Lake); the Lakes provided flood storage which reduced flows conveyed downstream. Site visits after the floods noted Colne Brook levels higher than the Lakes.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Colnbrook West Lake (part of the West Lakes) was identified in post‑flood site visits after the Jan–Feb 2014 event; the report notes the relationship between Colne Brook and the West Lakes during the 2014 floods and their role in flood storage dynamics.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Penstocks at Colnbrook West Lake were central to controlling flows into County Ditch during the flood event; at the time there was uncertainty over which authority should operate the asset. Temporary operating conditions were established after the flood, the main penstock was closed, and two other penstocks (HW1 and HW3) are controlled to prevent backflow to the road. A flap valve is to be fitted upstream of the outfalls to stop backflow.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Colnbrook West Lake threatened to backflow towards the adjacent road during the winter floods; penstocks at the lake were a focus for preventing lake water reaching the highway (controls and flap‑valve measures were specified).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Penstocks on the West Lake outlets were observed partially closed or fully open and submerged during the event; obstructed seating required tarpaulin and bagging to reduce flow. The main penstock being open allowed continued flow from the lake, and closure by the council on 12 February corresponded with significant drops in local water levels. The report also notes that even with the penstock shut, high flows in Colne Brook risked earlier overtopping of the West Lake embankment and continued flow towards Colnbrook.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Main penstock to the lake was open on 11/02/2014 allowing a sustained flow into Colnbrook; penstock seating obstructed and needed tarpaulin/sandbagging to reduce flow. All flood storage in the West Lakes was used up and the West Lake embankment overtopped, forcing flood water over the downstream embankment towards Colnbrook. The embankment crest was 9 cm below design, causing earlier overtopping. Closure of penstocks on 12/02/2014 led to observed falls in water levels.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: The status of the Colnbrook West Lake penstock is discussed as influencing flood outcomes: had the penstock been shut the local area might have experienced less flooding initially, but shutting it earlier could have led to overtopping of the Colnbrook West Lake embankment and still resulted in floodwaters reaching the area. Penstock operation therefore affected flood timing and extent.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Penstocks at West Lake were confirmed as open during the incident; the council sought to confirm responsibility and ensure they were closed to manage high water levels.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: The main penstock was located, shut and sealed with tarpaulin and sandbagging by Slough Borough Council staff who entered deep water during the flood response.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: West Lake operations were altered during the response: the main West Lake penstock was kept closed under a temporary winter agreement to control levels, there were concerns about backflow from the lake to the road (leading to a proposed flap valve in chamber CP110), and a formal penstock operation manual was proposed to manage future flood risk.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: High water levels at West Lake prompted operational changes to the main penstock (temporary gate closure over winter under agreement), actions to make the penstock safe to operate when levels are high, and marking of the penstock location with a permanent bollard; these measures were taken to reduce future flood risk.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Backflow from West Lake was identified as a source of potential flooding to the adjacent road; this prompted the proposal to fit a flap valve to the West Lake penstock chamber (CP110) to prevent lake-to-road backflow.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Environment Agency modelling reviewed after the event indicated Colnbrook West Lake would overtop for an event with a return period of less than 1 in 50 years, identifying the lake as a potential source/contributor to surface water flooding and prompting further monitoring and consideration.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: West Lake operations and management were changed to manage high water levels after the flood event: a temporary agreement kept the main penstock gate closed over winter and a formal penstock operation manual and other controls were proposed to manage lake outflows and reduce flood risk to adjacent areas.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Internal flooding of properties in Coleridge Crescent and adjoining Closes and in Cottesbrook Close was predominantly caused by elevated groundwater; the Albany Park area was predominantly flooded by fluvial flooding from the Cottesbrook Ditch. The village was also flooded when water overtopped Colnbrook West Lake and flowed into Colnbrook via Hawthorn Ditch and County Ditch.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Flood water passed into Colnbrook via watercourses and overland flow and also through groundwater due to saturated catchments; water levels in Colnbrook Village rose and later fell markedly after penstocks were sealed, confirming local flood impacts during the event.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Three key flood areas were identified in Colnbrook Village. Flood water passed into the village via watercourses, overland flow and through groundwater; flood area 1 (including Fawsley Close and Albany Park) was first attended by the Environment Agency on 31 January when those streets reported flooding. Flood flows into the village were aggravated by overtopping at West Lakes and flows from the County Ditch when a penstock was open.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Mill Street flooded from flow from the Colne Brook (river levels high but generally in bank); a section of road flooded where a defect hole in the raised brickwork channel wall allowed water into the carriageway. The flood envelope along Mill Street broadened during the event but fluvial (internal) property flooding was not reported; after the event one property reported internal flooding caused by groundwater. Flood waters eventually subsided.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: The focus of the flood event moved onto Colnbrook Village in January. Flood response actions included delivery of sandbags to locations identified in the emergency flood plan; suspension of refuse/recycling collections; closure of Albany Park to vehicles; delivery of emergency advice/letters to residents; placement of temporary waste bins where roads were inaccessible; provision of portable toilets and washing facilities (Coleridge Crescent); assistance to vulnerable residents and help moving belongings to upper floors.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Area‑wide flood mitigation and response: protection of critical infrastructure (including electricity) with sandbags; penstocks at West Lake confirmed open and highway penstocks closed/sandbagged where possible; sluice gates at Horton Mill were cleared; vulnerable people assessed and assisted; temporary services and facilities provided.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Deep water in the village; Slough Borough Council staff entered deep water to locate, shut and seal the main penstock at Colnbrook West Lake. Residents had homes flooded and were advised to leave flood‑damaged items in their front gardens for collection.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: The winter (Jan–Feb 2014) flooding affected residents in Colnbrook. Post‑event activity included a flood surgery attended by affected residents, setting up community and multi‑agency flood groups, strategic sandbag issuance at limited locations, advertising repair/renew grants to affected properties, and review of policies and local modelling. The response notes flooding was predominantly from groundwater and that vehicle bow waves exacerbated impacts.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: Settlement affected by the Jan–Feb 2014 flood event, prompting multi‑agency response and subsequent measures including river and ditch cleaning, changes to Horton Mill Weir operation, temporary West Lake penstock arrangements, and proposals for infrastructure investigations (culvert/gauging/penstock modifications).

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: During the investigation surrounding the Jan–Feb 2014 event, Colnbrook experienced issues with groundwater and local drainage: groundwater levels required consideration for drawdown ahead of winter, a groundwater gauge was proposed to be upgraded to daily/sub-daily logging to better understand movements, and local flow issues were observed where water was backing through the Bath Road culvert—indicating local surface-water/fluvial backflow affecting the settlement and drainage system.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation Colnbrook Flooding - February 2014

info.text: After the 2014 floods, site visits noted that Colne Brook river levels were higher than the lake levels (Old Slade Lake), indicating the lakes were involved in the flood event and observed as part of post‑flood inspections.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Victoria Road Area, Southend-On-Sea

info.text: Victoria Road area (City of Southend) experienced surface water flows and sewer surcharging on 20th October 2021: foul-contaminated flows discharged from Manilla Road east to the junction of Victoria Road and Shaftesbury Avenue, pooling at the low point between Collier Way and Shaftesbury Avenue. Water depths reached approximately 200–250 mm; flooding persisted ~2–3 hours (receding by ~02:00 on 21st October). Significant contaminated silt deposits remained for several days and were cleared by SCC and Anglian Water. Historical SCC LFRMS records also show internal flooding in the Victoria Road area on 24th August 2013 and 19th September 2014.

Management recommendations (allowing grass to remain longer) aim to slow runoff; potential future works could include enlarging culverts and pipes under bridges/footpaths to improve conveyance.

ref.title: Section 19 - Investigation: Brookside, Rolleston

info.text: On 16 February 2020 multiple properties on Brookside experienced internal flooding. Records indicate 6 properties experienced internal flooding according to East Staffordshire Borough Council, and 12 properties reported internal flooding to the Environment Agency. Property owners reported flood depths inside dwellings of 2 to 16 inches, with significant damage to interior decoration, carpets and flooring and many items beyond salvage. Flood gates on some properties proved ineffective. Many residents were unable to leave their properties for several hours. Outbuildings, gardens, driveways and the highway were also flooded. Floodwater contained mud and silt likely from upstream fields.

info.text: Runoff from an adjacent, higher field inundated the adopted footpath, overwhelmed the footpath gully/drain, flowed over the footpath and entered front gardens and properties via very low-level air bricks and then front doors, causing internal flooding of the dwellings. Properties had no flood protection in place.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Ilkeston Walk, Hardwick, Stockton On Tees

info.text: Flood water reached properties such that internal property flooding was possible; property-level protection (waterproof flood doors, one-way brick covers, external waterproofing) would prevent water entering and so avoid internal flooding. Without such measures residents experienced occasional short-term inconvenience rather than devastating internal flooding.

info.text: Widespread flooding across Warwickshire on 14/15 November 2019, including confirmed internal property flooding at multiple locations; recovery and follow-on actions largely complete.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation: Flooding 14/15 November 2019 Various Locations

info.text: Heavy rainfall on 14–15 November 2019 produced widespread runoff across Warwickshire: soils were wetter than average and many rivers were responsive and described as notably or exceptionally high by the Environment Agency. Environment Agency Flood Alerts and Flood Warnings were in force for river flooding across parts of the county.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation: Flooding 14/15 November 2019 Various Locations

info.text: Following heavy rainfall on 14 November, river levels rose notably across the county and rivers generally peaked later on 14 November or into 15 November; Environment Agency Flood Alerts and Flood Warnings and a Flood Guidance Statement were in force for parts of the county. Antecedent wet soils increased rapid runoff, and some smaller ordinary watercourses (particularly in steep or urban areas) responded more quickly to the rainfall.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation: Flooding 14/15 November 2019 Various Locations

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation: Flooding 14/15 November 2019 Various Locations

info.text: County‑wide rainfall on 14/15 November 2019 produced widespread flooding across many communities in Warwickshire. Rivers reacted quickly causing river flooding in some areas, and rainfall running over already saturated ground produced extensive surface water flooding; sewer and groundwater flooding also contributed in a minority of locations. The event led to multiple community impacts including flooded access that caused school closures and numerous locations requiring investigation and support.

ref.title: Section 19 Flood Investigation: Flooding 2020 Piccadilly Crescent, Kingsbury

info.text: Surface water runoff entered the local piped drainage (SWS) network which became restricted. CCTV found a significant hole, cracking and displaced joints in the 150mm vitrified clay pipe draining Piccadilly Crescent to Thistlewood Brook. The damaged pipe caused blockages and surcharge from a chamber in a garden, leading to highway build-up and overtopping of the kerb. Flow was funnelled through lowered front gardens and entered properties via front doors and open joints, causing internal property flooding.

These works indicate risk of surface water / drainage-related flooding to the street and properties.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: High river flows during Storm Henk led to flooding across many areas of West Berkshire. The impact was exacerbated by unprecedented groundwater levels which reduced the catchment's ability to absorb rainfall, increased runoff into watercourses, and resulted in river flows and levels taking an extended time to return to normal.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Across Burghfield (the wider parish containing Sheffield Bottom) flooding during the 2024 event was driven by fluvial sources from the River Kennet and the Kennet and Avon Canal and by overtopping of nearby lakes. Historic flooding (winter 2013/14) affected the same area.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Roads were inundated by a combination of surface water, fluvial floodwater and elevated groundwater. Station Road, Deans Copse Road, Hose Hill and Hagnar Road experienced flood depths that made roads impassable for cars and affected safe access and egress for AWE employees. Sheffield Bottom experienced prolonged standing floodwater (longer dissipation than 2013/14).

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Across West Berkshire the exceptionally wet winter elevated groundwater, producing springs at topographical lows and contributing to river and surface-water flooding. Exceptional rainfall during storms Henk, Isha and Jocelyn caused the River Lambourn and Great Shefford Stream to exceed capacity. Manholes were reported surcharging outside properties along Wantage Road; a potentially collapsed drain in front of Downside House on Wantage Road may have reduced sewer capacity. One property experienced external surface-water flooding on 04 Jan (floodwater reached ~150 mm; occupants used a pump for about an hour to prevent internal flooding). Approximately two properties experienced internal fluvial flooding from the River Lambourn following Storm Henk.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Lambourn experienced flooding in early January 2024. Local wardens and residents reported flooding resulted from multiple sources: fluvial flooding associated with the River Lambourn (the river flowed continuously through autumn/winter 2023/24), groundwater emergence, surface water runoff, and sewer flooding. Flooding occurred in areas mapped as Flood Zone 2 and areas of high surface-water flood risk. A photograph in the report (Figure 10-2) shows flooding at Wantage Road. The early-2024 event was reported as more prolonged but less severe than the winter 2013/14 event.

info.text: The local groundwater gauge recorded very high groundwater levels in January 2024; this reflects high groundwater conditions in the village that likely contributed to groundwater flooding impacts.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: January 2024 flooding affected the village from multiple sources (sewer, groundwater, fluvial and surface water). Properties experienced internal and external flooding and widespread disruption to wastewater facilities; some properties remained unable to use wastewater facilities when observed by WSP on 28 March.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: January 2024 flooding affected the village from multiple sources. Surcharged sewer manholes caused external sewer flooding and raw sewage to enter the winterbourne stream and the River Lambourn. Groundwater flooded one property internally (recurring incidents after initial event). External surface-water flooding affected at least one property’s rear garden (4 Jan) and was pumped to prevent internal inundation.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: In the Great Shefford area, high groundwater and fluvial flooding led to external flooding of residential gardens. Flooding was reported to have started on 09 Jan and remained evident during the site visit.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Heavy rainfall on already saturated ground caused surface water runoff from surrounding hills into Great Shefford. The sewer system was overrun, resulting in manholes surcharging outside properties along Wantage Road; a potentially collapsed drain in front of Downside House may have exacerbated sewer capacity issues.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Village was affected by groundwater and fluvial (river) flooding across roads and pavements during the January 2024 event; temporary pumping plans were referenced and no permanent flood defences were present.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Groundwater and fluvial (river) flooding across roads and pavements in the village, reported to the Environment Agency on 4 January 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Multiple flood sources (fluvial, groundwater, sewer and surface water) caused inundation across the village: properties and the local road network were flooded. West Berkshire Council attended to monitor the situation and enforce road closures; Thames Water attended to carry out remedial works; the Environment Agency had flood management responsibility.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The annual maximum groundwater level for Jan 2024 is recorded among the highest in the monitoring record (bar chart), indicating an elevated groundwater event at Great Shefford during January 2024; the Jan 2024 maximum nearly matches the previous peak in 2012.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: A temporary flood barrier plan for the village was judged unsafe and could not be deployed; instead the Environment Agency deployed a pumping plan in winter 2023/2024 to reduce flood risk to properties in Great Shefford. There are no permanent flood defence assets in this area.

Newbury experienced significant rainfall during the 4–5 January 2024 event that formed part of the flood event and was therefore investigated.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Newbury (south), including Northcroft and West Mills, experienced flooding beginning 4 January 2024. Flooding was caused by groundwater inundation, sewer surcharging and fluvial (river) factors, resulting in inundation of streets and properties in the Newbury South area.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: High groundwater in and around Newbury during winter 2023/24, combined with heavy rainfall from January storms, caused groundwater emergence and infiltration into the sewer network. The sewer system in Northcroft was inundated and surcharged into roads. River Kennet levels submerged road drainage outfalls, enabling river water to back up road gullies; road drainage continued to surcharge for approximately one week after rainfall ceased.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flood wardens reported road flooding in south Newbury in January 2024. Wardens believed Thames Water may have cleared a sewer blockage, after which no further road flooding was reported.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding across the south of Newbury during January 2024 from fluvial sources (River Kennet) and groundwater; external fluvial flooding was reported to properties in Ampere Road; Northcroft Lane (south Newbury) was closed from 10 Jan 2024 to 14 Jan 2024 due to flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Newbury was affected by the January 2024 flooding: Northcroft Lane in the southern part of Newbury was closed (10 Jan–14 Jan 2024) and Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue Service attended one flood-related incident in Newbury during Storm Henk.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Areas in the south of Newbury (including Northcroft and Northcroft Lane) were affected by flooding during the event: highway drainage overwhelmed/insufficient, sewer inundation and surcharging occurred, and fluvial flooding threatened properties (notably the rear of properties on Northcroft Lane). Recommendations include CCTV surveys, drainage maintenance, and review of flood defence walls.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding in south Newbury: 10 properties flooded (7 internally, 3 externally). Two road closures affecting Northcroft Lane and West Street. Sources recorded as fluvial, groundwater and sewer.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Beginning around 5 January 2024 the River Lambourn rose and breached in several places, resulting in internal and external flooding across north Newbury. Flooding sources reported were fluvial (river), groundwater and sewer.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Multiple locations in and north of Newbury were affected by fluvial (River Lambourn) and groundwater flooding, with concurrent sewer and surface-water issues. Approximately 24 properties along Newport Road experienced external fluvial or groundwater flooding; groundwater flooding persisted for months. Around four properties on Doveton Way experienced a mixture of external fluvial, groundwater, surface water and sewer flooding. Foul sewer flooding began on 4 December 2023 and persisted into the 2024 event; approximately eight properties on Newport Road experienced external sewer flooding. Drains were surcharging foul water on Pike Street and Trout Walk. Debris-filled fluvial floodwaters from Newport Road reached Lambourn Court Care Home and Walton Way/Trout Walk; the care home had significantly deep external groundwater and fluvial flooding (no internal flooding reported). Garages along Trout Walk are reported to have experienced external flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Areas of Newbury experienced internal and external flooding caused by elevated groundwater, the River Lambourn overtopping its banks, and sewer impacts; some properties remained inundated at the time of the site visit in early January.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Northern Newbury experienced flooding (photo evidence shows water reaching the edge of a residential building north of Coachman's Court). The town has embankment-style flood defences in the north that vary in maintenance; some areas were protected by Shaw Flood Alleviation Scheme.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Multiple reports of flooding across Newbury during the January 2024 flood event, including groundwater flooding, sewer flooding and fluvial flooding from the River Lambourn across the north of Newbury. The Environment Agency visited a property affected by internal groundwater flooding on Church Road on seven occasions. Community Information Officers visited the area between 04 Jan and 12 Jan 2024 to provide advice and gather information.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding in the north area of Newbury led to the closure of Pike Street and Walton Way. Royal Berkshire Fire and Rescue Service attended one incident in Newbury during Storm Henk.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Residents in Newbury were affected by flooding related to multiple interacting sources. During the site visit residents reported that Environment Agency flood alerts/warnings were issued too late. A blocked trash screen on Spout Ditch was observed obstructing flow and causing upstream backing that contributed to local inundation risk. Drains at Glebefields car park were reported unmaintained and may have reduced local drainage capacity.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Fluvial and groundwater flooding affected areas mapped as Flood Zone 2 and 3; significant sewer flooding occurred in high surface water flood risk areas. Flooding affected critical drainage areas including River Walk and Walton Way, causing property flooding and road closures.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Multiple flood sources (fluvial, groundwater and sewer) caused flooding in the Newbury (North) area; authorities attended and road closures were enforced.

info.text: Properties in Newbury were flooded; the Environment Agency holds a Property_flooding_log for Newbury recording properties confirmed as affected. EA Community Information Officers attended Newbury (and nearby Shaw) between 04/01/2024 and 12/01/2024 to provide advice and gather intelligence about property flooding. The EA did not deploy operational resources to the location.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Village experienced multi-source flooding in early 2024: River Thames overtopped between Cleeve Lock and Goring Lock causing fluvial flooding; groundwater emergence (springs) arose in agricultural fields north of Cleeve Court Road; surface water and sewer sources also contributed. Residents moved vehicles to higher ground due to flood depths.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: River Thames overtopped banks between Cleeve Lock and Goring Lock producing fluvial flooding; groundwater emerged as springs in agricultural fields north of Cleeve Court Road; surface water runoff from surrounding high ground and down Streatley Hill produced debris-filled flows and contributed to flooding; residents moved vehicles to higher ground due to unsafe vehicular access. Residential and commercial buildings experienced internal and basement flooding, including The Swan Hotel and the basement of St Mary's Church used for flood-equipment storage. The Swan Hotel lost trading while lower levels were inundated.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Multiple flood sources affected Streatley: River Thames overtopping caused external fluvial flooding in the low-lying Cleeve Court area (all 11 properties at Cleeve Court and 3 properties on Cleeve Court Road were flooded externally). High groundwater led to internal groundwater flooding reported by a resident on three occasions (including 5 January). Surface water runoff on Streatley Hill generated debris-filled flood currents. At least 2 properties in Cleeve Court experienced internal sewer flooding from sewage backflow. The Swan Hotel was affected by fluvial and surface water flooding, causing a loss of trading. Residents reported 2024 flood depths were deeper than in previous events, with maximum flood depths in gardens along Cleeve Court Road reaching around 1 m.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: River Thames overtopped its banks and flooded low-lying Cleeve Court in Streatley. High groundwater contributed to prolonged inundation and perched water. Sewers serving Cleeve Court backed up during the early flood period, with some sewage reaching lower bathrooms of properties; the local sewage pumping station appears to have been overwhelmed (pumps may have stopped) due to floodwater ingress/overload. Drainage ditches were observed to be overgrown, reducing conveyance and prolonging flooding. Lock telemetry failure and a lock gate failure were also reported during the flooding.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Residents and the local flood warden reported issues after heavy rainfall that prompted Thames Water to plan remedial actions (improved telemetry, faster responses to capacity alerts, upgraded/more powerful pumps) to address capacity exceedance and related impacts experienced by residents.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Internal fluvial flooding of a property in Streatley caused by debris build-up at Goring Lock (River Thames).

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Properties in the Streatley area experienced internal sewer flooding (residents reported properties had non‑return valves fitted) and groundwater flooding affecting premises (including basements). Highway gullies and ditches became blocked after flood events; residents reported flood alerts/warnings were often issued too late and flooding had already occurred prior to warnings.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Flooding began around 4 January 2024 (first signs reported 04/01/2024). Flooding in January 2024 was reported by residents and the Pangbourne flood warden as caused by fluvial sources (River Thames, Sulham Brook, River Pang) together with groundwater emergence. Historic event 2013/14 affected the village (see quant).

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Areas of the village (Flood Zone 2 and 3) experienced fluvial and groundwater flooding in early January 2024. Four properties experienced internal flooding (two residential, two commercial). One residential property had internal groundwater flooding starting 6 Jan 2024, lasting approximately three days, with flood depths reaching about 75 mm; that same property also experienced external fluvial flooding from the River Thames but overland entry was prevented by flood sacks.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Residential and commercial properties experienced internal flooding from both groundwater and river (fluvial) sources. One residential property had internal groundwater flooding followed by river water entering the rear of the property. One commercial property had its car park flooded when the River Thames overtopped and was internally flooded in early January. Another commercial property experienced combined groundwater and fluvial internal flooding, with external car park flooding progressing into the building; flows became dangerously strong and residents were evacuated to hotels. Roads and community infrastructure were affected: Mill Lane was impassable, the Wharf overtopped where the River Thames backed up the River Pang, and a medical surgery car park was flooded causing the surgery to relocate for about three days.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: High groundwater and elevated River Thames levels caused overtopping of the Thames and backing up of the River Pang, leading to flooding across Pangbourne. Debris built up on Whitchurch Weir, obstructing flows; silted grips on Mill Lane prevented effective drainage causing road flooding; at least one property suffered indirect flooding from burst pipes after supplies were turned off and then frozen and burst.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Pangbourne experienced fluvial flooding from the River Thames; the Environment Agency received five reports of flooding in the area, including internal flooding of two properties and external flooding of three properties. Community Information Officers visited on 4–5 January 2024 to advise residents and collect information.

info.text: Large areas of the village were flooded during the early‑2024 event: properties experienced fluvial flooding followed by groundwater and sewer impacts. info.text: Purley on Thames experienced elevated groundwater levels, fluvial (river) flooding and sewer flooding. Properties were reported flooded internally for up to two weeks, and external flooding remained visible during a site visit on 14 March 2024.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Low-lying parts of Purley on Thames were flooded when high groundwater, overtopping of the River Thames and an overburdened sewer system combined. River overtopping flooded the low-lying area of Lower Purley and affected garages converted to living accommodation; elevated groundwater exacerbated prolonged inundation.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Fluvial flooding overtopped the Blount's Meadow bund and affected properties in Purley on Thames: 2 properties experienced internal flooding; 10 properties experienced garage flooding; 12 properties experienced external garden flooding.

info.text: The Environment Agency received reports of flooding across Purley on Thames: internal fluvial flooding from the River Thames affected properties and external flooding affected other properties; Community Information Officers visited multiple days to provide advice; EA deployed pumps operating in Purley until property flood risk reduced.

info.text: Purley experienced a combination of fluvial (river), surface water and groundwater flooding mechanisms. In response to rising water levels in January 2024 the Environment Agency deployed pumps to reduce flood risk; pumps operated until the risk of property flooding was reduced. A flood bund located behind Wintringham Way is present as a local defence.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: The Sheffield Bottom area was inundated during the January 2024 flood event by fluvial sources (River Kennet and the Kennet and Avon Canal) and by overtopping of the lakes to the west. ref.title: S19 Flood Investigations: Storms Henk, Isha, and Jocelyn - January 2024

info.text: Area experienced fluvial, groundwater and surface-water flooding in January 2024. Approximately seven properties experienced internal flooding and approximately ten properties experienced external flooding. Specific local impacts included: 2 properties on Hose Hill with internal surface-water flooding (those 2 and a third property also had external surface-water flooding); 3 properties on Station Road with internal fluvial flooding (12 Jan 2024) and a further Station Road property with external fluvial flooding; 1 commercial property on Deans Copse Road with external fluvial flooding; 2 industrial properties on Arrowhead Road with internal fluvial flooding. Roads (Station Road, Deans Copse Road, Hose Hill, Hagnar Road) were flooded (flood depths ~150mm in places), made impassable to cars and affected safe access and egress.

info.text: Heavy rainfall on a saturated catchment caused local watercourses and drainage to be unable to convey flows. Culverts under Banbury Road had insufficient capacity causing upstream water to overtop and pond on Banbury Road (approx. 50 m west and 30 m east). Floodwater surrounded and entered a property on Banbury Road (entered front door, came up through the floor) producing internal flooding and mud throughout; external partially enclosed areas of the same property were filled to depths up to 600 mm. Five cars became stuck on Banbury Road and were written off. Surface water and agricultural run-off contributed to carriageway flooding. At the south/north watercourse at Brook Street flows rose, overtopped and extended up Brook Street, affecting surrounding land and gardens; gardens of three properties on Brook Street were affected. Floodwater subsequently receded over a few hours leaving mud and requiring professional cleaning.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Burcote Fields, Towcester, 22nd November 2012

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Burcote Fields, Towcester, 22nd November 2012

info.text: Intense rainfall on a saturated catchment caused existing drainage systems and watercourses to be unable to convey flows; systems overtopped and water flowed to the low point at Burcote Fields. Drainage at this location was not designed to drain the quantity of water experienced to the public sewerage system. Inlets and structures were affected by silt and debris, reducing flow capacity.

ref.title: Flood Investigation Report: Burcote Fields, Towcester, 22nd November 2012

ref.title: Sandford Lane Flood Investigation Report January 2016

info.text: Between 13 December and Christmas Day 2013 heavy rainfall (up to 100mm in places) caused the River Loddon and the River Blackwater to burst their banks. Repeated storms through late December, early January and into January–February 2014 kept river and groundwater levels high, contributing to inundation of the Thames floodplain and localised property flooding in areas close to the River Loddon, River Thames and River Blackwater.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: Recurrent heavy rainfall and high river and groundwater levels caused rivers (including the River Loddon and River Blackwater) to burst banks and added large volumes of water to the Thames floodplain, resulting in widespread internal and external property flooding across multiple parishes within the borough; Lower Thames reached highest levels for more than 65 years.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: During the winter 2013/14 (01 Dec 2013 - 28 Feb 2014) parts of Wokingham Borough experienced multiple sources of flooding: river flooding affected settlements within the borough (notably Wargrave, Shinfield and Charvil); surface water (pluvial) flooding affected areas including Swallowfield and Charvil; sewer flooding occurred in Swallowfield and Hurst; and high groundwater levels in parts of Wokingham contributed to other types of flooding.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: Winter 2013/14 flooding across Wokingham Borough affected six parishes and multiple villages; properties were flooded both internally and externally and some residents were displaced. Site visits (Sept–Nov 2014) found a small number of houses still uninhabitable due to flood damage.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: Experienced fluvial flood warnings and on-the-ground impacts during winter 2013/14: roads were flooded and impassable or worsening flooding to properties (prompting road closures), sandbags were supplied to residents, blocked drainage/structures were cleared and pumps used, and some residents suffered sewage backup requiring provision of Portaloos.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: Widespread flooding across the borough in winter 2013/14: River Loddon and River Blackwater burst their banks (noted between 13 Dec and Christmas Day 2013), sustained heavy rainfall and high groundwater produced repeated high river levels and inundation of floodplain areas, causing property flooding across Wokingham.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: Community experienced flooding linked to the winter 2013/14 flood event; informal Flood Wardens were operating locally prior to and during this event to assist preparedness and response.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: The village suffered flooding from three sources in winter 2013-14: surface water runoff from surrounding farmland, sewage from a surcharging Thames Water foul network, and river flooding from both the Loddon and Blackwater. High groundwater levels worsened flooding. Highway flooding was evident across the village.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

info.text: Village experienced significant surface water runoff channelled via field drains and ditches into the River Blackwater and onto the highway; highway flooding occurred at the junction of the B3349 and Swallowfield Street (late December) and an area of Swallowfield Street flooded; northern fields were affected by river flooding (River Loddon and River Blackwater) including fields south of Swallowfield Park drive which were completely flooded.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

Separately, ingress of surface water and groundwater into the foul sewer network during the winter 2013-14 event caused sewage flooding in the village: households suffered blocked lavatories and non-flowing wastewater; foul water mixed with flood water on local streets and sewage debris was left on roads requiring clearing.

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

ref.title: Wokingham Borough Council Flood Investigation Reports: Winter 2013/2014

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: An extremely intense rainfall event on 27th May 2018 produced surface water/flash flooding across Hollywood (part of the wider Wythall parish), triggering a multi‑agency response and recovery effort.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: On 27th May 2018 extremely intense rainfall overwhelmed highway drains and sewer infrastructure; roads became surface-water flow paths with deep pooling in low spots. Local watercourses were quickly overwhelmed, overtopped and backed up where culverts, fences or garages restricted flow. In most locations water levels fell quickly but in a small number of locations water remained high for an extended period, indicating drainage issues.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: The settlement experienced flooding that required establishment of an emergency response phone line, on-site advice/support (including at the Wythall Hub), assistance with removal of damaged goods, repair of damaged highways and sweeping of footways, and extensive inspection and surveying of drainage, sewers and local watercourses as part of the recovery and investigation.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: Settlement affected by the flood which prompted watercourse inspections and clearance, sewer and highway drainage responses, removal of a collapsed wall from Hollywood Brook, and subsequent drainage/highway remedial works.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: Surface water flooding affected the village on 27 May 2018, impacting local drainage and communities and prompting the investigation and recommendations (including investigation of upstream attenuation and installation of monitors).

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: Flooding associated with the Hollywood Brook and surface water runoff affected the community in Hollywood on 27th May 2018, causing property flooding, community disruption and resident health/welfare concerns that prompted recommendations for attenuation areas, monitoring, culvert/trash‑screen improvements and property flood resilience measures.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: An unprecedented short-duration rain storm on 27 May 2018 overwhelmed drainage and local watercourses, causing severe surface water / flash flooding that was described as extremely significant and devastating to the community. Residential drainage and watercourse infrastructure, although generally in good order, were overwhelmed; the lack of adequate space for water in period residential developments contributed to the scale of impact. Emergency response and ongoing recovery were reported as good and speedy.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

info.text: Flood flow routes concentrated through the central and eastern residential core of Hollywood. Multiple overland flow entry and exit points were identified at the settlement periphery; water routed from higher ground in the north and east toward lower-lying south and west, causing surface water to flow through residential streets and along major/minor roads.

ref.title: Hollywood Flood Event May 2018 Investigation Report

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report: Storm Babet 19th – 20th October 2023

info.text: Surface water/sewer-related flooding along Mustard Lane required sandbags to be deployed to control flow. Highway gullies on Mustard Lane (south of the Memorial Hall) operated and drained excess water. The existing drainage/sewer infrastructure runs under Mustard Lane and conveyed significant volumes of highway, property and land drainage into the area during the event.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report: Storm Babet 19th – 20th October 2023

info.text: Overland flow was controlled with sandbags delivered by the Council; highway gullies to the south of the Memorial Hall drained excess water. The statutory maps and CCTV show a combined public sewer and a larger drainage system running along Mustard Lane; defects identified included a failed pipe adjacent to the chamber near No.1 Mustard Lane (creating a significant void) and a defective liner that was later removed. The drainage system was cleaned to restore operation, but pipe weakening and subsequent failure occurred due to pressures during the event.

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report: Storm Babet 19th – 20th October 2023

info.text: A failed section of the drainage system was confirmed 1.0m from the chamber outside No.1 Mustard Lane, extending for approximately 10.0m upstream. The failure is attributed to increased pressure on the drainage system during Storm Babet; open-cut repair was required and completed in January 2024. Final remedial works include installing a continuous liner for the full length of the system to the chamber in Sandy Lane (approx. 50.0m).

ref.title: S19 Flood Investigation Report: Storm Babet 19th – 20th October 2023

info.text: Properties on Mustard Lane were flooded between 19 and 20 October 2023 due to surcharging of the drainage system driven by Storm Babet and prolonged heavy rainfall. Contributing factors cited include lack of drainage capacity for overland flow, significant tree roots, failure of a CIPP liner in sections (installed circa 2016) and failure of a pipe adjacent to a chamber near No1 Mustard Lane which created a significant void.

info.text: An extreme rainfall event on 10–12 June 2012 caused widespread flooding across parts of the county. Almost 800 properties across West Sussex were affected by flooding from a variety of sources; the worst affected areas included the Manhood Peninsula, Bognor Regis, Littlehampton and Worthing. The Bognor Regis conurbation (including Middleton on Sea, Elmer and Felpham) had reports of properties flooded primarily by surface water.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The county experienced unprecedented summer 2012 rainfall (notably 10–12 June 2012) that overloaded local drainage networks across the coastal plain. Flood water generally dissipated over 2–3 days with no significant infrastructure damage, but the event caused widespread surface water flooding.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Significant internal and external flooding occurred at multiple locations across West Sussex; some locations experienced flooding on more than one occasion.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Significant internal and external flooding occurred at multiple locations across West Sussex; some locations experienced flooding on more than one occasion. This prompted West Sussex County Council to conduct a Section 19 investigation.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Widespread surface water flooding during the June 2012 event; flooding patterns closely matched the county's Areas Susceptible to Surface Water Flooding maps. Prolonged heavy rainfall (some locations received large totals in 12–24 hours) generated excess runoff and caused inundation across parts of the county.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: West Sussex experienced very high short‑duration rainfall that generated excess runoff and led to surface water flooding in the county.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Numerous extreme rainfall observations were recorded across West Sussex during the event (Met Office and other networks). The report notes multiple very large local totals in the county and describes highly localised convective cells, indicating the county experienced intense rainfall that increased the likelihood of significant disruption and potential flooding in parts of West Sussex.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Extremely high, localised rainfall across West Sussex produced widespread surface water flooding (the majority of property flooding on 10–12 June) and some river-linked flooding; the Environment Agency issued Flood Alerts and Flood Warnings for multiple rivers and watercourses in the county.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Widespread extreme rainfall in June 2012 caused extensive surface water flooding across the county (main event 10–12 June 2012). Some property flooding occurred; river levels in parts of the county (notably Aldingbourne Rife and the Manhood Peninsula rife network) remained high for days after the rain.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Experienced flood incidents during the heavy rainfall of 10–12 June 2012, which disrupted roads, hospitals and schools and led to evacuations and protective/pumping operations across the county.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Cluster identified as affected by the June 2012 floods. Properties in this area suffered flooding impacts that ranged from external flooding (gardens, outbuildings, garages) to some properties being internally affected. Affected properties were mapped and prioritised for follow-up investigation.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: County-wide intense rainfall produced spatial clusters of property flooding, with the majority of affected properties concentrated in the southwest of the county (notably around the South Downs and adjacent coastal towns).

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: In June 2012 widespread flooding traumatised people and damaged homes; many residents faced the prospect of moving out of their homes for many months due to flood damage.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: A very heavy rainfall event on 10–12 June 2012 (in excess of a 1 in 200 year event) caused widespread surface water/urban flooding across West Sussex; highway drainage (road gullies) failed to cope with the intensity of the rain.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: An extreme rainfall event on 10/11 June 2012 produced widespread flooding across parts of the county, affecting communities and properties.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Widespread flooding across parts of the county between 10 June 2012 and 12 June 2012 caused by extreme rainfall and hydraulic overloading of drainage systems. Almost 800 properties were affected. Contributing factors cited include lack of riparian maintenance and loss of land drainage, infilling/piping of ditch lines, weed and plant growth slowing flow in ditches, and poor condition or loss of surface water sea outfalls.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Extreme rainfall overwhelmed drainage infrastructure across the county. Public drainage systems (including culverts) failed to cope with the volume of water, resulting in flooding that affected residents; the report also notes many residents were not registered for the EA flood warning service.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Widespread flooding across the county: WSFRS Command and Mobilising Centre received large numbers of calls for flooded properties; basement flooding at Worthing Hospital affected lift shafts; over twenty basement properties on South Terrace, Littlehampton required pumping and most residents left their properties; extensive flooding affected Felpham and Bognor Regis with water rescues; Aldingbourne Rife levels were lowered using an HVP; mutual aid from Hampshire crews was required to maintain emergency cover.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The county experienced flooding associated with the event of 10–12 June 2012, triggering community support and multi-agency recovery activity.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Extreme, highly localised rainfall was recorded in Bognor Regis during the event. The Environment Agency rain gauge at Bognor Regis recorded 114mm over the whole event — the highest 24‑hour total recorded at Bognor since EA records began in 1974 — and the report characterises this as approximately a 1-in-200-year (0.5% annual chance) rainfall event. A separate town council gauge and other local gauges reported substantially higher totals at nearby locations, indicating an exceptionally intense, localised storm over the Bognor area and implying a high potential for disruption.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Part of the area that experienced flood incidents during the heavy rainfall on 10–12 June 2012; flooding disrupted roads, hospitals and schools and contributed to evacuations and protective/pumping operations.

info.text: High volumes of surface water inundated and overwhelmed surface water and combined/foul sewer systems; surcharged systems and overwhelmed highway drainage caused flows to be transported above ground via roads into properties. Public foul drainage and local wastewater pumping stations were manned and additional pumps deployed to maintain operation.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Local roads and car parks (for example Wick Precinct; Banjo Road adjacent to South Terrace) were flooded; residents reported impacts including bow waves from vehicles on flooded roads, insufficient drain capacity, need for road closures, instances of foul water pumping, delayed emergency response and concerns over insurance and property reinstatement.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Central Worthing experienced flooding along and over the route of the piped/culverted Teville Stream during the June 2012 event; properties, gardens, roads and parkland in the area were flooded. Flooding incidents east of the hospital/Homefield Park contained sewage, indicating sewer surcharging and contamination.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: During 10 Jun 2012 - 12 Jun 2012 heavy rain coinciding with high tide reduced outflow through sea outfalls and caused sewer surcharging. Floodwaters spread laterally across West Worthing, inundating properties, gardens, roads and parkland; some flooding incidents reported contamination by sewage.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The Middleton area (specifically Central Drive, West Drive and Southdean Close) experienced surface water flooding during the June 2012 extreme event caused by a lack of highway drainage and failing soakaways; subsequent to the event WSCC jetted and cleansed the highway drainage system.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Overland surface water ran into the Elmer Sands Estate from fields to the north (Ancton Lodge Lane area) and along Elmer Road and Kingsmead Road. Highway drainage entered a culvert beneath Elmer Road that was observed to be flowing slowly during the June event, indicating restricted discharge; this culvert discharges into silted IDB ditches on the north side of Ancton Lane which restricted outflow and contributed to local flooding.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Areas of Middleton (including private estates such as Lodge Close and Willowbrook) experienced surface water flooding. Private and highway drainage were overwhelmed or constrained by silted/blocked culverts and restricted outlets, causing surface water to pond and back up into estate roads and properties. Investigations and jetting after the event confirmed blockages and culvert restrictions affecting flow and storage.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Part of the area where homes were flooded and visited by police and rescue teams; residents were assisted during search and evacuation operations.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Following the June 2012 flood WSCC carried out jetting and CCTV surveys; the Elmer Road to Ancton Lane ditch line was cleared of overgrowth and the piped highway drainage was jetted with repair work identified to the piped system.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Local residents (South Dean within Middleton) have an existing flood group and are progressing independently to address flood impacts.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: A259 (Felpham Way) experienced significant surface-water/urban flooding with road inundation extending into driveways and front gardens and vehicles partially submerged (photo evidence). Flooding was exacerbated by a tide-locked sea outfall requiring storage during high tide, reduced storage capacity where the overflow ditch has been infilled/enclosed within gardens, and loss of historical connection to Ley Road ditch; restrictions in the SWS surface water sewer (e.g. past root-blocking) were also noted as contributing factors. The Davenport Road area was pumped clear and A259 drained down following pumping.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Felpham's outfall infrastructure (Felpham Pumping Station and related tidal outfalls) is listed as EA responsibility and is described as operating normally during the 10–12 Jun 2012 flood event. Southern Water has separately proposed contingency pumping arrangements for flooding in Felpham.

info.text: Chichester was part of the Bognor-to-Chichester area that recorded very high rainfall on 10–12 June 2012; local drainage networks were overwhelmed, causing surface water/urban flooding in vulnerable low-lying locations.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.
