info.text: Multiple roads and residential areas in west Chichester were affected by surface water flooding (Parklands Road, Cedar Drive, Sherborne Road, Neville Road, Oliver Whitby Road, Langton Road, St Wilfrids Road); properties and gardens were flooded. The Fishbourne Road East/Apuldram Lane North system in west Chichester is known to flood in extreme events and flooded in 2012.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: High groundwater levels in parts of Chichester caused flooding (notably areas drained to soakaways), prompting surveys and proposed drainage improvements following the June 2012 flood.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Multiple locations in Chichester experienced flooding issues: high groundwater and drainage to soakaways caused flooding in parts of the city and highway drainage was overwhelmed in locations such as College Lane and junctions with A27/Bognor Road, prompting surveys and drainage improvements.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Prolonged heavy rain over 12–24 hours during the 10–11 June 2012 event generated excess runoff and led to flooding across Hampshire; the report lists Hampshire as one of the worst affected areas.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Persistent heavy rain beginning on 10 June tracked into East Hampshire and continued without interruption in worst affected parts, generating excess runoff that led to flooding; very heavy bursts were expected in eastern parts of the county and were likely to bring significant disruption.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Eastern parts of Hampshire were highlighted by the FGS as likely to receive very heavy bursts of rain on 10 June that could bring significant disruption; EA/other gauge coverage also recorded extreme rainfall across Sussex and eastern Hampshire that raised flood risk.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Significant, persistent heavy rain during the 10–11 June 2012 event affected East Sussex; the slow‑moving low pressure and prolonged rainfall produced excess runoff that contributed to flooding in the county.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Prolonged heavy rainfall across much of Sussex generated excess runoff leading to surface water flooding and significant disruption in affected parts.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Persistent, very heavy rainfall across Sussex on 10–11 June produced excess runoff leading to flooding in the worst-affected parts; the FGS and raingauge records identify Sussex as within the areas of concern with likely significant disruption (particularly in urban areas and from fast-responding rivers).

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Widespread surface water flooding during 10 Jun 2012 - 12 Jun 2012 that triggered a multi-agency response and subsequent multi-agency debrief; led to identification of strengths and weaknesses and production of recommendations to improve future flood response, communications and resilience.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Felpham was extensively flooded; residents were assisted by specially equipped water rescue crews and multi-agency teams completed searches of flooded patches and assisted trapped people.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Police (Arun neighbourhood team and Sussex Police) conducted systematic house-to-house checks across the affected area, accounted for vulnerable residents, and remained involved in recovery group work.

Properties in the cluster experienced flooding of gardens, outbuildings and garages and some internal property flooding; the cluster was included in prioritised investigation and mapping.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The Fishbourne Road East / Apuldram Lane North system is known to flood in extreme events. Four properties in this area flooded in 1994, 2001, 2010 and during the 2012 event. The culvert under the A27 was found to be of adequate size but requires maintenance to clear silt and possible obstructions; the Fishbourne Road East culvert was surveyed and found clear.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Surface water flooding affected private estate roads and properties (Lodge Close, Willowbrook, Ancton Lodge Lane). Flooding was caused or worsened by a restricted/abandoned culvert under Ancton Lodge Lane, private building encroachment into the watercourse, heavy siltation of open watercourses reducing storage and conveyance, a possibly partially blocked private outlet pipe in rear gardens of Ancton Close, and downstream outfall issues into IDD ditches. Southern Water deployed additional diesel pumps to assist removal of high volumes of surface water impacting residents and the sewerage system.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Residential properties flooded.

ref.title: Properties Affected by June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Surface water drainage from Lodge Close outfalls to an adjacent watercourse that was heavily silted and restricted; culvert restrictions and reduced storage capacity limited outfall flow, contributing to surface water flooding issues confirmed by jetting and investigation following the June 2012 event.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Residents formed a core flood action group and are preparing door-to-door engagement and an action plan to address flood impacts in their street.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Known properties flooded during the June 2012 flood event (multiple entries in the table).

ref.title: Properties Affected by June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The open watercourse within Willowbrook was heavily silted, reducing storage and flow carrying capacity and contributing to surface water flooding of the estate during the 10–12 June 2012 event. The outlet from Willowbrook passes north through a culvert in rear gardens of Ancton Close which may have been partially blocked, impeding discharge.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Residential property flooded.

ref.title: Properties Affected by June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: A culvert restriction under Ancton Lodge Lane (including an abandoned original culvert and flows through a higher-level WSCC highways culvert) reduced conveyance and contributed to surface water flooding in the local area during the 10–12 June 2012 event. These restrictions reduced storage capacity and restricted flows from Lodge Close piped outlets.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Surface water ran from the Ancton Lodge Lane area into the Elmer Sands Estate, contributing to overland flooding of properties during the June event.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Ditches on the north side of Ancton Lane received outfall from a restricted, silted culvert network; reduced storage and blocked/poorly levelled culverts restricted flow from Lodge Close/Willowbrook outlets, contributing to surface water backing up into the Lodge Close, Willowbrook and Ancton Lodge Lane estate areas during the June event.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Culvert outfalls discharge into IDB ditches on the north side of Ancton Lane; restricted discharge from these ditches (silted/standing water) reduced drainage capacity and contributed to flooding during the June event.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Ditch line between Elmer Road and Ancton Lane was cleared of overgrowth; piped system below the ditch was jetted and repair works were identified as part of drainage remedial works to address flooding.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Surface water ingress and blocked/draining issues required cutting grips into the ditch and rodding/repair of blocked gullies to relieve flooding; works specified to prevent road/footway flooding near Ancton Barn.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

Culvert flow was slow north of Elmer Road toward the Lucking Lane footway, and discharge is restricted by silted IDB ditches, contributing to surface-water inundation of the highway and adjacent properties.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Significant surface-water/urban flooding during the June 2012 event. Overland runoff from fields north of the settlement flowed along Elmer Road into the Elmer Sands Estate and Kingsmead Road; the culvert beneath Elmer Road was observed to be slow-flowing between Elmer Road and the Lucking Lane footway, collecting highway drainage and contributing to deep road flooding (photographic evidence shows vehicles negotiating deep floodwater).

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: During the June event the culvert section from Elmer Road north to the Lucking Lane footway was observed to be flowing slowly, and highway drainage was collected into the culvert; surface water ran along Elmer Road into the Elmer Sands Estate, contributing to flooding.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Listed as an NFF attendance point (car park opposite shops near Jubilee Hall) responding to impacts from the June 2012 surface water flooding; residents and businesses in the area sought help with property reinstatement and drainage issues.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Following flooding, emergency and remedial drainage works were required: a large hole beside a gully was made safe and needs permanent repair; buried chamber uncovered and lid installed to allow future jetting; rodding of gullies and pipes to locate blockages; jetters/tankers supplied to attend emergencies; digging out and clearing of ditch to restore flow (including a 100m section).

info.text: Flooding of this private highway and adjacent properties during the June 2012 event caused by inadequate highway drainage and failure of property soakaways and roof drainage under extreme conditions; a reported (but unverified) non-functioning private outfall to sea may have exacerbated drainage failure.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Area affected by inundation from the limited surface water system; the SWS surface water sewer discharges to sea via an outfall south of Davenport Road and the capacity of this outfall may have been insufficient, contributing to hydraulic overloading and flooding.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The Davenport Road area required pumping to clear floodwater. The sea outfall and the chamber south of Davenport Road (including pipe sizing and valve arrangements) are under investigation and an overpumping contingency is being developed to manage future tide-locked/high-tide periods.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: The sea outfall and an outfall chamber located south of Davenport Road required investigation and an operational contingency (over‑pumping) to manage flows, indicating the outfall/chamber were implicated in drainage failure during the event.

ref.title: West Sussex County Council Report On June 2012 Flood Event.

info.text: Felpham Way was inundated with floodwater across the road and into adjacent properties and driveways; vehicles were partially submerged.
